Pactolus.definition: Pactōlus (-los) ī, m , *paktwlo/s, a river of Lydia, with golden sands, V., O.—Prov.: tibi Pactolus fluat, i. e. boundless wealth, H., Iu.

Paean.definition: Paeān ānis, m the god of healing (an epithet of Apollo): signum Paeanis: Paeana voca, O.: Parce, Paean! Iu.—A hymn to Apollo, festive hymn, hymn of triumph, paean, C.: laetus, V.: victor canebat Paeana, Pr.—The charac…

Paeonius.definition: Paeōnius adj., of Paeon (god of physicians), healing, medicinal: herbae, V.: ope Paeoniā, O.

Palatinus.definition: Palātīnus adj., of the Palatium, Palatine: Evander, V.: colles, O.: Apollo (from his temple on the Palatine Hill), H.: laurus, before the imperial palace, O.: cubile, Iu.

Pales.definition: Palēs is, f PA-, an Italian goddess of shepherds and pastures , V., O.

Palicus.definition: Palīcus ī, m a son of Jupiter, worshipped at Palica, in Sicily, V., O.—The Palīcī were honored as twin brothers: stagna Palicorum, O.

Palilis.definition: Palīlis or Parīlis e, adj. Pales, of Pales : flamma, a fire of straw at the feast of Pales , O.: festa, O.— Plur n . as subst, the feast of Pales, shepherd festival (the 21st of April), C., O.

Palladium.definition: Palladium ī, n , palla/dion, an image of Pallas, C., V., O.

Pallantis.definition: Pallantis idos, f Aurora, O.—The day, O.

Pallas.definition: Pallas adis and ados, f , *palla/s, a surname of Athene (identified with the Roman Minerva), V., H., O.: Palladis ales, the owl, O.: Pallados arbor, the olive-tree, O.: iratā Pallade (i. e. invitā M<*>ervā), O.—Oil: i…

Pan.definition: Pān Pānos, acc. Pāna, m , *pa/n, Pan, son of Mercury, god of woods and shepherds, often represented as half man, half goat: Panos de more Lycaei, V.: semicaper, O.—Plur, gods like Pan, gods of the woods and fields, O.

Panomphaeus.definition: Panomphaeus ī, m , *panomfai=os, source of all oracles, i. e. Jupiter, O.

Panthoides.definition: Panthoidēs ae, m , *panthoi+/dhs, son of Panthus, Euphorbus, O.—Pythagoras, who claimed that he had been Euphorbus in a previous life, is called Panthoides, H.

Paphius.definition: Paphius adj. , *pa/fios, of Paphos (a city of Cyprus): myrtūs, i. e. sacred to Venus, V.: heros, Cyprian (i. e. Pygmalion), O.

Parca.definition: Parca ae. f PARC-, a goddess of Fate : Parca non mendax, H.: dura, O.—Plur, the Fates (i. e. Klotho, Lachesis, and Atropos), C., H., V., Iu.

Parthenope.definition: Parthenopē ēs, f , *partheno/ph, Neapolis (where the Siren Parthenope was buried), V., O.

Pataraeus.definition: Pataraeus (O.), or Patareus (trisyl., H.), adj., of Patara (a seaport of Lycia), Pataraean.

Pegasus.definition: Pēgasus (-os) ī, m , *ph/gasos, in fable, a winged horse of the Muses, afterwards a constellation, H., O.—Plur., of swift messengers, C.

Pelasgi.definition: Pelasgī ōrum, m , *pelasgoi/, the Pelasgians, oldest settlers of Greece, V.—The Greeks, V., O.

Penates.definition: Penātēs ium, m 1 PA-, the Penates, guardian gods of the family, household gods : vos Penates patriique di, V., H., O.: deos penatīs salutatum domum Devortar, T.: aedes deorum Penatium, L. — A dwelling, home, hearth (c…

Pergama.definition: Pergama (-mum, Enn. ap. C.), ōrum, n , *pe/rgama, the citadel of Troy, Troy, V., H., O.

Peripateticus.definition: Peripatēticus adj. , *peripathtiko/s, of the Peripatetic philosophy, Aristotelian: philosophi.

Persae.definition: Persae ārum, m , *pe/rsai, the Persians, S., C., N., H.—The Parthians, H.

Persephone.definition: Persephonē ēs, f , *persefo/nh, Proserpine, O.—Death, Tb., O.

Perses.definition: Persēs ae, m , *pe/rshs, a Persian, C., N.

Persicus.definition: Persicus adj. , *persiko/s, Persian, of Persia: regna, Iu.: apparatūs, i. e. luxurious, H.—Plur n. as subst, Persian history.

Phaeax.definition: Phaeāx ācis, m a Phaeacian; usu. plur, the Phaeacians (who lived luxuriously), C., V., O., Iu. —Sing. (poet.), a good liver, well-fed man, H.— Once As adj.: Phaeax populus, Iu.

Phanaeus.definition: Phanāeus adj. of Phanae (in Chios).—Poet.: rex Phanaeus, i. e. Phanaean wine, V.

Phantasos.definition: Phantasos ī, m , *fa/ntasos, a god of dreams, O.

Pharos.definition: Pharos (-rus) ī, f an island near Alexandria, with a famous light-house, Cs., O., Iu.—The lighthouse at Pharos, Cs.— A light-house: Tyrrhena, Iu.

Pharsalicus.definition: Pharsālicus or Pharsālius adj., Pharsalian, of Pharsalus (in Thessaly).

Philippicus.definition: Philippicus adj. , *filippiko/s, of Philip, Philippic: orationes, Cicero's orations against Antony (in allusion to those of Demosthenes against Philip of Macedon): divina Philippica, i. e. the second Philippic, Iu.

Philippus.definition: Philippus ī, m , *fi/lippos, a king of Macedonia, father of Alexander the Great, C., N.—A gold coin struck by King Philip, H.

Philomela.definition: Philomēla ae, f , *filomh/la, a daughter of Pandion, changed into a nightingale, V., O.—The nightingale, V.

Phlegethon.definition: Phlegethōn ontis, m , *flege/thwn, a river of fire in the Lower World, V.

Phoebas.definition: Phoebas adis, f , *foiba/s, a priestess of Phoebus; hence, an inspired woman, prophetess, O.

Phoebe.definition: Phoebē ēs, f , *foi/bh, goddess of the moon (the Roman Diana), V., O.: tertia, i. e. night, O.

Phoebeius.definition: Phoebēius (O.) or Phoebēus (V., O.), adj., of Phoebus, of Apollo.

Phoebigena.definition: Phoebigena ae, m Phoebus+GEN-, son of Phoebus , i. e. Aesculapius , V.

Phoebus.definition: Phoebus ī, m , *foi/bos, Apollo as the god of light, V., H.—The sun: dum fugat astra Phoebus, H., O.

Phoenices.definition: Phoenīces um, m , *foi/nikes, the Phoenicians (on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea), C., S., Cs., V., O.

Phoenissa.definition: Phoenīssa adj. f, *foi/nissa, of Phoenicia (on the Mediterranean Sea): Dido, V.: exul, i. e. Anna, O.—As subst, Dido, V.

Phrygius.definition: Phrygius adj. , *fru/gios, Phrygian, of Phrygia, C., L., V., H., O., Iu.—Plur f. as subst, the Phrygian women, V.—Trojan, of Troy: muri, O.: hymenaei, with Aeneas, V.

Phryx.definition: Phryx ygis, adj., Phrygian: augur, Iu.—As subst m. sing., V., O., Iu.—Usu. plur., *fru/ges, a luxurious people of Asia Minor, C., O., Ph., Iu. —The Trojans, H., O.—The Phrygians were regarded as stupid; hence, prov.: …

Picens.definition: Picēns ntis (C., L.), or Pīcēnus, adj. (S., Cs., C., L., H., Iu.), Picene, of Picenum (in Italy).

Pieris.definition: Pīeris idis, f , *pieri/s, a Muse (first worshipped in Pieria), H., O.—Plur, the Muses, C., V., H., Iu.

Pierius.definition: Pīerius adj. , *pie/rios, Pierian, of Pieria (in Macedonia); hence, Macedonian: paelex, H.—Of the Muses, poetic: antrum, H.: umbra, Iu., H., O., Ph.—Plur f. as subst, the Muses.

Pilumnus.definition: Pīlumnus ī, m pilum, a god of the Latins, who taught how to crush corn , V.

Pimpleus.definition: Pimplēus adj., of Pimpla (in Pieria, sacred to the Muses): mons, Ct.—As subst f., a Muse: duclis, H.

Piraeeus.definition: Pīraeeus (trisyl., C.) or Pīraeus (T., C., Ct., L., N., Pr.), ī, m, or Pīraea, ōrum, n (O.), *peiraieu/s, the port of Athens.

Piraeus.definition: Pīraeus adj., of the Piraeus: litora, O.

Pisaeus.definition: Pīsaeus adj., of Pisa (in Elis), Pisaean: Arethusa, O.: oliva, won in the Olympic games, Iu.

Pleias.definition: Plēïas or Plēas (Plīas) adis, f , *plhi+a/s or *pleia/s, a Pleiad, one of the seven stars, O.— Plur, the Pleiades, Pleiads, V., H., O.

Poecile.definition: Poecilē es, f , *poiki/lh (stoa/), the picture gallery, frescoed hall in the market-place of Athens, N.

Poeni.definition: Poenī ōrum, m the Carthaginians (as of Phoenician origin), C., V.—Sing, the Carthaginian, i. e. Hannibal.—Sing. collect.: Poenus advena, L.: uterque Poenus, i. e. Carthaginians in Africa and Spain, H.

Poeninus.definition: Poenīnus (Pennī-) adj. Penninus, from Celtic pen (peak), became Poeninus, as if from Poenus, after Hannibal's passage, Pennine (of the Alps, from the Great St. Bernhard to the St. Gotthard), L.

Pollux.definition: Pollūx ūcis, m , *poludeu/khs, a son of Tyndarus and Leda, twin brother of Castor, C., V., H.: geminus Pollux, i. e. Castor and Pollux, H.

Polyhymnia.definition: Polyhymnia ae, f , *polu/mnia (rich in song), one of the Muses, H., O.

Pomona.definition: Pōmōna ae, f pomum, the goddess of fruit and fruit-trees, Pomona , O.

Pompeius.definition: Pompēius (trisyl.), a, a gentile name.—As adj., of a Pompey, Cs., C., O.—Esp., Cn. Pompeius Magnus, the triumvir, Cs., C.

Porsena.definition: Porsena (C., H.), Porsenna (C., V.), or Porsinna (L.), ae, m a king of Etruria.

Portunus.definition: Portūnus ī, m portus, the god of harbors (the Greek Palaemon), C., V., O.

Priapus.definition: Priāpus ī, m , *pri/apos, Priapus, the god of gardens and vineyards, V., H., O., Iu.: vitreus, a drinking-vessel, Ct.—A lecherous man, O., Ct.

Primigenia.definition: Prīmigenia ae, f primus+GEN-, aboriginal, primal (of Fortuna, as guardian of her favorites from birth), C., L.

Procne.definition: Procnē (Progne), ēs, f , *pro/knh, a daughter of Pandion, turned into a swallow, O.—A swallow, V., O.

Procyon.definition: Procyōn —, m , *proku/wn, the little dog (rising before the dog-star), C., H.

Prometheus.definition: Promētheus (trisyl.), eī (ei, V.), acc. ea, voc. eu, *promhtheu/s (Forethinker), a son of Iapetus, who stole fire from heaven for men, C., H., V., Pr., O., Iu.

Proserpina.definition: Prōserpina (Pros-, H.), ae, f , *persefo/nh, Proserpine, wife of Pluto, and queen of the Lower World, C., V., H., O.: Imperiosa, i. e. death, H.

Proteus.definition: Prōteus (disyl.), eī, acc. ea, voc. eu, m , *prwteu/s, a sea-god of changeable form, V., H., O.: Protei columnae, i. e. the boundary of Egypt, V.: Quo teneam voltūs mutantem Protea modo? i. e. How bind one so fickle! …

Puniceus.definition: Pūniceus adj. Punicus, Punic, Carthaginian , O.— Reddish, red, purple-colored : taeniae, V.: rosa, H.: crocus, O.

Punicus.definition: Pūnicus (Poen-) adj. Poeni, Punic, Carthaginian : litterae: fides, i. e. perfidy , S.: perfidia, L.: regna, V.— Of the Phoenician color, purple, purplered : rostra (psittaci), O.: punico Lugubre mutavit sagum, H.

Pygmaeus.definition: Pygmaeus adj., Pygmaean, of the Pygmies (fabulous dwarfs of Africa): mater, i. e. Oenoe, queen of the Pygmies, O.: virgo, a female dwarf, Iu.

Pyrenaeus.definition: Pȳrēnaeus adj., of Pyrene, Pyrenaean: montes, the Pyrenees, Cs., L.: saltus, Cs., L.—As subst m., the Pyrenees, L.

Pythagoricus.definition: Pȳthagoricus (L.), *puthagoriko/s, adj., Pythagorean, of Pythagoras (a philos. of Samos).

Pythia1.definition: Pȳthia ae, f , *puthi/a, the priestess of the Delphic Apollo, the Pythoness, Pythia, C., N.

Pythia2.definition: Pȳthia ōrum, n , *pu/thia, the Pythian games, celebrated at Delphi every fourth year in honor of Apollo, H., O.

Pythicus.definition: Pȳthicus (L.), *puthiko/s, or Pȳthius (C., H., Pr., Iu.), *pu/thios, adj., Pythian, Delphic.

pabulatio.definition: pābulātiō ōnis, f pabulor, a collecting of fodder, foraging : nostrae pabulationes, Cs.: pabulatione intercludi, Cs.

pabulator.definition: pābulātor ōris, m pabulor a forager , Cs., L.

pabulor.definition: pābulor ātus, ārī, dep. pabulum, to forage : angustius, Cs.: pabulandi causā mittere, Cs.: pabulantes (nostros) profligant, Ta.— Supin. acc. : pabulatum cohortes misere, L.

pabulum.definition: pābulum ī, n 1 PA-, food, nourishment, food for cattle, fodder, pasturage, grass : pecoris, S.: secare pabulum, Cs.: comparare, N.: hirundo Pabula parva legens, V.: pabula carpsit ovis, O.: Pabula canescunt, i. e. the…

pacalis.definition: pācālis e, adj. pax, of peace, peaceful : olea, O.: laurus, token of peace , O.: flammae, on the altar of Peace , O.

pacatus.definition: pācātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of paco, pacified, quieted, peaceful, quiet, calm, tranquil, undisturbed : civitates: tempus: provincia pacatissima: nec hospitale quicquam pacatumve, L.: mare, H.: voltus, O.—As su…

pacifer.definition: pācifer fera, ferum, adj. pax+1 FER-, peacebringing, peaceful, pacific : oliva, V.: Cyllenius, Mercury , O.

pacificatio.definition: pācificātiō ōnis, f pacifico, a peace-making, pacification : spes pacificationis.

pacificator.definition: pācificātor ōris, m pacifico, a peace-maker, pacificator : Allobrogum: Athamanum, L.

pacificatorius.definition: pācificātōrius adj. pacificator, peace-making, pacificatory : legatio.

pacifico.definition: (pācificō) —, ātus, āre pacificus, to make peace, conclude peace : Iugurthā pacificante, S.: ad pacificandum stabis, L.— Supin. acc. : legati pacificatum venerunt, L.— To pacify, appease : caelestes pacificasset, Ct.

pacificus.definition: pācificus adj. pax+2 FAC-, peace-making, pacific, peaceable : persona.

paciscor.definition: pacīscor pactus, ī, dep. PAC-, to agree together, bargain, contract, agree, covenant, stipulate, transact : ut ex areā, nisi pactus esset orator, ne tolleret: magnā mercede cum principibus, ut, etc., L.: votis Ne Adda…

paco.definition: pācō āvī, ātus, āre pax, to make peaceful, quiet, pacify, subdue, soothe : Amanum: Galliam, Cs.: qui nuper pacati erant, Cs.: Erymanthi nemora, V.: incultae pacantur vomere silvae, are subdued , H.

pacta.definition: pacta ae, f 1 pactus, a betrothed woman, bride : gremiis adducere pactas, V.

pactio.definition: pactiō ōnis, f paciscor, an agreeing, agreement, covenant, contract, stipulation, bargain, pact : de civibus cum sociis facere pactiones: pactione libertatem perdere: neque ullum telum per pactiones loquentium traicie…

pactor.definition: pactor ōris, m paciscor, a contractor, negotiator : societatis pactores.

pactum.definition: pactum ī, n 1 pactus, an agreement, covenant, contract, stipulation, compact, pact : pactum est, quod inter aliquos convenit: in pacto manere, L.: pacti formula: ex pacto et convento.— A marriage-contract , Iu.—Abl. i…

pactus1.definition: pactus adj. P. of paciscor, agreed, settled, determined, covenanted, stipulated : pro capite pretium: pacta et constituta cum Manlio dies: merces, H.: coniunx, betrothed , V.

paedagogus.definition: paedagōgus ī, m , paidagwgo/s, a governor, preceptor, pedagogue (a slave to guide and attend children), C.—In jest, of an attentive lover, T.

paedico.definition: paedīco —, —, āre, to practice unnatural vice upon, Ct.

paedor.definition: paedor or pēdor ōris, m 2 PV-, nastiness, filth : barba pedore horrida, C. poët.: exuere pae<*> dorem, Ta.

paelex.definition: paelex or pēlex or pellex icis, f , pa/llac, a kept mistress, concubine (as rival of a wife): filiae pelex: matris, O.: (Medea) ulta paelicem, H.: horrida, Iu.: virginem servo pellicem dederat, Cu.

paene.definition: paene (not pēne), adv., nearly, almost, as I may say: duo maria paene coniungere: hostes victi, S.: senex paene agrestis: non solum . . . sed paene etiam, Cs.: Quam paene furvae regna Proserpinae . . . vidimus, H.: di…

paeninsula.definition: paenīnsula (pēn-) ae, f paene+insula, a peninsula , L., Ct.

paenitendus.definition: paenitendus (not poen-), adj. P. of paeniteo, to be repented of, blamable, objectionable : haud paenitendus magister, L.

paenitens.definition: paenitēns entis, adj. P. of paeniteo, repentant, penitent .—As subst m. : optimus est portus paenitenti mutatio consili.

paenitentia.definition: paenitentia (not poen-), ae, f paeniteo, repentance, penitence : celer, L.: eius (facinoris), Cu.: sera, Ph.: mutari in paenitentiam, Ta.

paeniteo.definition: paeniteō (not poen-), uī, —, ēre cf. poena, to make sorry, cause to repent : nihil, quod paenitere possit, facere: Paenitet et torqueor, O.: quo modo quemquam paeniteret quod fecisset?— To repent, be sorry : paenitere…

paenula.definition: paenula (pēn-) ae, f a woollen outer garment covering the body, travelling-cloak, mantle: paenulā inretitus: ita egi, ut non scinderem paenulam, did not tear his cloak (i. e. press him violently to stay).

paenulatus.definition: paenulātus adj. paenula, wearing the paenula, in travelling dress .

paeon.definition: paeōn ōnis, m , paiw/n, a metrical foot of one long and three short syllables (in any order).

paetulus.definition: paetulus adj. dim. paetus with a cast in the eye, slightly blink-eyed .

paetus.definition: paetus adj., with a cast in the eye, blinking, leering, H.

paganus.definition: pāgānus adj. pagus, of the country, of a village, rustic : foci, O.—As subst m., a countryman, peasant, villager, rustic , C.— As subst, a civilian, non-combatant , Iu., Ta.

pagatim.definition: pāgātim adv. pagus, by villages, in every village : templa pagatim sacrata, L.

pagella.definition: pāgella ae, f dim. pagina, a little page .

pagina.definition: pāgina ae, f PAC-, a leaf of paper, sheet, page : hanc paginam tenere: totas paginas commovere: paginas in annalibus magistratuum percurrere, L.: millesima, Iu.: postrema tua, letter. —A slab, tablet : insignis honoru…

paginula.definition: pāginula ae, f dim. pagina, a little page .

pagus.definition: pāgus ī, m PAC-, a district, canton, hundred, province, region : pagos et compita circum, the country , V.: si me toto laudet vicinia pago, Iu.—Among the Gauls and Germans, a district, canton , Cs., Ta.— Collect., the…

pala.definition: pāla ae, f for * pagla; PAC-, a spade : palae innixus, L.— The bezel (of a ring): anuli.

palaestra.definition: palaestra ae, f , palai/stra, a wrestling school, wrestling-place, place of exercise, gymnasium, palaestra: statuas in palaestrā ponere: gramineae palaestrae, V.—A place of discipline in rhetoric, school of rhetoric, …

palaestrice.definition: palaestricē adv., after the manner of the palaestra: in xysto spatiari.

palaestricus.definition: palaestricus adj. , palaistriko/s, of the palaestra, palaestric: motūs, i. e. of a dancingmaster: praetor, devoted to the palaestra.

palaestrita.definition: palaestrīta ae, m , palaistri/ths, a professional wrestler, gymnast.

palam1.definition: palam adj., openly, publicly, undisguisedly, plainly: nihil ausurus, S.: ad se adire, Cs.: quae in foro palam gesta sunt: agere: non per praestigias, sed palam: palam et aperte dicere: Luce palam, V.: palam duobus exe…

palam2.definition: palam praep., with abl. 1 palam, before, in the presence of : te palam, H.: Marte palam, O.: rem creditori palam populo solvit, L.

palatium.definition: palātium ī, n Pales, the Palatine hill, on which was the residence of Augustus ; hence, in plur, a palace : Romana, V.: secreta palatia matris, the temple of Cybele , Iu.: magni palatia caeli, the palace of the sky , O.

palatum.definition: palātum ī, n, and (rarely) palātus, ī , m the palate: quae (voluptas) palato percipiatur: boum dare membra palato, O.: udum, V.: obserare palatum, i. e. to be silent, Ct.: caeli, i. e. vault, Enn. ap. C.—Fig., the pal…

palea.definition: palea ae, f 1 PAL-, chaff : cum ne paleae quidem relinquerentur: inanes, V.: horna, H.

palearia.definition: paleāria —, plur n. palea, a dew-lap (of an ox).— Only nom. and acc: pendula, O.: a mento palearia pendent, V.

palimpsestus.definition: palimpsēstus ī, m , pali/myhstos, a parchment rewritten after erasure, palimpsest, C., Ct.

paliurus.definition: paliūrus ī, m , pali/ouros, a plant, Christ'sthorn, V.

palla.definition: palla ae, f 2 PA-, a long robe, mantle (worn by ladies): circumdata, H.: longa, V.: scissa, Iu. — A mantle, outer garment : cum pallā et cothurnis: honesta, the tragedian's garb , H.: Tyrio saturata murice (worn by Ap…

pallens.definition: pallēns entis, adj. P. of palleo, pale, wan : umbrae Erebi, V.: persona, Iu.: morte futurā, V.: terrore puellae, O.: morbi, making pale , V.: famā, bad , Ta.—Of color, faint, pale, yellowish, dark : violae, V.: hedera…

palleo.definition: palleō uī, —, ēre 2 PAL-, to be pale, turn pale, blanch : sudat, pallet: pallent amisso sanguine venae, O.: morbo, Iu.: Palleat omnis amans, must look pale , O.: Ambitione malā aut argenti pallet amore, H.: nunc utile…

pallesco.definition: pallēscō palluī, ere, inch. palleo, to turn pale, blanch : nullā culpā, H.: super his, to turn pale with emotion , H.: tardis curis, Pr.— To turn pale, be yellow : saxum quoque palluit auro, O.: pallescunt frondes, wi…

palliatus.definition: palliātus adj. pallium, dressed in a pallium (usu. of Greeks): Graeculus iudex: illi palliati, i. e. Grecian statues .

pallidulus.definition: pallidulus adj. dim. pallidus, somewhat pale, rather colorless , Ct., Iu.

pallidus.definition: pallidus adj. with comp. 2 PAL-, pale, pallid, colorless : ut pallidus omnis Cenā desurgat dubiā, H.: hospes pallidior statuā, Ct.: (Dido) morte futurā, V.: recto voltu et pallidus, i. e. well or sick , Iu.: Pallida m…

palliolum.definition: palliolum ī, n dim. pallium, a small Greek mantle, little cloak : sordidum, Caec. ap. C.; Iu.— A hood , O.

pallium.definition: pallium ī, n palla, a cover, coverlet : onerosa pallia iactat, Iu.— A Grecian cloak, mantle : umerum pallio onerare, T.: Pone adprendit pallio, T.: purpureum: cum pallio inambulare, L.

pallor.definition: pallor ōris, m 2 PAL-, pale color, paleness, wanness, pallor : quo tremore et pallore dixit!: albus, H.: gelidus, O.: pallor ora occupat, V.: amantium, H.: tot hominum pallores, the paleness of death , Ta.— Alarm, ter…

palma.definition: palma ae, f , pala/mh, the palm, flat hand: cum manum dilataverat, palmae illius similem, etc.: cavis undam palmis Sustinet, V.: faciem contundere palmā, Iu.—The hand: palmarum intentus: passis palmis salutem petere, …

palmaris.definition: palmāris e, adj. palma, of the palm, superior, excellent : statua.

palmarius.definition: palmārius adj. palma, of the palm, deserving the prize, excellent : sententia.—As subst n., a prize-achievement, masterpiece : palmarium repperisse, T.

palmatus.definition: palmātus adj. palma, bearing palms, embroidered with palm-twigs : tunica (of a triumphing general), L.

patrius1.definition: patrius adj. pater, of a father, fatherly, paternal : animus, T.: ius et potestas: maiestas, L.: poenas patrias persequi: mos: amor, V.: arae, i. e. of Father Apollo , O.: patrium mimae donare fundum laremque, H.: ace…

patrius2.definition: patrius adj. patria, of a native country, of home, native : sermo, C., H.: carmen, a national song , Cu.: palaestrae, V.

patro.definition: patrō āvī, ātus, āre, to bring to pass, execute, perform, achieve, accomplish, bring about, effect, finish, conclude: operibus patratis: bellum, bring to an end, S.: abesse, dum facinus patratur, L.: pacis patrandae m…

patrocinium.definition: patrōcinium ī, n patrocinor, protection, advocacy, defence, patronage : orbis terrae: cuius patrocinio civitas plurimum utebatur, S.: utraque factio Macedonum patrociniis utebatur, N.: voluptas plurimorum patrociniis …

patrocinor.definition: patrōcinor ātus, ārī, dep. patronus, to be a patron, afford protection, defend, support .—With dat: indotatis, T.

patrona.definition: patrōna ae, f patronus, a protectress, patroness : te mihi patronam capio, T.: lex sociorum populi R. patrona.

patronus.definition: patrōnus ī, m pater, a protector, defender, patron : nefas est deserere patronos, Cs.: plebis, L.: patroni civitatis, Cs.: coloniae.— The former master (of a freedman), C.— A defender, advocate, pleader : si patronus …

patruelis.definition: patruēlis e, adj. patruus, of a father's brother, child of a father's brother (cf. consobrinus): frater noster cognatione patruelis, amore germanus, by blood my cousin, my brother in affection.— Of a cousin, of cousin…

patruus1.definition: patruus ī, m pater, a father's brother, paternal uncle (cf. avunculus): Iunius, patruus pueri: tutor et patruus: qui dedit tribus patruis aconita, Iu.— A censor, reprover : pertristis: ne sis patruus mihi, H.

patruus2.definition: patruus adj. 1 patruus, of a father's brother, of an uncle : patruae verbera linguae, an uncle's , H.: ense cadit patruo, O.

patulus.definition: patulus adj. 2 PAT-, spread out, standing open, open, wide : pina duabus grandibus patula conchis, etc.: aures, H.: fenestrae, O.: latitudo, i. e. the open highway , Ta.— Spread out, spreading, extended, broad, wide :…

paucitas.definition: paucitās ātis, f paucus, a small number, fewness, scarcity, paucity : mira: uti multitudinem paucitas superaret, S.: legionem propter paucitatem despiciebant, Cs.: amicorum: paucitatem eorum insignem facere, L.

pauculus.definition: (pauculus) adj. dim. paucus, very few, very little ; only plur: loquitor paucula, T.: ut ibi pauculos dies esset.

paucus.definition: paucus adj. with comp. and sup. PAV-, few, little : in diebus paucis Chrysis moritur, T.: his paucis diebus, a few days ago : causae: paucorum hominum (i. e. paucis hominibus familiariter utens), H.: ne pauciores cum …

paulatim.definition: paulātim (not paull-), adv. paulum, by little and little, by degrees, gradually : paulatim Germanos consuescere Rhenum transire, Cs.: licentia crevit, S.: adnabam terrae, V.: vitia exuere, Iu.: circumfusā multitudine,…

paulisper.definition: paulisper (not paull-), adv. paulum+per, for a little while, for a short time : paulisper mane, T.: ab rege sustentati, S.: lecticā paulisper depositā: intermittere proelium, Cs.: sedit tacitus paulisper, donec, etc., L.

paulo.definition: paulō (not paull-), adv. abl n. of paulus.— As abl. of difference in expressions of comparison, by a little, a little, somewhat : liberius paulo: civis haud paulo melior, quam, etc.: paulo magis adfabre factus: paulo …

paululo.definition: paululō (not paull-), adv. abl n. of paululus, by a little, a little, somewhat : si nequeas paululo, at quanti queas, at a trifling price , T.: paululo deesse.

paululum.definition: paululum (not paull-), adv. paululus, a little, a very little, somewhat : concede istuc paululum, T.: mente paululum inminutā, S.

paululus.definition: paululus (not paull-), adj. dim. paulus, very little, very small : si paululum modo quid te fugerit, T.: via, L.: equi hominesque paululi et graciles, L.—As subst n., a little bit, trifle : paululum pecuniae, T.: paul…

paulum.definition: paulum (not paull-), adv. paulus, a little, somewhat : concede paulum istuc, a little way , T.: paulum a fugā aberant, S.: supra eum locum, Cs.: differre: paulum aspectu conterritus haesit, V.: paulum praelabitur ante…

paulus.definition: paulus (not paull-), adj. PAV-, little, small : paulo sumptu, T.— As subst n., a little, trifle : quasi vero paulum intersiet, T.: supplici, T.: lucri, T.: paulum huic Cottae tribuit partium, allotted a small part of …

pauper.definition: pauper peris, adj. with comp. and sup. PAV-, poor, not wealthy, of small means : homo: quae in patriā honeste pauper vivit, T.: ex pauperrimo dives factus: horum Semper ego optarim pauperrimus esse bonorum, H.: aquae,…

pauperculus.definition: pauperculus adj. dim. pauper, poor, poor little : anus, T.: mater, H.

pauperies.definition: pauperiēs —, acc f. pauper, poverty, limited means : hinc abii propter pauperiem, T.: pauperiem perferre, V.: pauperiem pati, H.: immunda, H.

paupero.definition: pauperō —, —, āre pauper, to impoverish, rob, deprive : te cassā nuce, H.

paupertas.definition: paupertās ātis, f pauper, poverty, small means, moderate circumstances : paupertas probro haberi, S.: patientia paupertatī s.— Need, want, indigence : Paupertas mihi onus visumst, T.: infelix, Iu.

pausia.definition: pausia ae, f a superior kind of olive, V.

pauxillulus.definition: pauxillulus adj. dim. pauxillus, dim. of paucus, very little .—As subst n., a little bit, trifling remnant : Nummorum, T.

pavefactus.definition: pavefactus adj. paveo+factus, in terror, dismayed, alarmed : ego, O.: pectora, O.

paveo.definition: paveō pāvī, —, ēre 4 PV-, to be struck with fear, be in terror, tremble, quake with fear, be afraid, be terrified : mihi paveo, T.: quaeres, quando iterum paveas, H.: incerto voltu pavens adcurrit, S.: admiratione pav…

pavesco.definition: pavēscō —, —, ere, inch. paveo, to begin to fear, be alarmed : omni strepitu, S.: bellum, Ta.

pavide.definition: pavidē adv. pavidus, with fear, fearfully, timorously : fugere, L.

pavidus.definition: pavidus adj. paveo, trembling, quaking, fearful, timid, timorous, shy : matres, V.: lepus, H.: aves, O.: ex somno mulier, startled out of her sleep , L.: oppidani pavidi, ne iam facta in urbem via esset, etc., in terr…

pavimentatus.definition: pavīmentātus adj. pavimentum, furnished with a pavement, paved : porticus.

pavimentum.definition: pavīmentum ī, n pavio, a level surface beaten firm, hard floor, pavement : facere: mero Tingere pavimentum, H.: palma ex pavimento extitisse, Cs.

pavio.definition: paviō —, —, īre 4 PV-, to beat, strike : terram.

pavito.definition: pavitō —, —, āre, freq. paveo, to tremble, quake, be fearful : prosequitur pavitans, V.— To have a chill , T.

pavo.definition: pāvō ōnis, m a peacock: cauda pavoni donata.—Eaten as a delicacy, H., Iu.

pavor.definition: pavor ōris, m 4 PV-, a trembling, quaking, shaking, terror, anxiety, fear, dread, alarm : pavor sapientiam omnem mi exanimato expectorat, Enn. ap. C.: pavor ceperat milites ne mortiferum esset volnus, L.: corda stravi…

pax.definition: pāx pācis, f PAC-, a compact, agreement, treaty, peace, treaty of peace, reconciliation : cum eis facta pax non erit pax: maritima: pro emptā pace bellum intulerunt: pacem petere, Cs.: pangere, L.: Nulla dies pacem ha…

peccans.definition: peccāns ntis, adj. P. of pecco, sinful, full of sin : immortalitas.—Plur n . as subst, offenders, sinners : ad officium peccantes redire cogere, N.

peccatum.definition: peccātum ī, n pecco, a fault, error, mistake, transgression, sin : pro huius peccatis ego supplicium sufferam? T.: si peccato locus esset, S.: peccatum est patriam prodere: stultitiae: paucis verbis tria magna peccata…

peccatus.definition: peccātus ūs, m pecco, a failing, fault, trespass : in manifesto peccatu teneri.

pecco.definition: peccō āvī (peccāris for peccāveris, Pr.), ātus, āre, to miss, mistake, do amiss, transgress, commit a fault, offend, sin: quid peccavi? T.: alius magis alio vel peccat vel recte facit: plura in hac re, T.: multa alia:…

pecorosus.definition: pecorōsus adj. pecus, rich in cattle : Palatia, Pr.

pecten.definition: pecten inis, m PEC-, a comb (for the hair): deducit pectine crines, O.: digitis inter se pectine iunctis, i. e. interlocked , O.— The reed, sley (of a loom): arguto percurrens pectine telas, V.— A comb, card, heckle (…

pecto.definition: pectō pēxī, pexus, ere PEC-, to comb : pexo capillo: caesariem, H.: barbam, Iu.: ferum (cervum), V.: ipsa comas pectar, O.

pectus.definition: pectus oris, n PAC-, a breast, breast-bone : pectore in adverso ensem Condidit, V.: in pectus cadit pronus, O.: latum demisit pectore clavom, H.: esse vincto pectore, ut gracilae sient, tightlaced , T.— The stomach : …

pecu.definition: (pecu) n PAC-, cattle, large cattle .—Only plur nom . and acc: pecua captiva praeter equos, L.: pecua relinquuntur, i. e. the pastures .

pecuarius.definition: pecuārius adj. pecua, of cattle : res, cattleraising .—As subst m., a cattle-breeder, grazier : diligentissimus: damnatis aliquot pecuariis, i. e. farmers of public pastures , L.—As subst n. plur., herds of cattle , V…

peculator.definition: pecūlātor ōris, m peculor, an embezzler, peculator , C., Ta.

peculatus.definition: pecūlātus ūs, m peculor, an embezzlement, peculation : aerari, S.: peculatūs damnari.

peculiaris.definition: pecūliāris e, adj. peculium, of private property, one's own, proper, special, peculiar : tuus testis: vestra patria peculiarisque res p., L.— Extraordinary, special : edictum.

peculium.definition: pecūlium ī, n pecu, property : cupiditas peculi: cura peculi, i. e. anxiety for gain , H.— Private property, separate estate : fili, L.: cultis augere peculia servis, fees , Iu.

pecunia.definition: pecūnia ae, f pecu, property, riches, wealth : pecuniam facere, accumulate : ut pecuniā fortunis<*> que nostris contentus sit: ea (i. e. pecora) pecunia illis est, L.— Money : Pecuniam neglegere, T.: publica: certa, a…

pecuniarius.definition: pecūniārius adj. pecunia, of money, pecuniary : indicium: rei pecuniariae socius, in a money matter : praemia rei pecuniariae, in money , Cs.

pecuniosus.definition: pecūniōsus adj. with sup. pecunia, moneyed, rich, wealthy : mulier: senectus, Ta.: homo pecuniosissimus.

pecus1.definition: pecus pecoris, n PAC-, cattle (all domestic animals kept for food or service): pabulum pecoris, S.: equinum, a stud , V.: setigerum, the bristly herd (i. e. of swine), O.: deus pecoris, i. e. Pan , O.: Ignavom fucos p…

pecus2.definition: pecus udis (plur acc. once pecuda, C.), f PAC-, a head of cattle, beast, brute, animal, one of a herd : pecudes pictaeque volucres, land animals , V.: quantum natura hominis pecudibus antecedat, domestic animals.—A sh…

pedalis.definition: pedālis e, adj. pes, of the size of a foot : sol mihi videtur quasi pedalis, a foot in diameter : in latitudinem trabes, Cs.

pedarius.definition: pedārius adj. pes, of the foot, at the foot : senatores, senators of no eminence, who voted as followers of others , Ta.—Plur m . as subst. (sc. senatores), C.

pedes.definition: pedes itis, m pes, a foot-traveller, walker : si pedes incedat, on foot , L.: cum pedes iret in hostem, V.: pedes per nives ingredi coepit, Cu.— A foot-soldier : ne quem peditem ad conloquium adduceret, Cs.: tria mili…

pedester.definition: pedester tris, tre, adj. pes, on foot, pedestrian , C.: copiae, infantry : exercitus, N.: scutum, of a foot-soldier , L.: acies, V.— On land, by land : pedestres navalesque pugnae: itinera, the roads by land , Cs.—Fig…

pedetemptim.definition: pedetemptim (-tentim) adv. pes+tempto, step by step, slowly : pedetemptim et sedato nisu, Pac. ap. C.: quaerendis pedetentim vadis in terram evasere (elephanti), L.—Fig., by degrees, gradually, cautiously : accessus: …

pedica.definition: pedica ae, f pes, a fetter, springe, snare : iumenta velut pedicā capta in glacie, L.: gruibus pedicas ponere, V.

pedisequa.definition: pedisequa ae, f pes+SEC-, a female attendant, waiting-woman, handmaid : ad pedisequas accedo, T.—Fig.: iuris scientiam eloquentiae tamquam pedisequam adiunxisti.

pedisequus.definition: pedisequus ī, m pes+SEC-, a follower on foot, footman, servant, page, lackey : clamor pedisequorum nostrorum.

peditatus.definition: peditātus ūs, m pedes, foot-soldiers, foot, infantry : civem peditatu instruere: peditatum cogere, Cs.

pedo.definition: pēdō pepēdī, pēditus, ere, to break wind, H.— P. perf. n. as subst., Ct.

pedum.definition: pedum ī, n pes, a shepherd's crook, sheephook , V.

pegma.definition: pēgma atis, n , ph=gma, a fixture of boards, bookcase, book-shelf: tua pegmata.—In a theatre, a movable platform, stage machine, Ph., Iu.

peiero.definition: pēierō, perierō, or periūrō āvī, ātus, āre per+iuro, to swear falsely, perjure oneself : verbis conceptis: quā re periuras? H.: Hic putat esse deos, et peierat, Iu.: ius peieratum, a false <*>ath , H.: periurati dii, …

peior.definition: pēior us, adj. comp; see 1 malus.

pelagius.definition: pelagius adj. , pela/gios, of the sea: cursus, Ph.

pelagus.definition: pelagus ī, n , pe/lagos, the sea: fervit aestu pelagus, Pac. ap. C.: pelagus tenuere rates, the open sea, V.: Commisit pelago ratem, H.: rector pelagi, i. e. Neptune, O.: pelago premit arva sonanti, fiood, V.

pelamys.definition: pēlamys ydis, f , phlami/s, a young tunnyfish, Iu.

pelicatus.definition: pēlicātus (paeli-) ūs, m the relation of a mistress, concubinage: matris pelicatum ferre: pelicatūs suspitio.

pellax.definition: pellāx ācis, adj. per+1 LAC-, seductive, deceitful : Ulixes, V.

pellectio.definition: pellēctiō ōnis, f pellego, a perusal .

pellicio.definition: pelliciō or perliciō lexī, lectus, ere see 1 LAC-, to allure, entice, inveigle, decoy, coax, wheedle : senem per epistulas, T.: mulierem ad se: populum in servitutem, L.: maiorem partem sententiarum sale tuo, won over .

pellicula.definition: pellicula ae, f dim. pellis, a small skin, little hide : haedina: furtivae aurum Pelliculae, i. e. the golden fleece , Iu.—Prov.: pelliculam curare, to coddle oneself , H.

pellis.definition: pellis is, f a skin, hide, felt, pelt: rugosa (ranae), Ph.: caprina: pelles pro velis, Cs.: fulvique insternor pelle leonis, V.: deformem pro cute pellem aspice, Iu.— Prov.: Detrahere pellem, i. e. to expose one's rea…

pellitus.definition: pellītus adj. pellis, covered with skins, clad in skins : oves, i. e. of very fine wool (protected by a covering of skins), H.— Esp., of the ancient Sardinians: Sardi, L.: testes, i. e. from Sardinia .

pello.definition: pellō pepulī, pulsus, ere 1 PAL-, to beat, strike, knock, push, drive, hurl, impel, propel : fores, T.: pueri pulsi: ter pede terram (in the tripudium), H.: undique magno Pulsa domus strepitu, H.— To drive out, drive …

peloris.definition: pelōris idis, f , pelwri/s, a large shell-fish, the giant mussel, H.

pelta.definition: pelta ae, f , pe/lth, a light shield, shaped like a half-moon, pelt, Thracian shield, L., V, O.

peltastae.definition: peltastae arum, m , peltastai/, soldiers armed with the pelt, peltasts, L., N.

peltatus.definition: peltātus adj. pelta, armed with the pelt , O.

pelvis.definition: pelvis is, f PLE-, a basin, laver , Iu.

penarius.definition: penārius adj. penus, for provisions : cella.

penatiger.definition: penātiger era, erum, adj. penates+GES-, carrying the household gods , O.

pendeo.definition: pendeō pependī, —, ēre PAND-, to hang, hang down, be suspended : sagittae pendebant ab umero: pendebant molles super ora capilli, O.: telum summo clipei umbone pependit, V.: chlamydemque, ut pendeat apte, Conlocat, ha…

pendo.definition: pendō pependī, pēnsus, ere PAND-, to suspend, weigh, weigh out : pensas examinat herbas, O.— To weigh out in payment, pay, pay out : stipendium quotannis, Cs.: pecuniam Pisoni: populo mercedem, Iu.— Fig., to pay, suff…

pendulus.definition: pendulus adj. PAND-, hanging, hanging down, pendent : collum, H.: libra, O.: tela, O.— Fig., doubtful, uncertain, hesitating : dubiae spe pendulus horae, H.

penes.definition: penes praep. with acc. 1 PA-, with, at the house of (only with acc. of pers. ; sometimes after its case): istaec iam penes vos psaltriast? T.: penes accusatorem fuisse: penes quem quisque sit, Cs.: mentis causa malae …

penetrabilis.definition: penetrābilis e, adj. penetro, penetrable, vulnerable : corpus nullo telo, O.— Piercing, penetrating : Boreae frigus, V.: fulmen, O.

penetralis.definition: penetrālis e, adj. penetro, piercing, penetrating, inward, inner, internal, interior, innermost : adyta, V.: foci.—As subst n., an inner part, interior, inside space, inner room : penetrale urbis, L.— Usu. plur: faust…

penetro.definition: penetrō āvī, ātus, āre penus+1 TER-, to enter, penetrate, betake oneself : sub terras: ad ipsos (deos): in castra hostium, L.: per angustias: eo, thus far , N.: penetrat vox ad aures, O.: in eam speluncam penetratum c…

penicillus.definition: pēnicillus ī, m dim. peniculus, a painter's brush, hair-pencil : luctum penicillo imitari: pingere coloribus tuis, penicillo meo, i. e. style .

peniculus.definition: pēniculus ī, m dim. penis, a sponge , T.

penis.definition: pēnis is, m a tail (old): caudam antiqui penem vocabant.—The penis, C., H., Iu.—Lust, wantonness, dissipation: ganeo, manu, ventre, pene bona patria laceraverat, S.

penitus.definition: penitus adv. PA-, inwardly, deeply, far within, into the inmost part : saxum excisum: defossa, V.: penitus terrae defigitur arbos, V.: penitus ad extremos finīs se recepisse, Cs.: penitus in Thraciam se abdidit, N.: m…

penna.definition: penna ae, f PET-, a feather, plume (on a bird; often confounded with pinna): pennarum taurum nitor, Ph.: maduere graves aspergine pennae, O.—Plur, a wing : quatere in aëre, O.: pennis coruscant, V. (al. pinnis).— A fe…

pennatus.definition: pennātus adj. penna, furnished with wings, winged : serpentes, O.

pensilis.definition: pēnsilis e, adj. PAND-, hanging, pendent, pensile : prumae, i. e. cushions of down , Iu.: uva, hung up to <*> , H.: horti, i. e. on arches , Cu.

pensio.definition: pēnsiō ōnis, f PAND-, a paying, payment, instalment : tribus pensionibus solvi, L.: tua coniunx nimium di<*> debet populo R. tertiam pensionem (i. e. the death of her third husband).— Rent, rental , Iu.

pensito.definition: pēnsitō āvī, —, āre, freq. penso, to weigh out, pay : vectigalia nobis: praedia, quae pensitant, i. e. are taxable .—Fig., to weigh, ponder, consider : (consilia) pensitanda, L.: saepe pensitato, an, etc., after often…

penso.definition: pēnsō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. pendo, to weigh, weigh out : aurum, L.: pensari eādem trutinā , i. e. judged by the same standard , H.— To counterbalance, contrast, compare : adversa secundis, L.: virtutibus vitia, L.— To…

pensum.definition: pēnsum ī, n P. n. of pendo, wool weighed out to a slave for a day's spinning, allotment of wool : nocturna carpentes pensa puellae, V.: famulasque ad lumina longo Exercet penso, V.: pensa manu ducunt, Iu.—Fig., a char…

penuria.definition: pēnūria (pāen-) ae, f SPA-, want, need, scarcity, destitution : victūs, H.: edendi, V.: rerum necessariarum, S.: frumenti, L.: virorum fortium: alcuius generis (amicorum): argenti, L.

penus.definition: penus —, m f., or n PA-, a store of food, provision, victuals : in cellulam penum omnem congerebam, T.: est omne, quo vescuntur homines, penus: portet frumenta penusque, H.: longam penum struere, V.

peplum.definition: peplum ī, n , pe/plos, an outer robe, robe of state, mantle (of a woman): Iliades peplum ferebant (of Athene), V.

per.definition: per praep. with acc. 1 PAR-. I. In space, through, across, through the midst of, from side to side of, traversing : itinera duo, unum per Sequanos . . . alterum per provinciam, Cs.: qui per agros fluit: it hasta per t…

pera.definition: pēra ae, f , ph/ra, a bag, wallet, Ph.

peraccommodatus.definition: per-accommodātus adj., very convenient: per fore accommodatum tibi, si, etc.

peracer.definition: per-ācer ācris, ācre, adj., very sharp.— Fig.: iudicium.

peracerbus.definition: per-acerbus adj., very harsh: uva gustatu.

peractio.definition: perāctiō ōnis, f perago, a completion : senectus aetatis est peractio tamquam fabulae, i. e. the last act of life's drama .

peracute.definition: peracūtē adv. peracutus, very sharply, with great keenness : moveri: queri.

peracutus.definition: per-acūtus adj., very clear, penetrating: vox. —Fig., very acute, very penetrating: homo: oratio.

peradulescens.definition: per-adulēscēns entis, adj., very young: homo.

peradulescentulus.definition: per-adulēscentulus ī, m dim, a very young man, N.

peraeque.definition: per-aequē adv., quite equally, uniformly: hoc peraeque in omni agro reperietis: terna milia peraeque in singulos mensīs, N.

peragito.definition: per-agitō —, ātus, āre, to harass, disturb: vehementius peragitati ab equitatu, Cs.

perago.definition: per-agō ēgī, āctus, ere, to thrust through, pierce through, transfix: latus ense, transpierce, O.—To pass through, traverse: freta, O.: cum sol peregit Signa, O.—To disturb, trouble, agitate: Sempronium usque eo, ut, …

peragratio.definition: peragrātiō ōnis, f peragro, a wandering through, traversing : itinerum.

peragro.definition: per-agrō āvī, ātus, āre per+ager, to wander through, travel, pass through, traverse : orbem terrarum: saltū s silvasque, V.—Fig., to go through, traverse, spread, search, penetrate : qua fines imperi sunt, ea . . . la…

peraltus.definition: per-altus adj., very high, lofty: ripae, L.

peramans.definition: per-amāns antis, adj., very fond: nostri.

peramanter.definition: per-amanter adv. peramens, very lovingly : me observant.

perambulo.definition: per-ambulō āvī, ātus, āre, to ramble through, go through, traverse, perambulate: viridia, Ph.: rura, H.: frigus perambulat artūs, runs through, O.: crocum floresque, i. e. the flower-strewn stage, H.

peramoenus.definition: per-amoenus adj., very pleasant: aestas, Ta.

peramplus.definition: per-amplus adj., very large, huge: simulacra.

perangustus.definition: per-angustus adj., very narrow: fretum: aditus, Cs.: via, L.: semita, Cu.

perappositus.definition: per-appositus (peradp-) adj., very suitable, highly becoming: illa mimis.

perarduus.definition: per-arduus adj., very difficult: mihi hoc perarduum et demonstrare.

perargutus.definition: per-argūtus adj., very acute, very shrewd: homo.

perarmatus.definition: per-armātus adj., thoroughly armed, well equipped: exercitus, Cu.

peraro.definition: per-arō āvī, ātus, āre, to plough through, furrow: rugis anilibus ora, O.—To furrow (a waxed tablet with the style), write: talia perarans manus, O.: peraratae tabellae, O.

perbelle.definition: per-bellē adv., very prettily, very finely: simulare.

perbene.definition: per-bene adv., very well: La<*>ine loqui: fecisse, L.

perbenigne.definition: per-benīgnē adv., very kindly, T.: per mihi benigne respondit.

perbibo.definition: per-bibō bibī, —, ere, to drink in: lacrimas, O.—Fig., to imbibe: rabiem, O.

perblandus.definition: per-blandus adj., very courteous, charming, engaging: successor: oratio, L.

perbonus.definition: per-bonus adj., very good: agri: perbono loco res erat.

perbrevis.definition: per-brevis e, adj., very short, brief, concise: orator: perbrevi tempore: altera pars per mihi brevis videtur.— Abl adv.: perbrevi, in a very short time.

percalesco.definition: per-calēscō caluī, —, ere, inch, to be heated through, grow very warm, O.

percallesco.definition: per-callēscō calluī, —, ere, inch, to become hardened, grow callous: civitatis patientia percalluerat.— Fig., to grow expert: usu rerum.

percarus.definition: per-cārus adj., very dear, much beloved: eis. —Very dear, too costly, T.

percelebro.definition: per-celebrō —, ātus, āre, to pronounce frequently, have often in one's mouth: de quā muliere plurimi versūs percelebrantur: percelebrata sermonibus res est.

perceler.definition: per-celer celeris, adj., very quick, sudden: interitus.

perceleriter.definition: per-celeriter adv., very quickly, very soon.

percello.definition: percellō culī, culsus, ere 1 CEL-, to beat down, throw down, overturn, upset : perculeris iam tu me, T.: eos Martis vis perculit.— To strike, smite, hit : femur, L.: deam, O.—Fig., to cast down, overthrow, ruin, destr…

perceptio.definition: perceptiō ōnis, f per+CAP-, a taking, receiving, gathering in, collecting : frugum.—Fig., perception, comprehension : animi perceptiones, notions .

perceptus.definition: perceptus adj. P. of percipio, perceived, observed.—Plur. n . as subst, doctrines, rules .

percipio.definition: percipiō cēpī (pluperf. percēpset, old poet. ap. C.), ceptus, ere per+capio, to take wholly, seize entirely, take possession of, seize, occupy : neque urbis odium me umquam percipit, T.— To take to oneself, assume : r…

percitus.definition: percitus adj. P. of per-cieo, greatly moved, roused, stimulated, excited : re atroci, T.: illud animo percito facere.— Excitable : ingenium, L.

percolo.definition: per-colō coluī, —, ere, to deck, beautify, adorn: quae priores eloquentiā percoluere, Ta.—To honor: coniugem, Ta.: multos praefecturis, Ta.

percommode.definition: percommodē adv. percommodus, very suitably, by great good-fortune : accidit: factum est.

percommodus.definition: per-commodus adj., very suitable, highly opportune: ipsis castris, L.

percontatio.definition: percontātiō (percūnct-) ōnis, f percontor, a persistent asking, questioning, inquiry : dictum non percontatione quaesitum: nihil de eo percontationibus reperire, Cs.: derecta, L.—As a figure of speech, C.

percontator.definition: percontātor (percūnct-) ōris, m percontor, a persistent asker, inquisitive fellow , H.

percontor.definition: percontor or percūnctor ātus, ārī, dep. per+contus, to search with a pole; the form percunctor was suggested by a mistaken etymology from cunctus, to ask particularly, question strictly, inquire, interrogate, investig…

percontumax.definition: per-contumāx ācis, adj., very obstinate, utterly contumacious, T.

percoquo.definition: per-coquō —, ctus, ere, to ripen: mora percoquit uvas, O.

percrebresco.definition: per-crēbrēscō (-bēscō) bruī or buī, —, ere, inch, to become frequent, grow prevalent, be spread abroad: quae (opinio) apud exteras nationes percrebruit: quod cum percrebuisset: cum fama percrebuisset, illum obsideri, Cs.

percrepo.definition: per-crepō —, —, āre, to resound, ring: locum percrepare vocibus.

percupio.definition: per-cupiō —, —, ere, to desire earnestly: Immo percupio, it suits me exactly, T.

percuriosus.definition: per-cūriōsus adj., very curious, highly inquisitive: servolus.

percuro.definition: per-cūrō —, ātus, āre, to heal thoroughly, cure completely: percurato volnere, L., Cu.

percurro.definition: per-currō percucurrī or percurrī, cursus, ere, to run, run along, run all the way, run through, hasten through, traverse, run over, pass over: curriculo percurre (ad villam), run quickly, T.: per temonem (currūs), alo…

percursatio.definition: percursātiō ōnis, f percurso, a travelling through, traversing : tua: Italiae.

percursio.definition: percursiō ōnis, f per+1 CEL, a running through, hastening over, rapid survey : animi multarum rerum.

percurso.definition: percursō —, —, āre, freq. percurro, to rove about : finibus nostris, L.

percussio.definition: percussiō ōnis, f percutio, a beating, striking : capitis percussiones, beatings on the head : digitorum, snapping .— As a measure of time, a beat : percussiones numerorum.

percussor.definition: percussor ōris, m percutio, a striker, murderer, assassin : Caesaris, C., Iu.

percussus2.definition: percussus ūs, m percutio, a beating, striking : Percussu crebro saxa cavantur, O.

percutio.definition: percutiō cussī (percusti, H.), cussus, ere per+quatio, to strike through and through, thrust through, pierce, transfix : gladio percussus: Mamilio pectus percussum, L.: coxam Aeneae, Iu.: non percussit locum, i. e. th…

perdepso.definition: per-depsō uī, ere, to knead, work over, Ct.

perdifficilis.definition: per-difficilis e, adj., very difficult: defensionis ratio: amnis transitu, L.

perdifficiliter.definition: perdifficiliter adv. perdifficilis, with great difficulty .

perdiligenter.definition: per-dīligenter with great diligence: epistulae scriptae.

perdisco.definition: per-discō didicī, —, ere, to learn thoroughly, get by heart: locus oratori perdiscendus: hominis speciem pingere, to know well how: diligentia in perdiscendo, Cs.

perdite.definition: perditē adv. perditus, recklessly, desperately : se gerere.— Desperately, immoderately : amare, T.

perditor.definition: perditor ōris, m perdo, a ruiner, destroyer : rei p.

perdiu.definition: per-diū adv., for a great while, very long.

perdives.definition: per-dīves itis, adj., very rich: mulier.

perdix.definition: perdīx īcis, f , pe/rdic, a plover, lapwing: garrula, O.

perdo.definition: per-dō (subj. perduint, T., C.), didī, ditus, ere, to make away with, destroy, ruin, squander, dissipate, throw away, waste, lose : fruges: se ipsum penitus: sumat, consumat, perdat, squander, T.: tempora precando, O.…

perdoceo.definition: per-doceō cuī, ctus, ēre, to teach thoroughly, instruct well: res difficilis ad perdocendum: alquid Utile mortales, O.: Phaeacida condere chartis te, O.

perdoctus.definition: perdoctus adj. P. of perdoceo, very learned, highly skilful : probe, T.: homo.

perdoleo.definition: (per-doleō) uī, —, ēre, to pain deeply, grieve greatly: tandem perdoluit (sc. tibi), T.

perdomo.definition: per-domō uī, itus, āre, to tame thoroughly, subdue, subjugate, conquer, vanquish, overcome: cives perdomiti: ad perdomandum Latium, L.: tauros furentes, tame, O.: Hispaniam, L.

perduco.definition: per-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to lead through, lead, bring, conduct, guide: filium illuc, T.: dum ad te legiones perducantur: legionem in Allobroges, Cs.: bovem ad stabula, V.—To bring, carry, lead, conduct: a lacu ad m…

peredo.definition: per-edō ēdī, ēsus, ere, to consume, devour: nec peredit ignis Aetnam, H.: Lacrimae peredere umore genas, Poët. ap. C.: morbo peresa Vellera, V.—To consume, waste away: quos amor crudeli tabe peredit, V.

peregrinabundus.definition: peregrīnābundus adj. peregrinor, travelling about : dux, L.

peregrinatio.definition: peregrīnātiō ōnis, f peregrinor, a sojourn abroad, travelling, travel : nobilis tua: peregrinationes communes: bestiae peregrinatione laetantur: longinqua, Ta.

peregrinator.definition: peregrīnātor ōris, m peregrinor, a wanderer, habitual traveller .

peregrinitas.definition: peregrīnitās ātis, f peregrinus, strange ways, foreign manners : in urbem infusa.

peregrinor.definition: peregrīnor ātus, ārī, dep. peregrinus, to sojourn in a strange land, be an alien, travel about : totā Asiā : in alienā civitate.—Fig., to go abroad, travel about, roam, wander : haec studia pernoctant nobiscum, peregr…

peregrinus.definition: peregrīnus adj. peregre, from foreign parts, strange, foreign, exotic, alien : mulier, H.: caelum, O.: reges: amores, for foreign women , O.: fasti, of foreign nations , O.: divitiae, H.: mores, Iu.: terror, of a fore…

perelegans.definition: per-ēlegāns antis, adj., very neat, elegant.

peremnis.definition: peremnis e, adj. per+amnis, relating to crossing a river : auspicia, on crossing a river .

peremptus.definition: perēmptus or perēmtus P. of perimo.

perendie.definition: perendiē adv. 1 PAR-, on the day after to-morrow : scies cras, summum perendie.

perendinus.definition: perendinus adj. perendie, after to-morrow : dies, Cs., C.

perennis.definition: perennis e (abl sing. perenne, O.), adj. with comp. per+annus, lasting throughout the year, everlasting, never failing, unceasing, perpetual, perennial : aquae: fons, Cs.: amnis, L.: cursus stellarum: adamas, O.: monu…

pereo.definition: per-eō iī or (rarely) īvī (perīt, Iu.; perīstī, Pr.; perīsse, L., O.), itūrus, īre, to pass away, come to nothing, vanish, disappear, be lost: ecqua inde perisset soror, T.: ne vena periret aquae, O.: lymphae Dolium p…

perfamiliaris.definition: per-familiāris e, adj., very intimate, most familiar: Philisto.—As subst, a familiar friend: meus: Lucullorum.

perfecte.definition: perfectē adv. perfectus, fully, completely, perfectly : eruditus: veritatem imitari.

perfectio.definition: perfectiō ōnis, f per+2 FAC-, a finishing, completing, perfection : operum: optimi: rerum reapse, non oratione perfectio.

perfector.definition: perfector ōris, m per+2 FAC-, a finisher, perfecter : mearum voluptatum, T.: dicendi.

perferens.definition: perferēns entis, adj. P. of perfero, bearing, brooking, patient : iniuriarum.

perficio.definition: perficiō fēcī, fectus, ere per+facio, to achieve, execute, carry out, accomplish, perform, despatch, bring about, bring to an end, finish, complete : comitiis perficiendis undecim dies tribuit, Cs.: iis comitiis perfe…

perfidelis.definition: per-fidēlis e, adj., very trusty: homo.

perfidia.definition: perfidia ae, f perfidus, faithlessness, treachery, perfidy : perfidiā deceptus.

perfidiose.definition: perfidiōsē adv. perfidiosus, faithlessly, treacherously, perfidiously : multa facta.

perfidiosus.definition: perfidiōsus adj. with sup. perfidia, faithless, treacherous, false, perfidious : fallax, perfidiosus: omnium perfidiosissimus: nihil perfidiosum in amicitiā.

perfrequens.definition: per-frequēns entis, adj., very crowded: emporium, L.

perfrico.definition: per-fricō cuī, —, āre, to rub all over, scratch: caput manu.—With os, to rub away blushes, cast off shame: cum os perfricuisti.

perfrigesco.definition: per-frīgēscō frīxī, —, ere, inch, to be chilled, catch cold: si perfrixit, i. e. is hoarse, Iu.

perfringo.definition: perfringō frēgī, frāctus, ere per+frango, to break through, break in pieces, shiver, shatter : iumenta nivem perfringebant, broke through , L.: saxo perfracto capite, his skull fractured , L.: perfracto saxo sortes er…

perfuga.definition: perfuga ae, m per+2 FVG-, a deserter : initio proditor deinde perfuga: pro perfugā ad eos venit, Cs.: de perfugis gravius quam de fugitivis consultum, L.

perfugio.definition: per-fugiō fūgī, —, ere, to flee for refuge: per tramites occulte in Galliam, S.: ad Porsinnam, L.: Corinthum, N.—To go over, desert: a Pompeio ad Caesarem, Cs.— Fig., to take refuge: in fidem Aetolorum, L.

perfunctio.definition: perfūnctiō ōnis, f per+1 FVG-, a performing, discharging : honorum: laborum, endurance .

perfuro.definition: per-furō —, —, ere, to rage furiously, rage on: incensus et ipse Perfurit, V.

pergaudeo.definition: per-gaudeō —, —, ēre, to rejoice greatly: Trebonium meum a te amari.

pergo.definition: pergō perrēxī, perrēctus, ere per+rego, to go on, proceed, press on, hasten, continue, go forward, march, make haste : horsum, T.: eādem viā: in Macedoniam: quā pergebat, agros vastare, marched , S.: ad castra, Cs.: a…

pergravis.definition: per-gravis e, adj., very weighty, highly important: pergravia, T.: testes.

pergraviter.definition: per-graviter adv. pergravis, very gravely, most seriously : Galbam reprehendere: offensus.

pergula.definition: pergula ae, f pergo, a school, lecture-room : omnis, the whole school , Iu.— A brothel , Pr.

perhibeo.definition: perhibeō uī, itus, ēre pro+habeo, to bring forward, adduce : alquem suo nomine.— To say , assert : ut Grai perhibent, V.: fratres, qui nuntii fuisse perhibentur.— To call, name : vatem hunc optimum: tellus, quae perhi…

perhonorificus.definition: per-honōrificus adj., very honorable: consalutatio: discessus.—Showing much honor, very respectful: collega in me.

perhorreo.definition: per-horreō —, —, ēre, to shudder at: casū s nostros, O.

perhorresco.definition: per-horrēscō ruī, ere, inch, to bristle up, roughen: aequor perhorruit, ran high, O.—To tremble greatly, shake with terror, shudder: toto corpore: clamore, O.: vexationem virginum: Bosporum, H.: conspicuum tollere ver…

perhorridus.definition: per-horridus adj., very dreadful: silvae, L.

perhumaniter.definition: perhūmāniter adv. perhumanus, very kindly, very politely : scripsit ad me.

perhumanus.definition: per-hūmānus adj., very kind, truly courteous: sermo: epistula.

periclitatio.definition: perīclitātiō ōnis, f periclitor, a trial, experiment : utilitates periclitatione percipere.

periculosus.definition: perīculōsus adj. with comp. and sup. periculum, dangerous, hazardous, perilous : consuetudo: iter: volnera: alea, H.: populo R. periculosum, Cs.: cum novorum fidem experiri periculosum duceret, S.: periculosum est, wi…

peridoneus.definition: per-idōneus adj., very suitable, well adapted: locus peridoneus castris, Cs.

perimo.definition: perimō or peremō ēmī, ēmptus or ēmtus, ere per+emo, to take away entirely, annihilate, extinguish, destroy, cut off, hinder, prevent : sin autem (supremus ille dies) peremit ac delet omnino: luna subito perempta est, …

perincommode.definition: perincommodē adv. perincommodus, very inconveniently, most unfortunately : accidit.

perinvisus.definition: per-invīsus adj., much hated, very odious.
