peritus.definition: perītus adj. with comp. and sup. 1 PAR-, experienced, practised, trained, skilled, skilful, expert : imperator: homines usu: Iber, H.: homo peritissimus in eis rebus: peritissimi duces, Cs.: multarum rerum: prodigioru…

periucunde.definition: per-iūcundē adv., very agreeably, most pleasantly: in hac suavitate versari: fuit enim periucunde, in the best humor.

periucundus.definition: per-iūcundus adj., very agreeable, most acceptable: alcui litterae: disputatio.—In tmesi: id mihi pergratum perque iucundum erit.

periurium.definition: periūrium ī, n periurus, a false oath, perjury : Caecinam periurio laedere: sceleratorum hominum: luimus periuria Troiae, V.: periuria dictare, Iu.: nihil periuria curant, Ct.

periurus.definition: periūrus (pēiū-) adj. with sup. per+ius, oath-breaking, false to vows, perjured : quid inter periurum et mendacem?: periurissimus leno: Troia, V.: fides, H.: Pelops, Ct.

perlabor.definition: per-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to slip through, glide over: in aedem foribus perlapsi angues, L.: Ad nos vix famae perlabitur aura, V.: inde perlapsus ad nos Hercules.

perlaetus.definition: per-laetus adj., very joyful: supplicatio, L.

perlate.definition: per-lātē adv., very widely: id (verbum) patet, is extremely broad.

perlateo.definition: per-lateō uī, —, ēre, to remain hidden, O.

perlego.definition: per-legō or pellegō lēgī, lēctus, ere, to view all over, examine thoroughly, scan, survey: omnia oculis, V.: dispositas per atria ceras, O.—To read through, peruse: perlectis litteris, S.: perlectam (epistulam), recit…

perlevis.definition: per-levis e, adj., very slight, trifling: perlevi momento fortunae pendēre, C., L.

perleviter.definition: per-leviter adv. perlevis, very lightly : commotus: pungit animi dolor.

perliberalis.definition: per-līberālis e, adj., very well bred, T.

perliberaliter.definition: per-līberāliter adv. perliberalis, with extreme courtesy, like a perfect gentleman : dicere: agere.

perlito.definition: per-litō āvī, ātus, āre, to offer sacrifices till favorable omens appear: bove, L.: primis hostiis perlitatum est, i. e. the first victims yielded favorable auspices, L.: diu non perlitatum tenuerat dictatorem, the lo…

perlonge.definition: perlongē adv. perlongus, a long way off , T.

perlubens.definition: per-lubēns or per-libēns entis, adj., very glad: me perlubente, to my great delight.

perlubenter.definition: per-lubenter adv. perlibens, very willingly, with great pleasure .

perluceo.definition: per-lūceō (pell-) lūxī, —, ēre, to shine through, glimmer: perlucens iam aliquid lux, i. e. in some measure piercing, L.: pelluces, i. e. you wear a transparent garment, Iu.— P. praes., transparent: perlucens aether: …

perlucidulus.definition: perlūcidulus (pell-) adj. dim. perlucidus, somewhat transparent : lapis, Ct.

perlucidus.definition: per-lūcidus (pellu-) adj. with comp, transparent, pellucid: pulvinus: membrana: fons, O.: Arcanique fides prodiga perlucidior vitro, H.— Extremely bright: stella.

perluo.definition: per-luō uī, ūtus, ere, to wash off, wash, bathe, lave: manūs puras undā, O.: perluitur solitā Titania lymphā, bathes, O.: in fluminibus perlui, Cs.

perlustro.definition: per-lūstrō āvī, ātus, āre, to go over, wander all through, traverse completely: hostium agros, L.—Fig., to view all over, examine, survey: materia perlustranda animo: omnia oculis, L.

permagnus.definition: per-māgnus adj., very great, vast, immense: hereditas: numerus, Cs.: tua res permagna agitur, interests: negotia, H.—As subst n., a very great thing: permagnum existimans (with acc. and infin.): permagni interest, it …

permaneo.definition: per-maneō mānsī, mānsūrus, ēre, to stay, hold out, last, continue, abide, be permanent, endure, remain, persist, persevere: ut quam maxime permaneant diuturna corpora: ira tam permansit diu, T.: quis confidit illud st…

permano.definition: per-mānō āvī, —, āre. to flow to, penetrate, reach: sucus permanat ad iecur: (venenum) in omnis partīs corporis.—Fig., to penetrate, reach, extend to: ne ad patrem hoc permanet, reach the ears of, T.: macula permanat …

permansio.definition: permānsiō ōnis, f per+1 MAN-, a remaining, abiding : quodvis supplicium levius est hac permansione, than abiding here.— A persistence : in unā sententiā: in ratione.

permarinus.definition: per-marīnus adj., escorting through the sea: Lares, guardian gods of voyagers, L.

permaturesco.definition: per-mātūrēscō ruī, —, ere, inch, to ripen fully: pomum, ubi permaturuit, O.

permediocris.definition: per-mediocris e, adj., very moderate: motus.

permeo.definition: per-meō —, —, āre, to go over, pass through, cross, traverse: maria ac terras, O.: longius in hostes, Ta.— Fig., to penetrate, pervade: (intellegentia) per omnia.

permetior.definition: per-mētior mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure through, measure out, measure: solis magnitudinem: permenso tempore lucis, i. e. at the end of life, Tb.—To traverse: classibus aequor, V.

permingo.definition: per-mingō mīnxī, —, ere, to make water upon, abuse, H.

permirus.definition: per-mīrus adj., very wonderful, amazing: illud vero mihi permirum accidit, fuisse, etc.—In tmesi: per mihi mirum visum est.

permisceo.definition: per-misceō miscuī, mīxtus, ēre, to mix together, mix thoroughly, commingle, intermingle: equites pedites permixti, S.: naturam cum materiā: permixti cum suis fugientibus, Cs.: permixtum senatui populi concilium, L.: g…

permissio.definition: permissiō ōnis, f permitto, a yielding, surrender at discretion : extra civium corpora, L.— Leave, permission : mea permissio mansionis tuae.

permissus1.definition: permissus P. of permitto.—As subst n., a permission: utor permisso, H.

permissus2.definition: (permissus, ūs) m per+MIT-, leave, permission ; only abl: permissu legis: Lentuli, L.

permitto.definition: per-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to let pass, let go, let loose: equos in hostem, i. e. ride at full speed, L.—To let go, reach with, cast, hurl: saxum in hostem, O.—Fig., to let loose, let go: tribunatum, exercise withou…

permixte.definition: permīxtē or permīxtim adv. permixtus, confusedly, promiscuously : dicere.

permixtio.definition: permīxtiō ōnis, f per+MIC-, a mixing together, mixture , C.— A confusion, disturbance : terrae, S.

permodestus.definition: per-modestus adj., very modest, extremely shy: homo: verba sensu permodesto, moderate, Ta.

permoleste.definition: permolestē adv. permolestus, with much trouble : alqd fero, am much vexed .

permolo.definition: per-molō —, —, ere, to grind thoroughly: uxores, H.

permotio.definition: per-mōtiō ōnis, f per+1 MV-, a moving, exciting, excitement : mentis: permotionis causā, to stir the feelings.—An emotion : permotiones animis datae.

permoveo.definition: per-moveō mōvī, mōtus, ēre, to move deeply, rouse, excite, agitate, influence, lead, induce, prevail on: quem res tanta non permovet, S.: maxime hac re permovebantur, quod, etc., were most influenced, Cs.: ne animo pe…

permulceo.definition: per-mulceō mulsī, mulsus, ēre, to rub gently, stroke: manu eum, O.: barbam, L.—To touch gently: aram flatu permulcet spiritus austri, blows softly upon, C. poët.: medicata lumina virgā, O.— Fig., to soothe, charm, ple…

permulto.definition: permultō adv. abl n. of permultus, very much, by far : clariora.

permultum.definition: permultum adv. permultus, very much, very far : permultum interest, utrum, etc.: permultum ante, very often before .

permultus.definition: per-multus adj., very much, very many: imitatores: colles, Cs.—As subst n.: permultum erit ex maerore tuo diminutum: permulta rogatus Fecit, H.

permunio.definition: per-mūniō īvī, ītus, īre, to finish fortifying, fortify thoroughly: quae munimenta incohaverat, L.: castris permunitis, L.

permutatio.definition: permūtātiō ōnis, f permuto, a change, alteration, revolution, crisis : magna rerum: temporum.— An interchanging, barter, exchange : captivorum, L.: mercium, Ta.: quae (pecunia) mihi ex publicā permutatione debetur, a …

permuto.definition: per-mūtō āvī, ātus, āre, to change throughout, alter completely: omnem rei p. statum.—To interchange, exchange: captivos, L.: galeam, V.: valle Sabinā divitias, H.—Of money, to exchange, pay by bill of exchange: illud…

perna.definition: perna ae, f , pe/rna, a haunch, ham with the leg, gammon: fumosa cum pede, H.

pernecessarius.definition: per-necessārius adj., very necessary, pressing: tempus.— Very closely connected, very intimate: amicus: homo mihi.—As subst m.: Leptae nostri: paternus.

pernecesse.definition: per-necesse adj. indecl, very necessary, indispensable: cum pernecesse esset.

pernego.definition: per-negō āvī, —, āre, to deny stoutly: alqd, T.: saepe appellati, pernegaverunt.

perniciabilis.definition: perniciābilis e, adj. pernicies, destructive, ruinous : nix oculis, Cu.: morbi, L.

pernicies.definition: perniciēs (not-tiēs), acc. em (gen. once iī, C.; dat. once iē, L., once iī, N.), f per+1 NEC-, destruction, death, ruin, overthrow, disaster, calamity, mischief : instructa ad perniciem, T.: senatoribus perniciem mach…

perniciose.definition: perniciōsē adv. with comp. perniciosus, destructively, ruinously, perniciously : multa perniciose sciscuntur in populis: perniciosius mereri.

perniciosus.definition: perniciōsus adj. with comp. and sup. pernicies, destructive, ruinous, baleful, pernicious : lubido, S.: flamma: leges, Cs.: scripta auctori perniciosa suo, O.: morbi perniciosiores: Obsequium ventris mihi perniciosius…

pernicitas.definition: pernīcitās ātis, f pernix, nimbleness, briskness, agility, swiftness : electi (milites) ad pernicitatem, Cs.: adde pernicitatem: pedum, L.

perniciter.definition: pernīciter adv. pernix, nimbly, swiftly : desilire, L.: exsilire, Ct.

pernimium.definition: per-nimium adv., quite too much, far too much: nimium inter vos, pernimium interest, T. —In tmesi: per parce nimium, T.

pernix.definition: pernīx īcis, adj. per+CNI-, persistent, persevering : iacet (taurus) instrato saxa cubili, V.— Nimble, brisk, active, agile, quick, swift, fleet : corpora exercitatione, L.: virgo pernicibus ignea plantis, V.: puella,…

pernobilis.definition: per-nōbilis e, adj., very famous: epigramma.

pernocto.definition: per-noctō āvī, ātūrus, āre, to stay all night, pass the night: foris, T.: ibi: extra moenia, L.: pro me pernoctet epistula tecum, O.: haec studia pernoctant nobiscum.

pernosco.definition: per-nōscō nōvī, nōtus, ere, to examine thoroughly: pernoscite, Furtumne factum existimetis, T.— To learn thoroughly, become fully acquainted with: non satis alqm, T.: rem cognoscite, Ut pernoscatis, etc., T.: motūs an…

pernotesco.definition: pernōtēscō tuī, ere, inch, to become generally known: ubi incolumem esse pernotuit, Ta.

pernotus.definition: per-nōtus adj., thoroughly known, well known: pugil regi, Cu.

pernox.definition: per-nox noctis, adj., through the night, all night: (bos) iacet pernox instrato cubili, V. (al. pernix): luna, full, L.: lunā pernocte, by the full moon, O.: luditur alea pernox, Iu.

pernumero.definition: per-numerō āvī, ātus, āre, to count out, reckon up: pecuniam, L.

pero.definition: pērō ōnis, m a long laced boot of raw hide (for soldiers and wagoners), V., Iu.

perobscurus.definition: per-obscūrus adj., very obscure: quaestio: fama, L.

perofficiose.definition: per-officiōsē adv., very serviceably, with devotion: me observare.

peropportune.definition: per-opportūnē adv. peropportunus, very seasonably, most opportunely : venire: cum te fortuna attulisset: bellum sumere, L.

peropportunus.definition: per-opportūnus adj., very seasonable, most opportune: diversorium: victoria, L.

peroptato.definition: per-optātō adv. optatus, exactly as desired : peroptato nobis datum est.

peropus.definition: per-opus adv., very necessary: peropus est, hunc cum ipsā loqui, T.

peroratio.definition: perōrātiō ōnis, f peroro, a summing up, peroration : eius.

perornatus.definition: per-ōrnātus adj., highly ornate: in dicendo.

perorno.definition: per-ōrnō āvi, —, āre, to adorn constantly: senatum, Ta.

peroro.definition: per-ōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to speak from beginning to end, plead throughout, harangue at length: a Quinto causa est Sesti perorata: breviter peroratum esse, L.: In Proculas, Iu.—To end, close, conclude, finish: strepitu …

perosus.definition: perōsus P. dep. per-odi, detesting, hating greatly, weary of, disgusted with : lucem, V.: genus omne Femineum, V.: Creten, O.: superbiam regis, L.: decemvirorum scelera, L.

perpaco.definition: per-pācō —, ātus, āre, to quiet completely, pacify thoroughly: omnibus perpacatis, L.

perparvolus.definition: per-parvolus (-vulus) adj. dim, very little, very small: signum: sigilla.

perparvus.definition: per-parvus (-vos) adj., very little, trifling, minute: navigium: culpa.—As subst n.: perparvum ex illis lucris.

perpastus.definition: per-pāstus adj., well fed: canis, Ph.

perpauci.definition: per-paucī ōrum, adj., very few: homo Perpaucorum hominum, i. e. select in his associates, T.: patres, L.—In tmesi: per pol quam paucos reperias amatores, T.—As subst n.: perpauca dicam: perpauca loquens, H.

perpauculi.definition: per-pauculī ōrum, adj. dim, very few: deduxit in Academiam perpauculis passibus.

perpaulum.definition: per-paulum adv., a very little: declinare.

perpaulus.definition: per-paulus adj., very little.—As subst n., a very little: loci.

perpauper.definition: per-pauper eris, adj., very poor: rex.

perpello.definition: per-pellō pulī, —, ere, to drive, urge, force, compel, constrain, prevail upon: ad deditionem, L.: orare, usque adeo, donec perpulit, carried his point, T.: Aulum spe pactionis, ut, etc., S.: decemviros, ut, etc., L.:…

perpendiculum.definition: perpendiculum ī, n perpendo, a plummet, plumb-line : ad perpendiculum columnas exigere, set by plummet : ad perpendiculum, perpendicularly : non directe ad perpendiculum, sed prone, Cs.

perpendo.definition: per-pendō pendī, —, ere, to weigh carefully, examine, ponder, consider: momenta officiorum: amicitia, quae tota veritate perpenditur, is valued altogether according to its truth.

perperam.definition: perperam adv. 1 PAR-, wrongly, incorrectly, untruly, falsely : istoc de nomine dixi, i. e. gave a false name , T.: facere: interpretari, L.

perpessio.definition: perpessiō ōnis, f perpetior, a bearing, suffering, endurance : harum rerum: laborum.

perpetior.definition: perpetior pessus, ī, dep. per+patior, to bear steadfastly, suffer firmly, stand out, abide, endure, be patient : contumelias, T.: inperia saeva, S.: o multa dictu gravia, perpessu aspera: supplicium, Cs.: mihi omnia p…

perpetro.definition: per-petrō āvī, ātus, āre per+patro, to carry through, complete, effect, achieve, execute, perform, accomplish, commit, perpetrate : ut Ilenses munere solverentur, Ta.—Usu. P. pass. : suo labore perpetratum, ne, etc., …

perpetuitas.definition: perpetuitās ātis, f perpetuus, uninterrupted duration, continuous succession, continuity, perpetuity : philosophi spectandi sunt ex perpetuitate atque constantiā, i. e. general tenor and system : ad perpetuitatem, for…

perpetuo1.definition: perpetuō adv. perpetuus, constantly, uninterruptedly, forever : hanc habere, T.: in vallo permanere, Cs.: loquens: virens buxum, O.

perpetuo2.definition: perpetuō —, —, āre perpetuus, to cause to continue, perpetuate : verba, talk without pausing : iudicum potestas perpetuanda.

perpetuus.definition: per-petuus adj. per+1 PAT-, continuous, unbroken, uninterrupted, constant, entire, whole, perpetual : agmen: vigiliaeque stationesque, a continuous line of , etc., Cs.: Perpetuis soliti patres considere mensis, V.: in…

perplaceo.definition: per-placeō —, —, ēre, to please greatly: ea (lex) mihi perplacet.

perplexe.definition: perplexē adv. perplexus, confusedly, ambiguously : mecum loqui, T.: indicare, L.

perplexus.definition: per-plexus adj. with comp, interwoven, entangled, involved, intricate: iter silvae, V.: carmen perplexius, L.—Fig., intricate, unintelligible, ambiguous, obscure, inscrutable: sermones, L.: responsum, L.—As subst n., …

perpolio.definition: per-poliō īvī, ītus, īre, to polish thoroughly, finish, make perfect: opus: ea, quae habes instituta: perpoliendi labor.

perpolitus.definition: perpolītus adj. P. of perpolio, thoroughly polished, refined : explicatio: omnibus iis artibus: vita humanitate.

perpopulor.definition: per-populor ātus, āre, dep., to lay waste utterly, devastate, pillage completely: Italiam, L.: perpopulato agro, L.: homines, Ta.

perpotatio.definition: perpōtātiō ōnis, f perpoto, a drinking-bout : intemperantissimae perpotationes.

perpoto.definition: per-pōtō āvī, —, āre, to keep drinking, tipple, carouse: totos dies: ad vesperum: perpotandi dulcedo, Cu.

perprimo.definition: perprimō —, —, ere per+premo, to press hard, press perpetually : cubilia, lie upon , H.

perpropinquus.definition: per-propinquus adj., very near: commutatio rerum, Att. ap. C.—As subst m., a very near relation: Auri.

perpulcher.definition: per-pulcher (-cer) chra, chrum, adj., very beautiful: dona, T.

perpurgo.definition: per-pūrgō (old perpūrigō) ā vī, ātus, āre, to cleanse thoroughly, purge: se quādam herbulā.— Fig., to clear up, explain: locus orationis perpurgatus ab iis: de dote tanto magis, arrange.

perpusillus.definition: per-pusillus adj., very small, very little: perpusillum rogabo (in a double sense adj. or adv. ), I will ask very little, or, the very little man.

perquam.definition: per-quam or per quam adv., as much as possible, extremely, exceedingly, T.: perquam grave est dictu: pauci, L.: breviter: per pol quam paucos reperias, T.

perquiro.definition: perquīrō —, quīsītus, ere per+quaero, to ask diligently after, make eager search for : vasa: vias in Suevos, Cs.: raptam, O.: non perquiris, cui dixit Apronius?: cognitionem rei, investigate .

perquisite.definition: (perquīsītē) adv. perquisitus, accurately, critically .—Only comp: perquisitius conscribere.

perraro.definition: perrārō adv. perrarus, very seldom, hardly ever : accidit: haec alea fallit, H.

perreconditus.definition: per-reconditus adj., most abstruse: ratio consuetudinis.

perrepo.definition: per-rēpō —, —, ere, to crawl over: tellurem genibus, Tb.

perrepto.definition: per-rēptō āvī, —, āre, freq, to creep over, crawl through: usque omne oppidum, T.

perridicule.definition: perrīdiculē adv. perridiculus, very laughably, most absurdly : homines augurabantur.

perridiculus.definition: per-rīdiculus adj., very laughable, highly absurd: doctrina.

perrogatio.definition: perrogātiō ōnis, f perrogo, the enactment of a law : legis Maniliae.

perrogo.definition: per-rogō —, —, āre, to ask in succession, complete the roll-call: perrogari sententiae non potuere, the voting could not be finished, L.

perrumpo.definition: per-rumpō rūpī, ruptus, ere, to break through, force a way through, get across: per medios hostīs, Cs.: in vestibulum templi, L.: nec per castra perrumpi posse, L.: paludem, Cs.: perrumpitur concretus aër: bipenni Lim…

persaepe.definition: per-saepe adv., very often: quod persaepe fit, C., H.

persalutatio.definition: persalūtātiō ōnis, f persaluto, a general salutation, greeting of everybody .

persaluto.definition: per-salūtō āvī, ātus, āre, to salute in succession: omnīs: deos, Ph.: a toto exercitu persalutatus est, Cu.

persancte.definition: per-sānctē adv., very sacredly, most solemnly: deierare, T.

persapiens.definition: per-sapiēns entis, adj., very wise: homo.

perscindo.definition: per-scindō —, —, ere, to rend asunder, tear in pieces: omnia perscindente vento, L.

perscitus.definition: per-scītus adj., very clever, very fine.—In tmesi: Per ecastor scitus puer, T.: per mihi scitum videtur.

perscribo.definition: per-scrībō īpsī, īptus, ere, to write in full, write at length, write out: res gestas populi R., S.: de meis rebus ad Lollium: hoc perscriptum in monumentis reperietis, ut, etc.: a primordio urbis res populi R., L.: v…

perscriptio.definition: perscrīptiō ōnis, f perscribo, a writing down, entry, official record : perscriptionum et liturarum adversaria: illud senatūs consultum eā perscriptione est, ut, etc., i. e. of such a tenor.—A making over by writing, …

perscriptor.definition: perscrīptor ōris, m perscribo, a book-keeper, accountant : faenerationis.

perscrutor.definition: per-scrūtor ātus, ārī, dep., to search through, examine, scrutinize: castelli planitiem, S.: (canes) perscrutabantur omnia.—Fig., to examine into, investigate: rationem criminum.

perseco.definition: per-secō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut up, extirpate, cut out: id (vitium), L.: rerum naturas, lay bare: perseca et confice, cut away (obstacles).

persedeo.definition: per-sedeō (-sideō) —, —, ēre, to remain sitting, sit continuously: totā nocte in speculis, Cu.: in equo persedendo, L.

persegnis.definition: per-sēgnis e, adj., very sluggish: proelium, L.

persentio.definition: per-sentiō sī, —, īre, to feel deeply: pectore curas, V.—To apprehend clearly, perceive distinctly: eam tali peste teneri, V.

persentisco.definition: per-sentīscō —, —, intens, to perceive clearly, detect: id, T.: Quot res dedere, T.

persequor.definition: per-sequor cūtus or quūtus, ī, dep., to follow perseveringly, follow after, follow up, pursue: certum est persequi, T.: me in Asiam, T.: exercitum: Hortensium ipsius vestigiis: alcuius vestigia: te, V.: Hanc persecuta…

perseverans.definition: persevērāns antis, adj. with comp. P. of persevero, persevering, persistent : perseverantior caedendi, L.

perseveranter.definition: persevēranter adv. with comp. perseverans, perseveringly : tueri, L.: perseverantius saevire, L.

perseverantia.definition: persevērantia ae, f persevero, steadfastness, perseverance : eius nimia, obstinacy : sententiae tuae: nautarum, Cs.

persevero.definition: persevērō āvī, ātus, āre perseverus, to abide, adhere strictly, continue steadfastly, persist, persevere : (navis) perseveravit, kept on its course , Cs.: in suā sententiā: in vitiis: in eo, ius publicano non dicere: …

perseverus.definition: per-sevērus adj., very strict: imperium, Ta.

persido.definition: per-sīdō sēdī, —, ere, to sink down, penetrate: Altius ad vivum, V.

persigno.definition: per-sīgnō —, —, āre, to register accurately, record: triumviri donis persignandis, L.

persimilis.definition: per-similis e, adj., very like, precisely similar: statua istius: isti tabulae liber, H.

persimplex.definition: per-simplex icis, adj., very simple: victus, Ta.

persisto.definition: per-sistō —, —, ere, to abide, persist: in impudentiā, L.—(For perf. system see persto).

persolvo.definition: per-solvō solvī, solūtus, ere, to unravel, solve, explain: hoc mihi.—To pay, pay out, pay over: pretium tibi, T.: pecuniam a discipulis suis Fufiis, pay by a draft on, etc.: (aes alienum) alienis nominibus suis copiis…

persona.definition: persōna ae, f per+SON-, a mask, false face (usu. of clay or bark, covering the head; worn by actors): tragica, Ph.: pallens, Iu.: mulier videtur, Non persona loqui, i. e. no man disguised , Iu.— An assumed character, …

personatus.definition: persōnātus adj. persona, in a mask, masked : Roscius: pater, i. e. in the play , H.—Fig.: cur personatus ambulem, in an assumed character .

postmodo.definition: post-modo or post modo adv., afterwards, after a while, a little later: Me esse . . . post modo rescisces, T.: inmeritis nocitura Postmodo te natis fraus, H.: publicum in praesentiā dedecus, postmodo periculum, L.

postmodum.definition: postmodum adv. post+modus, after a while, a little later : flecti precibus, L.

postpono.definition: post-pōnō posuī, positus, ere, to put after, esteem less, neglect, disregard: ut omnia postponere videretur, Cs.: scorto Officium, H.: vos natis suis, O.: omnibus rebus postpositis, laying aside everything, Cs.

postputo.definition: post-putō āvī, —, āre, to regard as secondary, disregard: omnīs res prae parente, T.

postquam.definition: post-quam or post quam conj, after that, after, as soon as, when : postquam convenere, S.: postquam Caesar pervenit, obsides poposcit, Cs.: post quam armis disceptari coeptum est: undecimo die postquam a te discessera…

postremo.definition: postrēmō adv. abl. of postremus; sc. tempore, at last, finally, last of all : inprimis . . . postremo, Cs.: agri, regna denique, postremo etiam vectigalia: primo . . . deinde . . . postremo, S.

postremum.definition: postrēmum adv. postremus, for the last time, last of all, at last : hodie postremum me vides, T.: eo die, quo postremum visus erat: Illum Postremum expellet heres, H.

postridie.definition: postrīdiē adv. i. e. posteri die, on the day after, the next day : postridie constituunt proficisci, Cs.: mane descendit: quid causae fuerit, postridie intellexi, quam discessi: postridie eius diei mane, Cs.—With acc,…

postscribo.definition: post-scrībō scrīpsī, —, ere, to add in writing: Tiberi nomen suo, Ta.

postulatio.definition: postulātiō ōnis, f postulo, a requiring, demand, request, desire : aequa et honesta: concessit senatus postulationi tuae: opinione valentior.— A complaint, expostulation : neque lites ullae inter eas, postulatio Numqu…

postulatum.definition: postulātum ī, n P. n. of postulo, a demand, request, claim : hoc de statuis: ut remittantur postulata per litteras: sua quoque ad eum postulata deferre, Cs.: cognitis suis postulatis, Cs.: postulata facere, N.: perage…

postulatus.definition: (postulātus, ūs) m postulo, a claim, suit, complaint : postulatu audito, etc., L.

postulo.definition: postulō āvī, ātus, āre PREC-, to ask, demand, claim, require, request, desire : incipiunt postulare, minari: nemo inventus est tam impudens qui postularet ut venderet: postulavere plerique, ut proponeret, etc., S.: su…

postumus.definition: postumus (posthu-) adj. sup. posterus.— Only of children, last, latest-born, late-born : mortuo postumo filio: tua postuma proles, son of your old age , V.

potens.definition: potēns entis (gen plur. potentum, V.), adj. with comp. and sup. P. of possum, able, mighty, strong, powerful, potent : animus, S.: familiae, L.: contra potentiorem auxili egere, Cs.: potentissimus civis: Roma opibus, …

potentatus.definition: potentātus ūs, m potens, might, power, rule, dominion : cum ad eum potentatus omnis recidisset: de potentatu contendere, Cs.: aemulo potentatūs inimicus, L.

potenter.definition: potenter adv. with comp. potens, strongly, mightily, vigorously : perrumpere saxa potentius Ictu fulmineo, H.: cui lecta potenter erit res, who has made a masterly choice , H.

potentia.definition: potentia ae, f potens, might, force, power : armorum tenendorum, L.: solis Acrior, V.: morbi, O.: occulti miranda fati, Iu.: Nate, mea magna potentia solus, i. e. source of my power , V.— Efficacy, virtue : herbarum, …

potestas.definition: potestās ātis, f potis.—Of persons, ability, power, capacity, force : in se potestatem habere tantae astutiae, such a power of craftiness , T.: aut potestas defuit aut facultas.—Of things, efficacy, force, virtue : po…

potio.definition: pōtiō ōnis, f PO-, a drinking : in mediā potione exclamavit.— A drink, draught, potion : contemptissimis escis et potionibus: cum potione sitis depulsa est.— A poisonous draught, potion, philter : potione mulierem sus…

potior1.definition: potior (potitur, T., V., O.; poterētur, Ct.; poterēmur, O.; poterentur, L., O.), ītus, īrī (potī, Enn. ap. C.), dep. potis, to become master of, take possession of, get, obtain, acquire, receive : libidines ad potiund…

potis.definition: potis or pote adj. indecl. with comp. potior, potius, and sup. potissimus POT-. I. Posit, able, capable (with es or est ): Potin ut desinas (sc. es)? Can you stop? T.: dum potis (es), aridum Compone lignum, H.: At non…

potissimum.definition: potissimum (-sumum) adv. sup. potis, chiefly, principally, especially, eminently, above all : Quem vocabo ad cenam Potissimum? T.: exsistat aliquis et potissimum Caecus ille: te potissimum hoc persequi oporteret: quid…

potius.definition: potius adv. comp. potis, rather, preferable, more : sed scin', quid volo potius facias? T.: nec vero imperia expetenda, ac potius non accipienda interdum: Galliam potius esse Ariovisti quam populi R., Cs.: si domus ha…

poto.definition: pōtō āvī, ātus (pōtūrus, Tb., Pr.), āre potus, to drink : potaturus est apud me, T.: si potare velit: aquam, Iu.: poturi (Tantali) deserit unda sitim, Tb.: poturas ire iubebat oves, Pr.—Of things, to drink up, suck in…

potor.definition: pōtor ōris, m PO-, a drinker : aquae potores, H.: Rhodani, i. e. dweller by the Rhone , H.— A drunkard, sot, toper : potores Falerni, H.

potrix.definition: pōtrīx īcis, f potor, a female tippler , Ph.

potulentus.definition: pōtulentus (pōcul-) adj. potus, drinkable. — Plur. n . as subst, drinkables, drinks : esculenta et potulenta.

potus1.definition: pōtus adj. P. pass. of bibo, drunk, drunk up : sanguine tauri poto: poti faece tenus cadi, drained , H.— That has drunk, drunken, intoxicated : domum bene potus redire: anus, H.

potus2.definition: pōtus ūs, m PO-, a drinking : immoderato extumefacta potu: potui esse, Ta.— A drink, draught : refectus potu, Cu.: cibi potūsque, Ta.

prae1.definition: prae adv. PRO-, before, in front : i prae, sequor, go on before , T.

prae2.definition: prae praep. with abl. 1 prae, before, in front of, in advance of : si huic aliquid paulum prae manu Dederis, at hand , i. e. ready money , T.: singulos prae se inermos mittere, S.: stillantem prae se pugionem tulit: p…

praeacutus.definition: prae-acūtus adj., sharp in front, sharpened, pointed: cacumina, Cs.: sudes, S.: cuspis, O.

praealtus.definition: prae-altus adj., very high: rupes, L.: mons, L.— Very deep: flumen, L.: proxima terrae praealta sunt, S.

praebeo.definition: praebeō uī, itus, ēre prae+habeo, to hold forth, reach out, proffer, offer, tender : os ad contumeliam, submit to open insult , L.: eis os tuum: collum cultris, Iu.: aurīs adulescentium conviciis, give ear , L.— To gi…

praebibo.definition: prae-bibō bibī, —, ere, to drink before, drink to: alcui venenum.

praebitor.definition: praebitor ōris, m praebeo, a furnisher : Minister et praebitor, an official purveyor .

praecalidus.definition: prae-calidus adj., very warm, hot: potio, Ta.

praecaveo.definition: prae-caveō cāvī, cautus, ēre, to take care, take heed, use precaution, be on one's guard, beware: mihi, to look out for myself, T.: ad praecavendum intellegendi astutia: ab insidiis, guard against, L.: vel ex supervac…

praecedo.definition: prae-cēdō cessī, cessus, ere, to go before, precede, lead the way, lead: cum coronis aureis (in a procession), L.: praecedebat ipse vinctus, L.: fama loquax praecessit ad aures, Deïanira, tuas, O.: is praecedens agmen…

praecellens.definition: praecellēns entis, adj. with sup. P. of praecello, superior, excellent, eminent, distinguished : vir virtute: vir omnibus rebus praecellentissimus.

praecello.definition: praecellō —, —, ere 2 CEL-, to surpass, excel : alqm fecunditate, Ta.: per nobilitatem, Ta.: genti, to rule over , Ta.

praecelsus.definition: prae-celsus adj., lofty, towering: rupes, V.

praecentio.definition: praecentiō ōnis, f prae+1 CAN-, a musical prelude .

praecento.definition: praecentō —, —, āre prae+canto, to utter incantations before : huic.

praeceps1.definition: praeceps cipitis, abl. cipitī, adj. prae+ caput, headforemost, headlong : praecipitem (me) in pistrinum dabit, T.: ut Sopatrum praecipitem deiciant: praeceps ad terram datus, dashed to the ground , L.: Desilit, O.: se…

praeceps2.definition: praeceps adv. 1 praeceps, headlong : vim mortalium praeceps trahit, Ta.

praeceptio.definition: praeceptiō ōnis, f prae+CAP-, a previous notion, preconception : ad eam praeceptionem accedere, quam, etc.— A precept, injunction : lex est recti praeceptio.

praeceptor.definition: praeceptor ōris, m prae+CAP-, a teacher, instructor, preceptor : vivendi atque dicendi: fortitudinis: philosophiae, N.: Aeacidae, O.

praeceptrix.definition: praeceptrīx īcis, f praeceptor, a preceptress : quā (sapientiā) praeceptrice.

praeceptum.definition: praeceptum ī, n P. n. of praecipio, a maxim, rule, precept, order, direction, command, injunction : praeceptorum plenus istorum, T.: praecepto ab iis observato, Cs.: sine praecepto ullius suā sponte struebatur acies, …

praecerpo.definition: praecerpō —, —, ere prae+carpo, to pluck beforehand, gather prematurely : messīs, O.—Fig., to take away, lessen, diminish : fructum offici tui.

praecido.definition: praecīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere prae+caedo, to cut off in front, cut off : caput praecisum ducis, L.: resistenti manum gladio: collegae sui praecidi caput iussit: ancoras, cut the cables.— To cut through, cut up : cotem nov…

praecingo.definition: prae-cingō nxī, nctus, ere, to gird, encircle, enclose: cautus praecingitur ense viator, girds himself, O.: praecincti recte pueri, properly girded, H.: altius ac nos Praecincti, i. e. more rapid travellers, H.: fonte…

praecino.definition: praecinō cinuī, —, ere prae+cano.—Of musicians, to make music before, play at : sacrificiis, L.: carmine cum magico praecinuisset anus, i. e. had uttered an incantation , Tb.— Of musical instruments, to make music bef…

praecipio.definition: praecipiō cēpī, ceptus, ere prae+capio, to take beforehand, get in advance : ab publicanis pecuniam insequentis anni mutuam praeceperat, had borrowed in advance , Cs.: aliquantum viae, get something of a start , L.: P…

praecipito.definition: praecipitō āvī, ātus, āre praeceps, to throw headlong, cast down, hurl down, precipitate : p<*>ae in mare praecipitatae, N.: currum scopulis, hurl against , O.: se ex altissimo muro: sese in fossas, Cs.: se (sc. de mu…

praecipue.definition: praecipuē adv. praecipuus, chiefly, principally, eminently : de consularibus disputare: civitati indulgere, Cs.: sanus, H.: sedulitas stulte urget, Praecipue cum, etc., especially , H.

praecipuus.definition: praecipuus adj. prae+CAP-, taken before others, particular, peculiar, especial : hanc rem habere praeter alios praecipuam, this special distinction , T.: non praecipuam, sed parem cum ceteris fortunae condicionem subi…

praecise.definition: praecīsē adv. praecisus, in short, in few words, briefly, concisely : dici.— Positively, absolutely : negare.

praecisus.definition: praecīsus adj. P. of praecidio, broken off, abrupt, precipitous : praecisis saxis, V.: iter, S.— Fig., of speech, abrupt .

praeclare.definition: praeclārē adv. with sup. praeclarus, very clearly, very plainly : intellego: memini.— Excellently, admirably, gloriously : praeclare nobiscum actum iri, si, etc.: se res habebat: simulacrum factum e marmore: nihil nis…

praeclarus.definition: prae-clārus adj. with comp. and sup, very bright, brilliant : iaspis, Iu.—Very beautiful, magnificent, honorable, splendid, admirable, remarkable, distinguished, excellent, famous: urbs situ praeclaro ad aspectum: opu…

praecludo.definition: praeclūdō sī, sus, ere prae+claudo, to shut off, shut, close : portas consuli, Cs.: fores, Pr.— To close, forbid access to : orbem terrarum civibus: maritimos cursūs praecludebat hiemis magnitudo. — To shut off, hinde…

praeco.definition: praecō ōnis, m prae+VOC-, a crier, herald : citat praeco legatos: praetoris.— A crier, auctioneer : si palam praeco praedicasset, dimidias venire partīs: haec per pracconem vendidit, by auction : fundum subiecit praec…

praecogito.definition: prae-cōgitō —, ātus, āre, to ponder beforehand, premeditate: praecogitatum facinus, L.

praecolo.definition: prae-colō —, cultus, ere, to cultivate beforehand.— Fig.: animi habitūs, ad virtutem quasi praeculti.—To embrace prematurely: nova et ancipitia, Ta.

praecompositus.definition: prae-compositus adj., arranged beforehand, studied: praecomposito ore, O.

praeconium.definition: praecōnium ī, n neut. of praeconius, the office of a public crier : facere.— A crying out in public, proclaiming, publishing : tibi praeconium deferam: praeconia famae, O.— A celebrating, laudation, commendation : ab …

praeconius.definition: praecōnius adj. praeco, of a public crier : quaestus, the business of a public crier .

praeconrumpo.definition: prae-conrumpō (-corrumpō) —, ruptus, ere, to corrupt beforehand, bribe in advance: donis me, O.: Illa venit, sed praeconrupta, Quae, etc., O.

praeconsumo.definition: prae-cōnsūmō —, sūmptus, ere, to waste in advance, spend beforehand: suas virīs bello, O.

praecontrecto.definition: prae-contrectō —, —, āre, to handle beforehand: videndo, i. e. survey, O.

praecordia.definition: praecordia ōrum, n prae+cor, the muscle which parts the chest from the abdomen, midriff, diaphragm : subter praecordia: praecordia pressit senis, i. e. stopped his breath , Iu.— The entrails, stomach : anulus in praec…

praecurro.definition: prae-currō cucurrī (rarely currī), —, ere, to run before, hasten on before, precede: propere, T.: ad Persea, L.: ante omnīs, Cs.: Barros equis albis, i. e. surpass, H.—Fig., to go before, precede, anticipate: eo fama …

praecursio.definition: praecursiō ōnis, f prae+1 CEL-, a going before : sine praecursione visorum, the previous occurrence of phenomena .—In rhet., a preparation of the hearer .

praecursor.definition: praecursor ōris, m prae+1 CEL-, a forerunner, advanced guard, vanguard , L.— A scout, spy .

praecutio.definition: praecutiō —, —, ere prae+quatio, to shake before, brandish in front : taedas, O.

praeda.definition: praeda ae, f prae+HED-, property taken in war, booty, spoil, plunder, pillage : praedam manubias in urbis ornamenta conferre: urbis praedā adducti: praedam militibus donare, Cs.: victores praedā spoliisque potiti, V.:…

praedabundus.definition: praedābundus adj. praedor, ravaging, pillaging, plundering : dicit se praedabundum eodem venturum, S.: exercitus, L.

praedamno.definition: prae-damnō —, ātus, āre, to condemn beforehand: praedamnatus conlega, L.—Fig., to give up in advance: spem, L.

praedatio.definition: praedātiō ōnis, f praedor, a taking of booty, pillaging : regnum praedationibus augere, Ta.

praedator.definition: praedātor ōris, m praedor, a plunderer, pillager : quos in eodem genere praedatorum pono: exercitus, praedator ex sociis, S.: aprorum, a hunter , O.— An avaricious man , Tb.

praedatorius.definition: praedātōrius adj. praedator, plundering, predatory : manus (militum), marauders , S.: naves, pirate-ships , L.

praedelasso.definition: prae-dēlassō —, —, āre, to weary out beforehand: incursūs quae (moles) praedelassat aquarum, O.

praedestino.definition: prae-dēstinō —, —, āre, to set before as a goal, predestine: sibi triumphos, L.

praediator.definition: praediātor ōris, m praedium, a purchaser of mortgaged estates at auction, dealer in real property .

praediatorius.definition: praediātōrius adj. praediator, of mortgaged land : ius, the law of mortgages .

praedicabilis.definition: praedicābilis e, adj. 1 praedico, praiseworthy, laudable : ali<*>uid.

praedicatio.definition: praedicātiō ōnis, f 1 praedico, a public proclamation, publication by a crier : luctuosa et acerba: tribuni, L.— A praising, praise, commendation : clementia omnium praedicatione decoranda.

praedicator.definition: praedicātor ōris, m 1 praedico, a public praiser, eulogist : benefici.

praedico1.definition: prae-dicō āvī, ātus, āre, to make known by proclamation, announce, publish, proclaim: de quo homine praeconis vox praedicat: palam dimidias venire partīs.—To make known, announce, proclaim, herald, relate, declare ope…

praedico2.definition: prae-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to say before, premise: hoc primum tibi, T.: haec eo mihi praedicenda fuerunt, ut, etc.—To foretell, predict, forebode: defectiones solis: nihil adversi accidit non praedicente me, that I …

praedictio.definition: praedictiō ōnis, f prae+DIC-, a foretelling, prediction : mali: vatum.

praedictum.definition: praedictum ī, n P. neut. of 2 praedico, something previously said : velut ex predicto, as if by preconcert , L.— A foretelling, prediction, prophecy : Chaldaeorum praedicta: vatium.— An order, command : dictatoris, ne…

praediolum.definition: praediolum ī, n dim. praedium, a small estate .

praedisco.definition: prae-discō —, —, ere, to learn beforehand: ea quae agenda sunt: Ventos, V.

praedispositus.definition: prae-dispositus P., arranged beforehand, distributed in advance: nuntii, L. (dub.).

praeditus.definition: praeditus adj. prae+datus, gifted, provided, possessed, furnished : parvis opibus: mundus animo: singulari inmanitate: simulacrum summā religione, i. e. held in high reverence .

praedium.definition: praedium ī, n prae+HED-, a farm, estate, manor : praedibus et praediis populo cautum est: habet in urbanis praediis, city lots : fructus praediorum: rusticum, L.: gnatis dividere, H.

praedives.definition: prae-dīves itis, adj., very rich, affluent: Perseus, L., Iu.: praedivite cornu Autumnus, O.

praedo.definition: praedō ōnis, m praeda, one that makes booty, a plunderer, robber : urbes praedonibus patefactae: praedones latronesque, Cs.: maritimus, a pirate , N.: perfidus, V.: digna praedone marito, i. e. who had stolen her , O.…

praedoctus.definition: prae-doctus P., instructed in advance: ab duce, S.

praedor.definition: praedor ātus, ārī praeda, to make booty, plunder, spoil, rob : spes praedandi: licentia praedandi, L.: praedantes milites, Cs.: classis pluribus locis praedata, Ta.: in re frumentariā: omnibus in rebus, upon every opp…

praeduco.definition: prae-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to draw out before, construct in front: fossas viis, Cs.: murum, Cs.: castris fossam, Tb.

praedulcis.definition: prae-dulcis e, adj., very pleasing, delightful: decus, V.

praedurus.definition: prae-dūrus adj., very hard, hardened: corium, Ta.— Very strong: homo viribus, V.: corpora, V.: tempora, O.

praeeo.definition: prae-eō iī (īvī), —, īre, to go before, lead the way, precede: ut consulibus lictores praeirent: praeeunte carinā, V.: novi praeeunt fasces, O.— Fig., to go before, precede: naturā praeeunte.— To recite beforehand, di…

praefatio.definition: praefātiō ōnis, f praefor, a preliminary form of words, formula of announcement : donationis: sacrorum, L.

praefectura.definition: praefectūra ae, f praefectus, the office of an overseer, overseership, superintendence : domūs, Iu.— The office of governor in a province, provincial deputyship, prefecture : praefecturas sumere: multorum consulum pra…

praefectus.definition: praefectus ī, m P. of praeficio, an overseer , director, superintendent : morum, N.: nec vero mulieribus praefectus praeponatur: annonae, L.: praefecti libidinum suarum.—In public life, a president, superintendent, co…

praefero.definition: prae-ferō tulī, lātus, ferre, to bear before, carry in front, hold forth: dextrā facem: in fascibus insignia laureae, Cs.: fasces praetoribus praeferuntur: praelatos hostīs adoriri, as they rode by, L.: signa militari…

praeferox.definition: prae-ferōx ōcis, adj., very violent, impetuous, insolent: animus, L.: ingenio, Ta.

praefervidus.definition: prae-fervidus adj., very hot: balneum, Ta. — Fierce: ira, L.

praefestino.definition: prae-fēstīnō —, ātus, āre, to hasten before, be precipitate: deficere, L.—To pass in haste: sinum, Ta.

praeficio.definition: praeficiō fēcī, fectus, ere prae+facio, to set over, place in authority over, place at the head, appoint to command : alquem Asiae: imperatorem bello: his (legionibus) legatos, Cs.: pontifices sacris: te lucis Avernis…

praefidens.definition: prae-fīdēns entis, adj., too trustful, over-confident: te praefidentem tibi Repriment legum habenae, C. poët.: homines sibi.

praefigo.definition: prae-fīgō fīxī, fīxus, ere, to fasten before, set up in front, affix: ripa sudibus praefixis munita, Cs.: arma puppibus, V.—To tip, head, point: asseres cuspidibus praefixi, Cs.: iacula praefixa ferro, L.: ferro praef…

praefinio.definition: prae-fīniō īvī, ītus, īre, to determine beforehand, ordain, prescribe: praefinire non est meum: dies in lege praefinita: tibi, quo minus, etc.: praefinisti, quo ne, etc.

praefinito.definition: praefīnītō adv. P. abl. n. of praefinio, in the prescribed manner : loqui, T.

praefloro.definition: praeflōrō —, ātus, āre prae+flos, to deflower beforehand, lessen, tarnish : gloria eius victoriae praeflorata, L.

praefluo.definition: prae-fluō —, —, ere, to flow along, flow by: infimā valle, L.: provinciam, Ta.: regna Dauni, H.

praefoco.definition: praefōcō —, —, āre prae+faux, to choke, strangle, suffocate : animae viam, O.

praefodio.definition: prae-fodiō fōdī, —, ere, to dig in front of: portas, V.—To bury in advance: aurum, O.

praefor.definition: (prae-for) fātus, ārī, dep., to say beforehand, utter in advance, premise, preface: in parte operis mei licet mihi praefari, quod, etc., L.: quae de deorum naturā praefati sumus, etc.: arcana se et silenda adferre pra…

praefracte.definition: praefrāctē adv. praefractus, inflexibly, resolutely : aerarium defendere.

praefractus.definition: praefrāctus adj. with comp. P. of praefingo. —Of style, rude, abrupt : Thucydides praefactior. —Of character, unyielding : Aristo.

praefrigidus.definition: prae-frīgidus adj., very cold: Auster, O.

praefringo.definition: praefringō frēgī, frāctus, ere prae+frango, to break off before, break to pieces, shiver : hastas, L.: praefracto rostro (triremis), Cs.

praefulcio.definition: prae-fulciō —, —, īre, to prop up, support.— Fig.: illud praefulci, ut, etc., make sure.

praefulgeo.definition: prae-fulgeō —, —, ēre, to beam forth, shine greatly, glitter in front: praefulgebat huic triumphus, L.: Nitor smaragdi collo praefulget tuo (sc. pavonis), Ph.: equus praefulgens unguibus aureis, V.: triumphali decore,…

praegelidus.definition: prae-gelidus adj., very cold: Alpes, L.

praegestio.definition: prae-gestiō —, —, īre, to desire greatly, delight: videre: Ludere, H.: apisci, Ct.

praegracilis.definition: prae-gracilis e, adj., very slender: proceritas, Ta.

praegravis.definition: prae-gravis e, adj., very heavy: onus, O.: corpore, L.: vino, Ta.: delatores, very wearisome, Ta.: principi, Ta.

praegravo.definition: prae-gravō —, ātus, āre, to press heavily upon, oppress with weight, encumber: exonerare praegravante turbā regnum, L.: praegravata telis scuta, burdened, L.—Fig., to burden, oppress, weigh down: dantem et accipientem…

praegredior.definition: praegredior gressus, ī, dep. prae+gradior, to go before, go in advance, precede : alios praegredientes: nuntios, L.— To pass by, pass : ea (castra), L.

praegressio.definition: praegressiō ōnis, f prae+GRAD-, a going before, preceding : stellarum.—Fig., precedence : causae.

praegressus2.definition: praegressus ūs praegredior, an advance : rerum praegressū s, i. e. steps in development .

praegustator.definition: praegustātor ōris, m praegusto, a foretaster, cup-bearer .—Fig.: libidinum tuarum.

praegusto.definition: prae-gustō āvī, —, āre, to taste beforehand: oleas, L.: cibos, O.: medicamina (i. e. antidota), Iu.

praeiaceo.definition: prae-iaceō —, ēre, to lie before: campus, qui castra praeiacet, Ta.

praeiudicatus.definition: praeiūdicātus adj. P. of praeiudico, decided beforehand, prejudged : praeiudicatum eventum belli habetis, L.: opinio, prejudice .—As subst n. : id ipsum pro praeiudicato ferre, as already decided , L.: ut ne quid huc …

praeiudicium.definition: prae-iūdicium ī, n a preceding judgment, anticipatory sentence, previous decision, precedent: his duobus praeiudiciis damnatus: neminem praeiudicium rei tantae adferre, i. e. anticipate the judgment (of the Senate), L…

praeiudico.definition: prae-iūdicō āvī, ātus, āre, to prejudge, decide beforehand: de hoc (homine): de iis censores praeiudicent, give preliminary judgment (before the case is heard by the judges).

praeiuvo.definition: prae-iuvō iūvī, —, āre, to aid before: adfec, tam eius fidem, Ta.

praelabor.definition: prae-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to glide before, move by, float past: piscis praelabitur ante, C. poët.: rotis flumina, glide by the streams on wheels, V.

praelambo.definition: prae-lambō —, —, ere, to lick beforehand. (mus) praelambens omne, quod adfert, H.

praelego.definition: prae-legō —, —, ere, to sail by, skirt: Campaniam, Ta.: oram, Ta.

praeligo.definition: prae-ligō —, ātus, āre, to bind on before, bind to: fasces praeligantur cornibus, L.—To bind up, tie up: os praeligatum.

praelongus.definition: prae-longus adj., very long: gladii, L.: hasta, Ta.

praeluceo.definition: prae-lūceō lūxī, —, ēre, to shine before, shed light upon: ne ignis noster facinori praeluceat, Ph.—Fig., to shine before, light up: (amicitia) bonam spem praelucet in posterum, lights up hope. —To outshine, surpass: …

praelustris.definition: praelūstris e, adj., very illustrious, magnificent: arx, O.—Plur n. as subst: praelustria vita, avoid grandeur, O.

praemandata.definition: praemandāta ōrum, n P. of prae-mando, a warrant of arrest : praemandatis requisitus.

praematurus.definition: prae-mātūrus adj., too early, untimely, premature: hiems, Ta.: exitus, Ta.: cineres, Iu.

praemedicatus.definition: prae-medicātus adj., protected by medicines, charmed: Aesonides, O.

praemeditatio.definition: praemeditātiō ōnis, f praemeditor, a considering beforehand, premeditation : futurorum malorum: diuturna.

praemeditor.definition: prae-meditor ātus, ārī, dep., to think over beforehand, consider in advance, premeditate: nihil, ne bellum haberent, L.: id ferundum modice esse: quo animo accedam: quae renuntiarent, L.: mala praemeditata: tentans ci…

praemetuens.definition: prae-metuēns adj. P. of praemetuo, apprehensive : doli, Ph. (al. dolum).

praemetuo.definition: prae-metuō —, —, ere, to fear beforehand, be apprehensive: suis, Cs.: coniugis iras, V.

praemineo.definition: praemineō (prae-ēm-) —, —, ēre, to transcend, excel: ceteros peritiā legum, Ta.

praemitto.definition: prae-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to send forward, despatch in advance: legiones in Hispaniam, Cs.: legatum ad flumen, S.: odiosas litteras: ad Boios, qui doceant, etc., Cs.: cum sese Italicam venturum praemisisset, had s…

praemium.definition: praemium ī, n prae+EM-, an advantage, prerogative, favor, license, privilege : licebat legis praemio, by the special favor of the law : Frontis urbanae praemia, the license of city assurance , H. — A reward, recompens…

praemolior.definition: prae-mōlior —, īrī, dep., to prepare beforehand: praemoliendam sibi ratus rem, L.

praemoneo.definition: prae-moneō uī, itus, ēre, to forewarn, admonish beforehand: me, ut magnopere caverem: Praemoneo, numquam scripta modesta legat, O.: conatūs hostis, warn of, L.—To foretell, predict, prophesy, presage: ferunt audita co…

praemonitus.definition: praemonitus ūs, m praemoneo, a forewarning, premonition : Praemonitūs deūm, O.

praemonstrator.definition: praemōnstrātor ōris, m praemonstro, one who points out the way, a guide , T.

praemonstro.definition: prae-mōnstrō —, —, āre, to predict, presage, prognosticate: magnum aliquid populo R.: ventos futuros, C. poët.

praemordeo.definition: prae-mordeō —, —, ēre, to bite off, snip off: ex hoc alqd, Iu.

praemorior.definition: prae-morior tuus, ī, dep., to die prematurely, O.

praemortuus.definition: prae-mortuus adj., prematurely dead: iacuere, velut praemortua, membra, O.—Fig.: praemortui esse pudoris, i. e. to have lost shame, L.

praemunio.definition: prae-mūniō īvī, ītus, īre, to fortify in front: aditūs magnis operibus, Cs.: non praemunito vallo, L.—Fig., to fortify, protect, secure: genus (dicendi) praemunitum: ut ante praemuniat, prepare his defences (of an ora…

praemunitio.definition: praemūnītiō ōnis, f praemunio, a fortifying beforehand, preparation : orationis.

praenarro.definition: prae-nārrō āvī, —, āre, to tell beforehand: rem, T.

praenato.definition: prae-natō —, —, āre, to swim before, flow by: domos praenatat amnis, V.

praeniteo.definition: prae-niteō uī, —, ēre, to shine in preference, be more attractive: cur tibi iunior praeniteat, H.

praenomen.definition: prae-nōmen inis, n the first name, praenomen, personal name (e. g. Marcus, usu. written M.): filius, cui Marco praenomen erat, L.: sine praenomine familiariter ad me epistulam misisti.

praenosco.definition: prae-nōscō —, —, ere, to learn beforehand, foreknow: futura: promissum sibi caelum, O.

praenotio.definition: praenōtiō ōnis, f prae+GNA-, a preconception, innate idea : deorum.

praenubilus.definition: prae-nūbilus adj., very cloudy, gloomy: arbore lucus, O.

praenuntia.definition: prae-nūntia ae, f a harbinger, foreteller: belli, O.: stellae calamitatum praenuntiae.

praenuntio.definition: prae-nūntiō (not-nūnciō), —, ātus, āre, to announce beforehand, foretell, predict: hanc venturam (esse), T.: futura: de eorum adventu, N.

praenuntius.definition: prae-nūntius (not-nūncius), ī, m a foreteller, harbinger, omen: lucis ales, i. e. the cock, O.

praeoccupatio.definition: praeoccupātiō ōnis, f praeoccupo, a seizing beforehand, preoccupation : locorum, N.

praeoccupo.definition: prae-occupō āvī, ātus, āre, to seize upon beforehand, preoccupy: Macedoniam, N.: opportuna loca, L.: praeoccupatum sese legatione ab Cn. Pompeio, Cs.—Fig., to seize in advance, preoccupy: animos timor praeoccupaverat,…

praeopto.definition: prae-optō āvī, ātus, āre, to choose rather, desire more, prefer: exsilio modicam domi fortunam, L.: suas leges Romanae civitati, L.: nemo non illos sibi quam vos dominos praeoptet, L.: immerito quam iure violari, Cu.:…

praepando.definition: prae-pandō —, —, ere, to spread out, extend. —Fig.: hibernos temporis ortūs, C. poët.

praeparatio.definition: praeparātiō ōnis, f praeparo, a making ready, preparation : diligens: animi ad minuendum dolorem.

praeparatus.definition: prae-parātus adj. P. of praeparo, prepared, provided, furnished, ready : praeparatos quodam cultu proficisci ad dormiendum: bene Pectus, H.: aures: oratio, L.—As subst n. : ex ante praeparato sustentari, from the stor…

praeparo.definition: prae-parō āvī, ātus, āre, to make ready beforehand, prepare, equip, make preparations: ea quae videntur instare: ante navīs, L.: locum domestici belli causā , Cs.: praeparato ad talem casum perfugio, L.: pecunia stipe…

praepedio.definition: praepediō īvī, ītus, īre prae+pes, to entangle, shackle, fetter : praepeditis Numidarum equis, Ta.— To hinder, embarrass, obstruct, impede : sese praedā, hamper themselves , L.: omnī s (bonas artīs) avaritia praepedie…

praependeo.definition: prae-pendeō —, —, ēre, to hang before, hang down in front: ubi tegumenta praependere possent ad, etc., Cs.: praependent sertae, Pr.

praepes.definition: praepes petis, abl. pete or petī, gen plur. petum, adj. prae+PET-, outstripping ; hence, in augury, significant in flight, of good omen, favorable (of birds of good augury): praepes Laeva volavit avis, Enn. ap. C.: pr…

praepilatus.definition: praepilātus adj. 3 pila, tipped with a ball, carrying a button : missilia, i. e. blunied , L.

praepinguis.definition: prae-pinguis e, adj., very fat, of superior fertility: solum, V.

praepollens.definition: prae-pollēns entis, adj., eminent, superior, excellent: gens divitiis, L.: vir virtute, L.

praepolleo.definition: prae-polleō luī, —, ere, to surpass in power: quibus additis praepollebat, Ta.: mari, Ta.

praepondero.definition: prae-ponderō —, —, āre, to make heavier, regard as superior: praeponderari honestate.

praepono.definition: prae-pōnō posuī, positus, ere, to place in front, put upon, affix: aedibus vestibula: fronti olivam, i. e. crown, H.—To put before, place first: versūs in primā fronte libelli, O.: ultima primis, H.: pauca praeponam, …

praeporto.definition: prae-portō —, —, āre, to bear before, C. poët.

praepositio.definition: praepositiō ōnis, f praepositus, a setting before, prefixing : negationis.—In grammar, a prefix .—Fig., a preferring, preference .

praepositus1.definition: praepositus adj. P. of praepono, preferable, preferred .—As subst n., that which is desirable (opp. both to the absolete good, and to evil).

praepositus2.definition: praepositus ī, m P. of praepono, a prefect, president, chief : legatorum tuorum.

praepostere.definition: praeposterē adv. praeposterus, in reverse order, out of order : litteras reddere: tecum agere.

praeposterus.definition: prae-posterus adj., in reverse order, in disorder, inverted, perverted, absurd, preposterous, unseasonable: quid tam praeposterum dici potest?: gratulatio: consilia.—Of persons, perverse, unreasonable, absurd: semper:…

praepotens.definition: prae-potēns entis, adj., very able, excelling in power, superior: viri: rerum omnium Iuppiter: terrā marique Karthago: armis Romanus, L.— Plur m. as subst: opes praepotentium.

praepropere.definition: praeproperē adv. praeproperus, in extreme haste, headlong : festinans, L.: agendo, L.

praeproperus.definition: prae-properus adj., too hasty, sudden, precipitate: festinatio: celeritas, L.: ingenium, rash, L.

praeputium.definition: prae-pūtium ī, n 3 PV-, the foreskin, prepuce : praeputia ponere, Iu.

praequeror.definition: (prae-queror) questus, ī, to complain beforehand: multa praequestus, O.

praeradio.definition: prae-radiō —, —, āre, to outshine: stellis signa minora suis, O.

praerapidus.definition: prae-rapidus adj., very swift, exceedingly rapid: gurges, L.: fluminum celeritas, Cu.

praerigesco.definition: prae-rigēscō uī, ere, inch, to become very stiff: praereguisse manūs, Ta.

praeripio.definition: praeripiō ripuī, reptus, ere prae+rapio, to snatch away, carry off : arma Minervae, O.: aliis laudem.— To seize prematurely : deorum beneficium festinatione, i. e. presume upon.—To forestall, anticipate : hostium cons…

praerodo.definition: prae-rōdō —, sus, ere, to gnaw off, nibble: praeroso hamo, i. e. the bait, H.

praerogativus.definition: praerogātīvus adj. prae-rogo, to ask first, voting first, asked before others : centuria, which cast the first vote in the comitia (originally the century of the equites, afterwards that which obtained the right by lo…

praerumpo.definition: prae-rumpō —, ruptus, ere, to break off before, tear away in front: retinacula classis, O.: funes praerumpebantur, were broken off, Cs.

praeruptus.definition: praeruptus adj. P. of praerumpo, broken off, steep, abrupt, rugged : saxa: iugum, Cs.: nemus, H.: mons, V.—Fig., hasty, rash, precipitate : audacia: iuvenis animo, Ta.

praes.definition: praes praedis, m prae+vas, a surety, bondsman : praedes pecuniae publicae accipere: praedes dare: per praedem agere: praedibus acceptis aedificia perfecturi, L.: cavere populo praedibus ac praediis, to procure securit…

praesaepe.definition: praesaepe (praesēpe) is, n prae+saepes, an enclosure, stable, stall, fold, pen : Stabant (equi) in praesaepibus altis, V.: bona donavit praesaepibus, has spent his substance on his stables , Iu.: fucos a praesaepibus …

praesaepio.definition: prae-saepiō (-sēpiō) psī, ptus, īre, to fence in front, block up, barricade: aditūs trabibus, Cs.: omni aditu praesaepto, Cs.

praesagio.definition: praesāgiō īvī, —, īre praesagium, to feel in advance, perceive beforehand, have a presentiment, forebode : nescio quid mi animus praesagit mali, T.: quasi praesagiret: hoc ipsum animo, L.

praesagitio.definition: praesāgītiō ōnis, f praesagio, a presentiment, foreboding, faculty of divining, prophetic power : in animis.

praesagium.definition: praesāgium ī, n 1 SAC-, a presentiment, foreboding, presage : vatum praesagia, O.: mentis, O.

praesagus.definition: prae-sāgus adj., perceiving beforehand, divining, prophetic, presaging: pectora, O.: mali mens, V.: luctū s suspiria, O.—Prophetic, indicating beforehand: Verba senis, O.: fulminis ignes, V.

praescio.definition: prae-sciō īvī, —, īre, to know beforehand, foreknow: ante, T.

praescisco.definition: prae-scīscō —, —, ere, to learn beforehand: animos volgi longe, V.: quam quisque provinciam haberet, L.

praescius.definition: prae-scius adj., foreknowing, prescient: corda, V.: lingua, O.: vates venturi, V.

praescribo.definition: prae-scrībō īpsī (scrīpstī, T.), īptus, ere, to write before, prefix in writing: sibi nomen, V.: auctoritates praescriptae, the names of senators recorded as voting.—To describe beforehand: formam futuri principatūs, …

praescriptio.definition: praescrīptiō ōnis, f prae+SCARP-, a prefix in writing, title, inscription, preface, introduction : legis.—Fig., a pretext, excuse, pretence : honesta praescriptione rem tegere, Cs.— A limit, restriction, proviso : rat…

praescriptum.definition: praescrīptum ī, n P. n. of praescribo, a previous direction, precept, limitation, proviso, regulation : legum imperio et praescripto fieri: omnia agere ad praescriptum, Cs.: ad praescriptum consulis comitia habita, L.…

praeseco.definition: prae-secō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut off before, cut away, cut off, cut out: praesectis mulierum crinibus, Cs.: partem, O.—Fig.: Praesectum deciens non castigavit ad unguem, i. e. accurately, H. (al. perfectum).

praesens.definition: praesēns entis (abl. of persons usu. ente; of things, entī), adj. with comp. P. of praesum, at hand, in sight, present, in person : quia ades praesens, because you are here , T.: quo praesente, in whose presence : pau…

praesensio.definition: praesēnsiō ōnis, f prae+SENT-, a foreboding, presentiment : per exta inventa.— A preconception .

praesentia.definition: praesentia ae, f praesens, a being at hand, presence : eorum praesentiam vitare: (Nemea) celebrare praesentiā suā , L.: urget praesentia Turni, V.: animi, presence of mind , Cs.: deorum praesentiae.— Impression, effic…

praesentio.definition: prae-sentiō sēnsī, sēnsus, īre, to feel beforehand, perceive in advance, have a presentiment of, presage, divine: animo, Cs.: animus ita praesentit in posterum, ut, etc.: amorem, O.: dolos, V.: ibi me adesse, T.: tale…

praesertim.definition: praesertim adv. 1 SER-, especially, chiefly, principally, particularly : praesertim ut nunc sunt mores, etc., T.: retinenda est verecundia, praesertim naturā ipsā magistrā: praesertim homines tantulae staturae, Cs.: (…

praeses.definition: praeses idis, m and f SED-, a protector, guard, guardian, defender : tribunus, quem maiores praesidem libertatis esse voluerunt: Praeside tuta deo, O.— A superintendent, chief, president : belli, i. e. Minerva , V.: q…

praesidens.definition: praesidēns entis, m P. of praesideo, a president, ruler : superbia praesidentium, Ta.

praesideo.definition: praesideō sēdī, —, ēre prae+sedeo, to guard, watch, protect, defend : huic urbi, atque huic rei p.: alii, ut urbi praesiderent, relicti, L.— To preside over, manage, superintend, direct, command : ad portas urbanis re…

praesidiarius.definition: praesidiārius adj. praesidium, serving for defence : milites, in garrison , L.

praesidium.definition: praesidium ī, n praeses, defence, protection, guardianship, help, aid, assistance : proficisci praesidio suis, N.: amicitiam populi R. sibi praesidio esse oportere, Cs.: tectus praesidio firmo amicorum: Ut meae stulti…

praesignifico.definition: prae-sīgnificō —, —, āre, to indicate beforehand: hominibus quae sint futura.

praesignis.definition: prae-sīgnis e, adj. prae+signum, pre-eminent, distinguished : tempora cornu, O.: facie, O.

praesono.definition: prae-sonō uī, —, āre, to sound before: praesonuit sollemni tibia cantu, O.

praestabilis.definition: prae-stābilis e, adj. with comp, pre-eminent, distinguished, excellent: res magnitudine: dignitas praestabilior: fuerat praestabilius, preferable, T.: nihil amicitiā praestabilius: neque aliud praestabilius invenies, S.

praestans.definition: praestāns antis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of 2 praesto, pre-eminent, superior, excellent, distinguished, extraordinary : omnibus et ingenio et diligentiā, surpassing all : usu et sapientiā , for experience and wisd…

praestantia.definition: praestantia ae, f praestans, pre-eminence, superiority, excellence : animantium reliquarum, over other creatures : di omnium rerum praestantiā excellentes, in all things .

praestes.definition: praestes itis, m 2 prae+STA-, a protector, guardian : praestitibus Laribus, O.

praestigiae.definition: praestīgiāe ārum, f STIG-, deceptions, illusions, sleights, jugglery, trickery : verborum, tricks of words : quasi praestigiis depelli: non per praestigias, sed palam compilare, secretly : quo magis argui praestigias …

praestituo.definition: praestituō uī, ūtus, ere prae+statuo, to determine beforehand, fix in advance, prescribe : tibi quidemst olim dies praestituta, T.: diem praestituit operi faciundo: die praestitutā , L.: nullā praestitutā die, without…

praesto1.definition: praestō adv. for * praesito, P. abl. of * prae-sino, at hand, ready, present, here : Ipsum praesto video, T.: domi Praesto apud me esse, T.: togulae lictoribus ad portam praesto fuerunt: praesto est enim acerba memori…

praesto2.definition: prae-stō itī, itus (P. fut. praestatūrus), ā re, to stand out, stand before, be superior, excel, surpass, exceed, be excellent: suos inter aequalīs: civitas hominum multitudine praestabat, Cs.: sacro, quod praestat, p…

praestolor.definition: praestōlor ātus, ārī, dep. 1 STAR-, to stand ready for, wait for, expect : ad Clupeam, Cs.: tibi ad Forum Aurelium: quem praestolare? T.

praestringo.definition: prae-stringō inxī, ictus, ere, to draw together, fasten up, bind fast, compress: Syracosio (laqueo) praestrictā fauce, O.—Fig., of the sight, to make dull, blunt, dim, dazzle: oculos: fulguribus praestringentibus acie…

praestruo.definition: prae-struō ūxī, ūctus, ere, to build before, block, stop up, make impassable, make inaccessible: aditum obice montis, O.: Porta Fonte fuit praestructa, stopped up, O.: Hospitis effugio omnia, against the escape, O.—Fi…

praesul.definition: praesul sulis, m 2 SAL-, a leader in a dance, leader of a procession .

praesultator.definition: praesultātor ōris, m praesulto, a leader in a dance, leader of the festal procession (of a slave flogged before a procession in the circus), L.

praesulto.definition: praesultō āre prae+salto, to dance before, swagger before : hostium signis, L.

praesum.definition: prae-sum fuī, esse, to be before, be set over, preside over, rule, have charge of, command, superintend: in provinciā, govern: omnibus Druidibus, Cs.: provinciae, S.: censor factus, severe praefuit ei potestati, N.: e…

praesumo.definition: prae-sūmō —, ūmptus, ere, to take before, take first: domi dapes, O.: remedia, Ta.—Fig., to anticipate, take for granted: spe bellum, i. e. anticipate victory by confidence, V.: praesumpta apud militem illius anni qui…

praesutus.definition: prae-sūtus P., sewed up: (hasta) foliis praesuta, i. e. covered, O.

praetego.definition: prae-tegō —, —, ere, to protect: cavo aere caput, Pr.

praetempto.definition: prae-temptō (-tentō) —, —, āre, to examine previously, make trial: baculo iter, O.: pedibus iter, Tb.: pollice chordas, O.: praetemptata crimina, experimental, Ta.— Fig., to test beforehand: sui vires, O.

praetendo.definition: prae-tendō dī, tus, ere, to stretch forth, reach out, extend, present: hastas dextris, V.: fumos manu, i. e. fumigate, V.: praetenta Tela, presented, O.: coniugis taedas, i. e. assume to be your husband, V.—To spread …

praetepesco.definition: prae-tepēscō uī, —, ere, to grow warm before.—Fig.: Si tuus praetepuisset amor, O.

praeter1.definition: praeter adv. PRO-, except, besides, unless, save, other than, not : ne quis praeter armatus violaretur, L.: multitudini diem statuit . . . praeter rerum capitalium condemnatis, S.: Nil praeter canna fuit, O.

praetervolo.definition: praeter-volō —, —, āre, to fly by, pass in flight: praetervolans corvus glaebam amisit, Cu.: (equum) praetervolat Ales.—In tmesi: Etrusca praeter et volate litora, H.—Fig., to slip by, escape: sententiae saepe hominum…

praetexo.definition: prae-texō xuī, xtus, ere, to weave before, fringe, edge, border: Purpura praetexit amictūs, O.: litora Praetexunt puppes, V.: nationes Rheno praetexuntur, border on the Rhine, Ta.—To border, furnish, provide, adorn: p…

praetinctus.definition: 'prae-tinctus P., steeped previously, moistened beforehand: semina veneno, O.'

praetor.definition: praetor ōris, m for * praeitor; prae+1 I-, a leader, head, chief, president, chief magistrate, chief executive, commander : se praetores appellari volebant (the chief magistrates of Capua): maximus, L.: creant praetor…

praetorianus.definition: praetōriānus adj. praetorium, of the bodyguard, praetorian : miles, Ta.

praetorium.definition: praetōrium ī, n praetor.—In a camp, the general's tent : tueri praetorium, L.: fit concursus in praetorium, Cs.—In a province, the governor's residence, government house : curritur ad praetorium.—Plur, a palace : sede…

praetorius.definition: praetōrius adj. praetor, of the praetor, of praetors, praetorian : ius, the praetor's decisions : comitia, the election of praetor , L.: potestas, the praetor's authority : turba, about the praetor .— As subst m., one…

praetrepidans.definition: prae-trepidāns antis, adj., very hasty, impatient: mens, Ct.

privatio.definition: prīvātiō ōnis, f privo, a taking away, privation : doloris.
