probo.definition: probō āvī, ātus, āre probus, to make good, esteem good, approve, esteem, commend : quis est, qui non probet: villam, L.: alqd in ipsis: Caesar maxime probat coactis navibus mare transire, Cs.: antequam civitas suffect…

probrosus.definition: probrōsus adj. probrum, shameful, ignominious, infamous : crimen: Italiae ruinae, H.: carmina, lampoons , Ta.

probrum.definition: probrum ī, n a shameful act, base deed: ignaviae luxuriaeque probra, S.: emergere ex paternis probris.— Immodesty, lewdness, unchastity: probri insimulare feminam.— Shame, disgrace, dishonor, infamy, degradation: Quin…

probus.definition: probus adj. with comp, estimable, good, serviceable, excellent, superior, upright, honest, honorable, virtuous: artifex, skilful, T.: mulier, T.: hoc homine probior esse: navigium: fruges.—As subst m.: probi oratio, a…

procacitas.definition: procācitās ātis, f procax, pertinacity, obtrusiveness, impudence : a procando nominata: hominis, N.

procaciter.definition: procāciter adv. with comp. and sup. procax, boldly, impudently, wantonly : ortus sermo, Cu.: flagitatum stipendium procacius quam, etc., L.: procacissime patris tui memoriae inludunt, Cu.

procax.definition: procāx ācis, adj. PREC-, pertinacious, bold, insolent, forward, pert, wanton : mulier: in lacessendo: sermo, S.: libertas, Ph.: Auster, V.

procedo.definition: prō-cēdō cessī, —, ere, to go before, go forward, advance, proceed, march on, move forward, go forth: in portum: nil procedere lintrem Sentimus, H.: pedibus aequis, O.: lente atque paulatim proceditur, Cs.: processum …

procella.definition: procella ae, f pro+1 CEL-, a violent wind, storm, hurricane, tempest : nimbi, procellae, turbines: stridens Aquilone, V.: si mugiat Africis Malus procellis, H.: raperent mea poma procellae, O.: procella nivem effudera…

procellosus.definition: procellōsus adj. procella, full of storms, stormy, tempestuous : ver, L.: Noti, i. e. bringing storms , O.

procer.definition: (procer, eris) m pro+2 CEL-, a nobleman, aristocrat : Agnosco procerem, Iu.—Plur, the leading men, chiefs, nobles, princes : audiebam nostros proceres clamitantes: Etruscorum, L.: delectos populi ad proceres, V.

procere.definition: (prōcērē) adv. procerus, extensively .—Only comp: bracchium procerius proiectum, stretched out farther .

proceritas.definition: prōcēritās ātis, f procerus, a high growth, height, tallness : huius, his tall stature : arborum. — Extent, length : pedum.

procerus.definition: prōcērus adj. with comp. and sup. pro+2 CEL-, high, tall, long : collum: (Galatea) procerior alno, O.: inter hos procerissimas pōpulos: lupi, large , H.— Long, extended : aves procero rostro: palmae, Ct.: anapaestus, …

processio.definition: prōcessiō ōnis, f pro+1 CAD-, a marching on, advance (opp. reditus): longior.

processus2.definition: prōcessus ūs, m pro+1 CAD-, an advance, course, progression, progress, process, movement : processum volt, the progress of the discourse : in processu coepit crudescere morbus, in its course , V.: tantos processūs eff…

procido.definition: prōcidō idī, —, ere pro+cado, to fall forward, fall down, fall prostrate : ad pedes Achilleï, H.: universi prociderunt, L.: cupressus Procidit late, H.

procinctus.definition: (prōcīnctus, ūs) m pro+2 CAN-, a girding up, readiness for battle .—Only abl sing. : in procinctu testamentum facere, on the battle-field : ex quo in procinctu testamenta perierunt, i. e. the custom of making wills on…

proclamator.definition: prōclāmātor ōris, m proclamo, a crier, bawler (of a bad advocate; dub.).

proclamo.definition: prō-clāmō āvī, ātus, āre, to call, cry out, vociferate: adsunt, defendunt, proclamant: magnā voce, V.: Quid non proclames, si, etc., Iu.: pro sordidis hominibus, in defence of, L.

proclino.definition: prō-clīnō āvī, ātus, āre, to bend forward, bend, incline: mare in haec litora, O.: adiuvat rem proclinatam, tottering, Cs.: proclinatā iam re, i. e. at the crisis, Cs. ap. C.

proclivi.definition: prōclīvī adv. with comp. proclivis, downward, headlong, precipitately : proclivi labuntur, rush downward : proclivi currit oratio: labi verba proclivius, i. e. more rapidly .

proclivis.definition: prōclīvis e, adj. with comp. pro + clivus, sloping, steep, going downward, downhill : per proclivem viam duci, L.: undae, Ct.— As subst n. : pelli per proclive, downhill , L.—Fig., downwards, descending, downhill, dec…

proclivitas.definition: prōclīvitās ātis, f proclivis, a tendency, predisposition, proneness : ad morbos.

proconsul.definition: prō-cōnsul is, m a governor of a province, military commander, proconsul (usu. sent out from Rome at the end of his term as consul): (Caelius) Pompeio proconsuli contubernalis: proconsules de provinciis Romam redierun…

proconsularis.definition: prōcōnsulāris e, adj. proconsul, of a proconsul, proconsular : salarium, Ta.: imago, of the military tribuneship , L.

proconsulatus.definition: prōcōnsulātus ūs, m proconsul, the office of a proconsul, proconsulate : ex proconsulatu Asiae, Ta.

procor.definition: procor —, ārī, dep. procus, to ask, demand : a procando procacitas nominata.

procrastinatio.definition: prōcrāstinatiō ōnis, f procrastino, a putting off from day to day, procrastination .

procrastino.definition: prōcrāstinō —, —, āre pro+crastinus, to put off till the morrow, defer, delay, procrastinate : rem: res non procrastinatur.

procreatio.definition: prōcreātiō ōnis, f procreo, a begetting, generation : liberorum: hominum.

procreator.definition: prōcreātor ōris, m procreo, a begetter, creator : mundi: a procreatoribus amari, by parents .

procreatrix.definition: prōcreātrīx īcis, f procreator, she that brings forth, a mother : philosophia artium.

procreo.definition: prō-creō āvī, ātus, āre, to bring forth, beget, generate, procreate, produce: fetūs: liberos ex uxoribus, N.: terra ex seminibus truncos procreat.— Fig., to produce, make, cause, occasion: (tribunatus) ortus inter arm…

procubo.definition: prō-cubō —, —, āre, to lie stretched out: ubi saxea procubet umbra, V.

procudo.definition: prō-cūdō dī, sus, ere, to fashion by hammering, forge: ensīs, H.: vomeris obtusi dentem, V. —Fig.: procudenda lingua est, to be fashioned.

procul.definition: procul adv. pro+1 CEL-, in the distance, at a distance, away, apart, far, afar off, from afar : Delos, tam procul a nobis posita: non procul, sed hic praesentes (di): ubi turrim constitui procul viderunt, Cs.: in pela…

proculco.definition: prōculcō āvī, ātus, āre pro+calco, to tread down, trample upon : eques sua ipse subsidia proculcavit, rode down , L.: proculcato senatu, Ta.: hunc ungula proculcat equorum, V.: segetes in herbā, O.: proculcatas (ranas…

procumbo.definition: prōcumbō cubuī, cubitum, ere CVB-, to fall forwards, sink down, fall prostrate : Gallis ad pedes<*> ne cogerentur, etc., Cs.: genibus, O.: in vestibulo curiae, L.: in genua, Cu.: Coroebus Penelei dextrā Procumbit, V.:…

procuratio.definition: prōcūrātiō ōnis, f procuro, a caring for, charge, superintendence, administration, management, procuration : rei p.: sua cuique procuratio est restituta: rerum humanarum: ministerii, L.— An expiatory sacrifice, expiat…

procurator.definition: prōcūrātor (once proc-, O.), ōris, m procuro, a manager, overseer, superintendent, agent, administrator, deputy, procurator, keeper : per procuratorem gerere: regni, viceroy , Cs.: Caesaris, deputy , Ta.: procurator n…

procuratrix.definition: prōcūrātrīx īcis, f procurator, a governess, protectress : sapientia hominis.

procuro.definition: prō-cūrō (proc-, O., Tb.), āvī, ātus, āre, to take care of, attend to, look after: in pecuniā maximā procurandā: corpora, V.: sacrificia, Cs.—Of an agent or trustee, to take care of, manage: negotia Dionysi, act as st…

procurro.definition: prō-currō cucurrī and currī, cursum, ere, to run forth, rush forward, charge: temere extra aciem, Cs.: ferocius, L.: ad repellendum hostem, Cs.: longius, to rush farther on, V.: ubi alterno procurrens gurgite pontus r…

procursatio.definition: prōcursātiō ōnis, f procurso, a sally, onset : per procursationem commissa pugna, L.

procursatores.definition: prō-cursātorēs ōris, m procurso, skirmishers, sharpshooters , L.

procurso.definition: prōcursō —, —, āre, freq. procurro, to keep up sallies, continue skirmishing : quid procursantes pauci tererent tempus, L.: cum ab stationibus procursaretur, L.

procursus.definition: prōcursus (ūs), m procurro, a running forth, running on : procursu concitus axis, whirled furiously onward , V.— A sally, onset : procursu militum, L.: Procursu rapido invadere, V.

procurvus.definition: prō-curvus adj., curved in front, crooked, winding: falx, V.: litora, V.

procus.definition: procus ī (gen plur. procūm, C.), m PREC-, a wooer, suitor : natam nulli veterum sociare procorum, V.: Penelope difficilis procis, H.: forma Multorum fuit spes procorum Illa, O.: impudentes proci, i. e. shameless canva…

prod-.definition: prōd- old form of pro, in prod-eo, prod-est.

prodeambulo.definition: prō-deambulō (Fleck.) or prōd-ambulō (Speng.), —, —, āre, to walk abroad, T.

prodeo.definition: prōd-eō iī, itus, īre, to go forth, come forth, come forward: pultat forīs: Anus prodit, T.: foras, to come out of doors: quae, si prodierit, audiet, shall appear as a witness: ex portu, Cs.: obviam de provinciā deced…

prodico.definition: prō-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to put off, defer, adjourn, fix in advance: prodictā die: diem, adjourn the trial, L.: prodicta dies est, an adjournment was had, L.

prodige.definition: prōdigē adv. prodigus, lavishly, extravagantly : vivere.

prodigentia.definition: prōdigentia ae, f prodigo, extravagance, profusion : opum, Ta.

prodigialiter.definition: prōdigiāliter adv. prodigium, unnaturally, extravagantly : variare rem, H.

prodigiosus.definition: prōdigiōsus adj. prodigium, unnatural, wonderful, marvellous, prodigious : atria Circes, O.: cura Veneris, O.: fides, Iu.

prodigium.definition: prōdigium ī, n prod-+3 AG-, a prophetic sign, token, omen, portent, prodigy : multa prodigia eius numen declarant: (lunam deficientem) nullum esse prodigium: non mihi iam furtum, sed monstrum ac prodigium videbatur, i…

prodigo.definition: prōdigō ēgī, —, ere prod-+ago, to squander, waste : sumptibus sua, Ta.

prodigus.definition: prōdigus adj. prod-+1 AG-, wasteful, lavish , prodigal (opp. liberalis): femina, Iu.: aeris, H.— As subst: largitor et prodigus, a spendthrift.— Rich, fertile : tellus, O.: locus herbae, H.—Fig., lavish, prodigal, pro…

proditio.definition: prōditiō ōnis, f pro + 1 DA-, a betrayal, treason, treachery : multorum in nos proditionem notabis: amicitiarum proditiones: per proditionem libertas amissa, L.: alcui proditionem agere, to contrive , Ta.

proditor.definition: prōditor ōris, m pro+1 DA-, a betrayer, traitor : pro ducibus proditores habere: disciplinae, L.: risus proditor latentis puellae, H.

prodo.definition: prō-dō didī, ditus, ere, to put forth, exhibit, reveal: Medusae squalentia ora, O.—To bring forth, produce, propagate: genus alto a sanguine Teucri, V.: Quae dies ut cesset prodere furem, Iu.— To put forth, relate, re…

prodoceo.definition: prō-doceō —, —, ēre, to teach openly, proclaim: haec Ianus summus ab imo Prodocet, H.

prodromos.definition: prodromos ī, m , pro/dromos, a forerunner, advance-messenger: Pompeiani.—Plur, a northnortheast wind that blows before the rising of the dog-star.

produco.definition: prō-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere (prō dūxe for prōdūxisse, T.), to lead forth, lead forward, bring out: eum rus hinc, T.: copias pro castris, Cs.—By legal process, to produce, bring forward, cause to appear: eum in conspect…

producte.definition: prōductē adv. productus, lengthened, long : dicere litteram (opp. breviter).

productio.definition: prōductiō ōnis, f pro+DVC-, a lengthening, prolonging : temporis: verbi.

producto.definition: prōductō —, —, āre, freq. produco, to throw before, interpose : huic malo moram, T. (dub.).

productus.definition: prōductus adj. with comp. P. of produco, lengthened, long, prolonged, protracted : commoditates corporis tam productae temporibus: productiora alia, too long : nomen, formed by prolongation : neu sit quinto productior…

proegmena.definition: proēgmena ōrum, n , prohgme/na, preferable things (in the Stoic philosophy).

proeliator.definition: proeliātor ōris, m proelior, a fighter, combatant , Ta.

proelior.definition: proelior ātus, ārī, dep. proelium, to join battle, engage in battle, fight : pedibus, Cs.: ad Syracusas: proelians interficitur, Cs.: vehementer proeliatus sum, contended (in court).

proelium.definition: proelium ī, n a battle, combat : non proeliis neque acie bellum gerere, S.: proelium facere, to engage: proelia inire, L.: redintegrare, Cs.: proeliis uti secundis: uno proelio confecta res: Punica passi proelia, the …

profano.definition: profānō āvī, ātus, āre profanus, to render unholy, desecrate, profane, violate : ut dies festi profanarentur, L.: festum, O.: pudorem, Cu.

profanus.definition: profānus adj. pro+fanum, out of the temple, not sacred, common, profane, unholy : loci: aedificia: flamma, O.: animalia, unclean , Ta.: sacra profanaque omnia spoliare: procul este, profani, ye uninitiated , V.: Cerer…

profectio.definition: profectiō ōnis, f pro+2 FAC-, a going away, setting out, departure : mea: profectionem parare, to prepare for setting out , Cs.: repentina in Oretanos, L.: pecuniae, i. e. source .

profecto.definition: profectō adv. pro+facto, actually, indeed, really, truly, assuredly, certainly : non est ita, iudices, non est profecto: negare.

profectus3.definition: prōfectus —, abl. ū, m pro+2 FAC-, advance, effect, increase, profit, success : sine profectu, O.: profectu carere, O.

profero.definition: prō-ferō tulī, lātus, ferre, to carry out, bring forth, produce: arma ex oppido, Cs.: (nummos) ex arcā .—To extend, stretch out, reach forth, put forth: digitum: pedem, advance freely, H.—To move on, set forward: sign…

professio.definition: professiō ōnis, f profiteor, a public acknowledgment, avowal, declaration, expression, profession, promise : pietatis, Ta.: postquam professionibus detecta est magnitudo aeris alieni, L.: in Leontino iugerūm.— A busin…

professorius.definition: professōrius adj. professor (late), of a public teacher : lingua, Ta.

professus.definition: professus adj. P. of profiteor, avowed, confessed : culpa, O.: mors, i. e. certain , Ph.

profestus.definition: pro-fēstus adj., non-festival, not a holiday, common: festis profestisque diebus, working-days, L.: luces, working-days, H.: lux, H.

proficio.definition: prōficiō fēcī, fectus, ere pro+facio, to make headway, advance, make progress, have success, profit, succeed, effect, accomplish : quid erat profectum, nisi ut, etc.: tantum profeci tum, ut, etc.: nihil in oppugnation…

proficiscor.definition: proficīscor fectus, ī, dep. proficio, to set forward, set out, start, go, march, depart : fortasse tu profectus alio fueras, were going somewhere else , T.: cum in Italiam proficisceretur, was about to start , Cs.: Ut…

profiteor.definition: profiteor fessus, ērī, dep. pro+fateor, to declare publicly, own freely, acknowledge, avow, confess openly, profess : non solum fateri, sed etiam profiteri: fateor atque etiam profiteor: apertissime studium suum: se n…

profligator.definition: prōflīgātor ōris, m profligo, a spendthrift, prodigal , Ta.

profligatus.definition: prōflīgātus adj. with sup. P. of profligo, wretched, vile, corrupt, abandoned : iudicia: tu omnium mortalium profligatissime: homines.

profligo.definition: prōflīgō āvī, ātus, āre 1 FLAG-, to strike to the ground, cast down utterly, overthrow, overcome, conquer : aciem hostium: classem hostium, Cs.: hostīs, N.—Fig., to overthrow, ruin, destroy, crush : rem p.: tantas ope…

proflo.definition: prō-flō āvī, —, āre, to blow forth, breathe out: flammas, O.—Fig.: pectore somnum, i. e. the heavy breathing of sleep, V.

profluens.definition: prōfluēns adj. P. of profluo, flowing along : aqua profluens.—As subst f . (sc. aqua), running water : in profluentem deferri.—Fig., of speech, flowing, fluent : genus sermonis: celeritas.

profluenter.definition: prōfluenter adv. profluens, flowingly : ergo omnia profluenter (adsint), i. e. in rich measure .

profluentia.definition: prōfluentia ae, f profluens, a flowing forth : loquendi, stream of words .

profluo.definition: prō-fluō fluxī, —, ere, to flow forth, flow along: Mosa profluit ex monte, Cs.: umor profluit, V.: sanguis profluens, Enn. ap. C.—Fig., to glide, proceed imperceptibly: ab his fontibus profluxi ad hominum famam: ad li…

profor.definition: pro-for ātus, ārī, dep., to speak out, say, speak: plura, H.: et sic accensa profatur, V.: quibus ille profatur; Forsitan, etc., O.

profugio.definition: pro-fugiō fūgī, —, ere, to flee, run away, escape: Cirtam, S.: ex oppido, Cs.: domo, L.: cum vi prope iustorum armorum profugisset: ex proelio in provinciam, S.: aliquo militatum, T.: agros, flee from, H.: dominos, Cu…

profugus.definition: profugus adj. pro+2 FVG-, that flees, fugitive, in flight : milites profugi discedunt, S.: domo, L.: currus, O.— Wandering, nomad : profugi Seythae, H.— Banished, exiled : Hannibal patriā, L.: Troiani, qui profugi inc…

profundo.definition: pro-fundō (prō-, Ct.), fūdī, fū sus, ere, to pour out, pour forth, shed copiously, cause to flow: sanguinem pro patriā: lacrimas oculis, V.: lacrimae se subito profuderunt, burst forth.— To bring forth, produce, utter…

profundum.definition: profundum ī, n profundus, a depth : esse in profundo (aquae): maris, O.— The depths of the sea, deep sea : ex profundo molem ad caelum erigit, Att. ap. C.: profundo Vela dabit, V.: genitor profundi, i. e. Neptune , O.…

profundus.definition: pro-fundus adj. with sup, deep, profound, vast: mare: pontus, V.: Danuvius, H.: fornax, O.: profundae altitudinis convalles, L.: profundissimus libidinum gurges.—Thick, dense: Erebi nox, V.: silvae, Cu.—High: caelum, …

profuse.definition: profūsē adv. with comp. profusus, immoderately, excessively : eo profusius sumptui deditus erat, S.— Confusedly, in disorder : tendentes in castra, L. (al. effuse).

profusus.definition: profūsus adj. P. of profundo.—Of persons, lavish, extravagant, profuse : nepos: alieni appetens, sui profusus, lavish of his own , S.—Of things, extravagant, excessive, profuse : profusis sumptibus vivere: epulae: gen…

progener.definition: prōgener ī, m a grand-daughter's husband, Ta.

progenero.definition: prō-generō —, —, āre, to beget, generate: nec Progenerant aquilae columbam, H.

progenies.definition: prōgeniēs —, acc. em, abl. ē, f pro+GEN-, descent, lineage, race, family : Progeniem vostram ab atavo proferens, T.: divina: Progeniem Troiano a sanguine duci, V.— Descendants, posterity, offspring, progeny, child : s…

progenitor.definition: prōgenitor ōris, m pro+GEN-, the founder of a family, an ancestor, progenitor : maiorum suorum, N.: progenitore comanti Esse sata, O.

progigno.definition: prō-gīgnō genuī, —, ere, to beget, bear, bring forth: res, quae ex iis (seminibus) progignuntur: Illam terra parens Progenuit, V.: te saevae progenuere ferae, O.

prognatus.definition: prō-gnātus adj., born, descended, sprung: ex Cimbris, Cs.: ab Dite patre, Cs.: Bona bonis, T.: docere semet prognatos, his own children, H.: Romulus deo, L.: Tantalo prognatus, i. e. Atreus, grandson of Tantalus.—Of p…

prognostica.definition: prognōstica ōrum, n , prognwstika/, harbingers, weather-signs (a work of Aratus translated by Cicero).

progredior.definition: prōgredior gressus, ī, dep. pro+gradior, to come forth, go forth, go forward, go on, advance , proceed : regredi quam progredi malle: in locum iniquum, Cs.: ante signa, L.— Fig., to proceed, advance, go on, make progr…

progressio.definition: prōgressiō ōnis, f pro + GRAD-, a going forward, progression, advancement, progress, growth, increase : omnium rerum principia suis progressionibus usa augentur: admirabilis ad excellentiam: rei militaris.—In rhet., a…

progressus2.definition: prōgressus ūs, m pro+GRAD-, a going forward, advance, progress : alqm progressu arcere: progressūs et regressūs constantes (of planets).—Fig., advancement, progress, growth, increase : aetatis: primo progressu, at the…

prohibeo.definition: prohibeō uī (old subj perf. prohibessit, C.), itus, ēre pro+habeo, to hold before, hold back, keep away, check, restrain, hinder, prevent, avert, keep off, debar : praedones procul ab insulā: vim hostium ab oppidis, C…

prohibitio.definition: prohibitiō ōnis, f pro+HAB-, a forbidding, legal prohibition : tollendi.

proicio.definition: prōiciō iēcī, iectus, ere pro+iacio, to throw forth, cast before, throw out, throw down, throw : Tu (canis) Proiectum odoraris cibum, thrown to you , H.: aquilam intra vallum, Cs.: infantem provectum in mare proieceru…

proiectio.definition: prōiectiō ōnis, f pro+IA-, a throwing forward, stretching out : brachii.

proiectus.definition: prōiectus adj. P. of proicio, stretched out, extended, jutting out, projecting : urbs in altum: saxa, V.— Prostrate, outstretched : ego in antro, V. —Fig., prominent, conspicuous : audacia: cupiditas.— Inclined, addic…

proinde.definition: pro-inde (often disyl.: old proin; usu. monosyl., T.), adv., hence, therefore, accordingly, then (in advice or exhortation): Proinde hinc vos amolimini, T.: proinde si qui sunt, ita sint parati: proinde parati intenti…

prolabor.definition: prō-lābor lapsus, ī, to glide forward, slide along, slip: at Canis ad caudam serpens prolabitur Argo, C. poët.: conlapsus pons, usque ad alterius initium pontis prolabi eum leniter cogebat, to slide along, L.—To fall …

prolapsio.definition: prōlapsiō ōnis, f pro+2 LAB-, a slipping, falling : ingredi sine prolapsione.

prolatio.definition: prōlātiō ōnis, f pro+TAL-, a bringing forward, adducing, mentioning : exemplorum.— A putting forward, advancing, extension : finium, L.— A putting off, deferring, delay, postponement : iudici: rerum: diei, Cs.

prolato.definition: prōlātō —, —, āre, freq. prolatus, to extend, enlarge : agros, Ta.— To put off, defer, delay, postpone : id (malum) opprimi prolatando: consultationes, S.: nihil prolatandum ratus, L.: prolatando, by procrastination ,…

prolecto.definition: prōlectō —, —, āre, freq. prolicio, to allure, entice forth, lead on : egentīs spe legationis: praeda animos prolectat, O.

proles.definition: prōlēs is, f pro+1 OL-, a growth, offshoot, offspring, progeny, children, descendants, race, posterity : futurorum hominum: gemella, O.: di Romulae genti date prolem, H.: pulchra, V.: ferrea, the iron race , C. poët.:…

proletarius.definition: prōlētārius adj. proles, relating to offspring ; hence, in the division of the people by Servius Tullius, affording to the state only children, having no estate, of the lowest class, proletary .

prolicio.definition: prōliciō —, —, ere prolacio, to allure forth, incite : voluptas tardā prolicienda morā, O.

prolixe.definition: prōlixē adv. with comp. prolixus, largely, abundantly, copiously, freely : Capillus passus, T.: id fecit.— Freely, readily, cheerfully, bountifully : Accipit nemo prolixius, entertains more liberally , T.: polliceri: …

prolixus.definition: prōlixus adj. with comp. LIC-, well-disposed, obliging, courteous : natura: animus: in Pompeium prolixior.— Favorable, fortunate : cetera spero prolixa esse his competitoribus.

prologus.definition: prōlogus ī, m , pro/logos, a preface to a play, prologue: Nullum invenire prologum, T.—One who recites a prologue, T.

proloquor.definition: prō-loquor cūtus, ī, dep., to speak out, utter, express, declare, announce: miserias Medeai caelo atque terrae, Enn. ap. C.: cogitata, T.: in senatu proloqui, se prohibiturum, etc., L.—To foretell, predict, Pr.

prolubium.definition: prōlubium ī, n pro+LIB-, desire, inclination, fancy , T.

proludo.definition: prō-lūdō sī, —, ere, to play beforehand, prelude, practise: ad pugnam, V.: Sic ubi prolusit, O. —Fig.: sententiae quibus proluserint, which began the speech: Iurgia proludunt, wrangling comes first, Iu.

proluo.definition: prō-luō luī, lūtus, ere, to wash forth, throw out, cast out: genus omne natantum fluctus Proluit, V.—To wash off, wash away: tempestas ex montibus nives proluit, Cs.: silvas Eridanus, V.—To wash, moisten, wet, drench:…

prolusio.definition: prōlūsiō ōnis, f pro+LVD-, a prelude, preliminary exercise, trial, essay .

proluvies.definition: prōluviēs —, f pro+3 LV-, an overflow, inundation : mira.— Refuse, filth : foedissima ventris, V.

promereo.definition: prō-mereō uī, —, ēre, to deserve, be deserving of, merit: quando bene promeruit, fiat, T.

promereor.definition: prō-mereor meritus, ērī, dep., to deserve, merit, earn, be worthy: Ita velim me promerentem ames, T.: levius punitus quam sit promeritus: paratiores ad bene de multis promerendum: te numquam negabo (ea) Promeritam, V.

promeritum.definition: prō-meritum ī, n P. n. of promereor, desert, merit : vestrum in nos: deae, O.

prominens.definition: prōminēns entis, adj. P. of promineo, prominent .—As subst n., a projection : in prominenti litoris, Ta.: prominentia montium, Ta.

promineo.definition: prō-mineō uī, —, ēre, to stand out, jut, be prominent, overhang, project, extend: Phaselis prominet penitus in altum, L.: coma Prominet in voltūs, hangs over the face, O.: nemorum coma gelido prominet Algido, H.: matr…

promisce.definition: prōmiscē adv. promiscus, in common, indiscriminately, indifferently : iudicium promisce stultis ac sapientibus datum: aedificari, i. e. without regard to private ownership of land , L.

promiscue.definition: prōmiscuē adv. promiscuus, in common , promiscuously, confusedly, indiscriminately : (mares et feminae) promiscue in fluminibus perluuntur, Cs.: puberes atque negotiatores interficere, S.

promiscus.definition: prōmiscus adj. pro+MIC-, in common, indiscriminate, promiscuous : usus rerum omnium, L.—As subst n. : nec arma in promisco, i. e. in every man's hands , Ta.— Common, mean : promisca ac vilia mercari, Ta.

promiscuus.definition: prō-miscuus adj. pro+MIC-, mixed, without distinction, in common, indiscriminate, promiscuous : conubia, i. e. between patricians and plebeians , L.: divina atque humana promiscua habere, S.— As subst n. : in promiscu…

promissio.definition: prōmissiō ōnis, f pro+MIT-, a promising, promise : provinciae: scelerum.—In rhet., a promise .

promissor.definition: prōmissor ōris, m pro+MIT-, a promiser, braggart , H.

promissum.definition: prōmissum ī, n P. n. of promitto, a promise : nostrum: promisso teneri: promissis induxit alquem: deum promisso ludit inani, O.: illis promissis standum non est: promissis manere, V.: Dic aliquid dignum promissis, H.:…

promissus.definition: prōmissus adj. P. of promitto, hanging down, long : coma, L.: capillo esse promisso, Cs.

promitto.definition: prō-mittō mīsī (prōmīstī for prōmīsistī, T., Ct., prōmīsse, Ct.), missus, ere, to let go, put forth, let hang down, let grow: capillum ac barbam, L. —Fig., to set in view, assure beforehand, foretell, predict: mihi al…

promo.definition: prōmō prōmpsī, prōmptus, ere pro+emo, to take out, give out, bring forth, produce : iubeo promi utrosque (scyphos): signa ex aerario prompta, L.: medicamenta de narthecio: vina dolio, H.: pugionem vaginā, Ta.: Sol, di…

promoneo.definition: prō-moneō —, —, ēre, to forewarn: de istius scelere promoneri.—To warn further: te.

promota.definition: prōmōta ōrum, n P. of promoveo, preferable things .

promoveo.definition: prō-moveō mōvī (prōmōrat for prōmōverat, H., Ph.), mōtus, ēre, to move forward, cause to advance, push onward, advance: saxa vectibus, Cs.: assa in alterum angulum: castra ad Carthaginem, move onward, L.: hasta suā sp…

prompte.definition: (prōmptē) adv. with comp. 1 promptus, readily, quickly : dare operam, Ta.— Easily : promptius expediam, Iu.—Fig., openly, freely : dicam paulo promptius.

promptus1.definition: prōmptus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of promo, set forth, brought forward, disclosed, exposed, manifest : aliud clausum in pectore, aliud promptum in linguā habere, S.: prompta et aperta: nihil quod non istius cupidit…

promptus2.definition: (prōmptus, ūs) only abl. ū, m promo+ EM-, in the phrase, in promptu, public, open, visible, manifest, before the eyes : ut (decorum) sit in promptu: ingenium in promptu habere, show his ability , S.: in promptu scrini…

promulgatio.definition: prōmulgātio ōnis, f promulgo, a public announcement, formal publication, promulgation : leges sine ullā promulgatione latae.

promulgo.definition: prōmulgō āvī, ātus, āre, to bring forward publicly, propose openly, publish, promulgate: de salute alcuius: leges quae promulgatae fuerunt: res multos dies promulgata: hoc promulgare ausus est, ut, etc., to propose to…

promulsis.definition: prōmulsis idis, f pro+mulsum, an appetizer, whet, first course (usu. of eggs or salt fish).

promunturium.definition: prōmunturium (prōmon-) ī, n pro + 2 MAN-, a projecting part of a mountain, spur , L. — A mountain projecting into the sea, headland, promontory : in promunturio fanum est Iunonis: (oppida) posita in extremis promuntur…

promus.definition: prōmus ī, m pro+EM-, a cellarer, steward, butler : foris est promus, H.

promutuus.definition: prō-mūtuus adj., paid beforehand, advanced, lent in advance: insequentis anni vectigal promutuum, i. e. advanced for the next year, Cs.

prone.definition: prōnē adv. pronus, inclined, leaning, slanting ; opp. directe ad perpendiculum, Cs.

pronepos.definition: pro-nepōs ōtis, m a great-grandson, C., O.

pronuba.definition: prōnuba ae, f pro+NEB-, she who prepares the bride, bride's-woman : Iuno, V., O.: Bellona manet te pronuba, i. e. discord shall preside over the marriage , V.: Tisiphone, O.

pronuntiatio.definition: prōnūntiātiō ōnis, f pronuntio, a public declaration, publication, proclamation : quā pronuntiatione factā , Cs.: lege et pronuntiatione condemnatus, i. e. the decision of the court .—In rhet., utterance, delivery, ma…

pronuntiator.definition: prōnūntiātor ōris, m pronuntio, a relater, narrator : rerum gestarum.

pronuntiatum.definition: prōnūntiātum ī, n P. n. of pronuntio, in logic, a proposition, axiom .

pronuntio.definition: prō-nūntiō āvī, ātus, āre, to make publicly known, publish, proclaim, announce: decretum: leges: in vendundo eam rem, disclose: amplius de consili sententiā : palam de sellā, sese eius nomen recepturum.—To utter, rend…

pronurus.definition: prō-nurus ūs, f a grandson's wife, O.

pronus.definition: prōnus adj. with comp. PRO-, turned forward, bent over, inclined, leaning, hanging, stooping, bending : pecora, quae natura prona finxit, S.: pronus pendens in verbera, leaning forward to strike , V.: pronus magister …

prooemium.definition: prooemium ī, n , prooi/mion, an introduction, preface, proem: citharoedi, prelude: legis: prooemia rixae, beginnings, Iu.

propagatio.definition: prōpāgātiō ōnis, f 1 propago, an extension, enlargement : finium imperi: quae propagatio et soboles origo est rerum p., extension of relationship.—An extension, prolongation : vitae: imperi, L.— A propagation : vitium…

propagator.definition: prōpāgātor ōris, m 1 propago, an extender, one who lengthens : provinciae, i. e. of command in a province .

propago1.definition: prōpāgō āvī, ātus, āre pro+PAC-, to set forward, extend, enlarge, spread, increase : finīs imperi: eo bello terminos populi R. propagari, L. — To generate, procreate, engender, propagate : stirpem in centesimum annum:…

propago2.definition: prōpāgō or (of persons) propā gō inis, f pro+PAC-, a set, layer, slip, shoot : propagines nonne efficiunt, ut, etc.: adulta vitium, H.— Offspring, descendant, children, race, breed, stock, progeny, posterity : Alipedi…

propalam.definition: prō-palam adv., openly, publicly, manifestly: signis conlocatis: haec dicere, L.

propatulus.definition: prō-patulus adj., open in front, not covered, open, uncovered: in propatulo locc.—As subst n., an open place: in propatulo aedium, in the open court, L.: volgo in propatulis epulati sunt, in the courts, L.: pudicitiam…

prope.definition: prope adv. with comp. propius (for sup., see proximē ); also praep. with acc.—In space, near, nigh: tam prope Italiam videre: adulescentia voluptates prope intuens (opp. procul): prope est spelunca quaedam: bellum tam…

propello.definition: prō-pellō pulī, pulsus, ere, to drive forward, drive forth, drive away, drive out: hostīs, Cs.: hostem a castris, L.: pecora pastum propulsa, L.: in profundum e scopulo corpora, O.: saxa in subeuntes, hurl, Cu.: propu…

propendeo.definition: prō-pendeō —, ēnsus, ēre, to hang down, preponderate: tantum propendere illam (lancem) putet, ut, etc.— Fig., to weigh more, preponderate: si bona propendent.—To be inclined, be disposed, be favorable: (animi iudicium…

propense.definition: prōpēnsē adv. with comp. propensus, willingly, readily, with inclination : propensius senatum facturum, L.

propensio.definition: prōpēnsiō ōnis, f pro+PAND-, inclination, propensity : ad summam bonum adipiscendum.

propensus.definition: prōpēnsus adj. with comp. P. of propendeo, hanging down, preponderant : id fit propensius.— Inclining towards, coming near, approaching : disputatio ad veritatis similitudinem propensior.— Inclined, disposed, prone, r…

properanter.definition: (properanter) adv. with comp. propero, hastily, speedily, quickly : alqd accipere, Ta.: beneficia properantius, quam aes mutuum, reddere, S.: properantius ire, O.

properantia.definition: properantia ae, f propero, a hastening, haste : ex tantā properantiā, S.: periculum ex properantiā, Ta.

properatio.definition: properātiō ōnis, f propero, a hastening, haste : mea.

properato.definition: properātō adv. properatus, quickly, speedily : ad mortem agitur, Ta.

properatus.definition: properātus adj. propero, hurried, accelerated, rapid, quick, speedy : mors, O.: gloria rerum, O.: naves, Ta.

propere.definition: properē adv. properus, hastily, in haste, quickly, speedily : Curre, T.: egredere, N.: Cumas se recepit, L.: naves onerare, S.

properipes.definition: properipēs edis, adj. properus+pes, swift of foot : dux, Ct.

propero.definition: properō āvī, ātus, āre properus, to make haste, hasten, be quick, be in haste, go quickly : mihi properandum necessario est: haec properantes scripsimus, in haste : simulabat sese negoti gratiā properare, S.: ad praed…

properus.definition: properus adj. pro+2 PAR-, quick, speedy, hastening : aurigae, V.: Telamon, O.: potentiae adipiscendae, Ta.: quoquo facinore clarescere, Ta.

propexus.definition: prō-pexus P., combed forward, combed down, hanging: in pectore barba, V.: ad pectora barba, O.: crinis, Ta.

propino.definition: propīnō (prō-, T.), āvī, — , āre, to drink to one's health, pledge: propino hoc pulchro Critiae. —To hand over, yield up: Hunc comedendum et ebibendum vobis propino, pass on, T.

propinquitas.definition: propinquitās ātis, f propinquus, nearness, vicinity, proximity, propinquity : hostium, Cs.: locorum: castra aptissima maris propinquitate, Cs.: silvarum petunt propinquitates, Cs.—Fig., relationship, affinity, kindred…

propinquo.definition: propinquō —, —, āre propinquus, to draw near, come nigh, approach : vis inimica propinquat, V.: scopulo, V.: ripae, V.— To bring near, bring on, hasten, accelerate : rite Augurium, V.

propinquus.definition: propinquus adj. with comp. prope, near, nigh, neighboring : rus, T.: loca, S.: urbs: nimium Sol, H.: urbi montes, N.: itinera loca, L.: exsilium paulo propinquius, O.—As subst n., neighborhood, vicinity : ex propinquo…

propior.definition: propior ius, gen. ōris, adj. comp. (for sup., see proximus) cf. prope.—In space, nearer, nigher : portus propior, V.: tumulus, L.: Ut propior patriae sit fuga, O.: propior montem suos conlocat, S.—Plur n . as subst: p…

propitio.definition: propitiō —, ātus, āre propitius, to appease, propitiate : Iovem, Cu.: propitiata Iuno, Ta.

propitius.definition: propitius adj. prope, favorable, well-disposed, gracious, kind, propitious : dii mihi: parentes, T.: uti volens propitius suam sospitet progeniem, L.

propola.definition: propōla ae, m , propw/lhs, a forestaller, retailer, huckster: vinum a propolā.

propono.definition: prō-pōnō posuī, positus, ere, to put forth, set forth, lay out, place before, expose to view, display: vexillum, Cs.: manūs, caput, O.: ediscendos fastos populo: in publico epistulam.—Fig., to set before the mind, pro…

propositio.definition: prōpositiō ōnis, f propono, a presentation, representation, conception : vitae: animi.— A principal subject, theme , C.—In logic, the fundamental assumption .

propositum.definition: prōpositum ī, n P. n. of propono, that which is proposed, a plan, intention, design, resolution, purpose : quidnam propositi haberet, Cs.: adsequi, to attain : propositum tenere, L.: peragere, N.: tenax propositi, H.—…

propositus.definition: prōpositus adj. P. of propono, exposed, open : omnibus telis fortunae vita; tabernis apertis proposita omnia in medio vidit, L.: oppida ad praedam, Cs.: mulier omnibus, accessible.— At hand, impending : vitae periculum.

propraetor.definition: prō-praetor ōris, m an ex-praetor, made governor of a province without military command, propraetor: a propraetoribus administrari.

proprie.definition: propriē adv. proprius, personally, severally, as one's own, properly, in person : parte (campi) frui: quod tu amandus es, id est proprie tuum: cuius causam neque senatus publice neque ullus ordo proprie susceperat: qu…

proprietas.definition: proprietās ātis, f propius, a property, peculiarily, peculiar nature, quality : singularum rerum singulae proprietates: definitio genere de claratur, et proprietate quādam: frugum proprietates, peculiar kinds , L.

proprius.definition: proprius adj., not common with others, own special, several, individual, peculiar, particular, proper: tria praedia Capitoni propria traduntur, as his private property: familia, L.: proprio Marte, by his own bravery, …

propter1.definition: propter adv. prope, near, hard by, at hand : ibi angiportum propter est, T.: cum duo reges propter adsint: duo filii propter cubantes: cornix volans, Ph.

propter2.definition: propter praep. with acc. 1 propter, near, hard by, next to, close to : hic propter hunc adsiste, T.: qui propter <*>e sedit: insulae propter Siciliam. —Fig., on account of, by reason of, for the sake of, through, in v…

propterea.definition: propter-eā adv., therefore, for that cause, on that account: Ea res est, proptereaque nunc misera est, T.: haec propterea de me dixi, ut, etc.: id propterea hunc sequor, T.—Esp., in the phrase, propterea quod, because…

propudium.definition: propudium ī, n pro+4 PV-, a shameful act (old); hence, of a person, a scandal, a vile wretch : illud Antonius.

propugnaculum.definition: prōpūgnāculum ī, n propugno, a bulwark, tower, rampart, fortress, defence : ut propugnaculo ceteris (navis) esset: pontī s et propugnacula iungunt, V.: Siciliae, i. e. the fleet : navium, i. e. ships furnished with to…

propugnatio.definition: prōpūgnātiō ōnis, f propugno, a defence, vindication : dignitatis tuae: suscepi propugnationem pro ornamentis tuis.

propugnator.definition: prōpūgnātor ōris, m propugno, one who fights in defence, a defender, soldier : a propugnatoribus relictus locus, Cs.—Esp., in a ship, a marine, soldier : remigum propugnatorumque numerus, Cs.: classis inops propter di…

propugno.definition: prō-pūgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to go forth to fight, sally, make sorties: ex silvis rari, Cs.—To fight in defence, repel an assault, resist: uno tempore propugnare et munire, Cs.: pro suo partu: multos e muris propugnantes…

propulsatio.definition: prōpulsātiō ōnis, f propulso, a driving back, warding off : periculi.

propulso.definition: prōpulsō —, ātus, āre, freq. propello, to drive back, ward off, repel, repulse : ibi, S.: hostem, Cs.: inimicorum impetūs.—Fig., to ward off, avert, repel : quod tu speres, propulsabo facile, will put out of the quest…

propylaea.definition: propylaea —, n , propu/laia, a gateway, entrance; esp., the Propylaea to the Parthenon.

prora.definition: prōra ae, f , prw=|ra, the forepart of a ship, bow, prow: prorae admodum erectae, Cs.: terris advertere proram, V.: prorae tutela Melanthus, i. e. the lookout, O.: prorae litore inlisae, L.— Prov.: mihi prora et puppi…

prorepo.definition: prō-rēpō rēpsī, —, ere, to creep forth, crawl out: (formica) non usquam prorepit, H.

proripio.definition: prō-ripiō puī, reptus, ere, to drag forth: hominem proripi iubet: nudos pedes, i. e. spring forth, O.: se ex curiā repente proripuit, rushed out: se ex curiā domum, S.: se portā foras, Cs.: se undique in publicum, rus…

prorogatio.definition: prōrogātiō ōnis, f prorogo, a prolongation, extension : imperi, of one's command , L.: diei, postponement .

prorogo.definition: prō-rogō āvī, ātus, āre, to prolong, continue, extend, protract: quinquenni imperium Caesari: provinciam: imperium in insequentem annum, L.: Alterum in lustrum, meliusque semper Proroget aevum, H.—To put off, defer: d…

prorsum.definition: prōrsum adv. pro+vorsum, forwards : cursari rursum prorsum, to and fro , T.—Fig., absolutely, at all : prorsum nihil intellego, T.

prorsus.definition: prōrsus adv. pro+vorsus, forward, right onward : prorsus ibat res: huc prorsus se inruere, rush right in on us , T.—Fig., by all means, certainly, utterly, absolutely, entirely : tacere, T.: nullo modo prorsus adsenti…

prorumpo.definition: prō-rumpō rūpī, ruptus, ere, to break forth, break out, rush forth, make an attack: in hostīs, V.: vis morbus in imum intestinum prorupit, N.: (Aetna) prorumpit ad aethera nubem, breaks out in, V.—Pass: It mare prorup…

proruo.definition: prō-ruō ruī, rutus, ere, to rush forth, make an onset, sally: quā (dextrum cornu) proruebat, Cs.: in hostem, Cu.—To cast down, tear down, pull down, throw down, overthrow, overturn, demolish, prostrate: eā parte (muni…

prosapia.definition: prōsāpia ae, f a stock, race, family: homo veteris prosapiae, S.: eorum, ut utamur veteri verbo, prosapiam.

proscaenium.definition: proscaenium (proscēn-) ī, n , proskh/nion, the front part of the stage, proscenium: theatrum et proscaenium, L.—Plur, a stage, theatre, V.

proscindo.definition: prō-scindō —, —, ere, to plough, break up: terram iuvencis, V.: ferro campum, O.—Fig., to satirize, revile, defame: summotum (me) patriā, O.

proscribo.definition: prō-scrībō scrīpsī, scrīptus, ere, to make public by writing, publish, proclaim, announce: in eum diem Kalendas Martias: non proscriptā neque edictā die: proscribit se auctionem esse facturum. —To post up, offer for s…

proscriptio.definition: prōscrīptiō ōnis, f pro+SCALP-, a public notice of sale, advertisement : bonorum: praediorum.— Proscription, outlawry, confiscation : proscriptionis miserrimum nomen: de capite civis et de bonis proscriptionem ferre.

proscripturio.definition: prōscrīpturiō —, —, īre, desider. proscribo, to desire to proscribe .

proscriptus.definition: prōscrīptus ī, m P. of proscribo, an outlaw, proscribed person, one under the ban : lex, quae proscriptum iuvari vetat: in proscriptorum numero esse, S.

proseco.definition: prō-secō cuī, ctus, āre, in religion, of parts of the victim to be offered, to cut off, cut away: hostiae exta, L.—P. pass., plur. n. as subst: inposuit prosecta aris, i. e. the entrails, O.

prosemino.definition: prō-sēminō —, ātus, āre, to sow, scatter, plant: ostreas.—Fig., to continue, propagate: proseminatae sunt familiae.

prosequor.definition: prō-sequor cūtus (quūtus), ī, dep., to follow, accompany, attend, follow after, escort: eum milites electi sunt prosecuti, Cs.: unum illum, N.: exsequias illius funeris, attend: lacrimis ad fores, O.: Aeneas Prosequit…

proseucha.definition: proseucha ae, f , proseuxh/, a place for prayer, oratory, Iu.

prosilio.definition: prōsiliō uī, —, īre pro+salio, to leap forward, spring forth, spring up : quidnam hic properans prosilit, T.: temere: ex tabernaculo, L.: de capitis paterni Vertice (Minerva), O.: e convivio, Cu.—Of things, to spring …

prosocer.definition: prō-socer erī, m a wife's grandfather, O.

prospecto.definition: prōspectō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. prospicio, to look forth, look out, look at, view, behold, see after off, gaze upon : ex tectis fenestrisque, L.: Campani moenia urbis prospectantes repleverant, L.: mare: proelium, S.:…

prospectus2.definition: prōspectus ūs, m pro+SPEC-, a lookout, distant view, prospect : cum saepibus prospectus impediretur, Cs.: prospectum ager arbustis consitis prohibebat, S.: pulcherrimo prospectu porticus: adempto propinquo congredient…

prospeculor.definition: prō-speculor ātus, ārī, to look out, explore: Siccium prospeculatum ad locum castris capiendum mittunt, L.: e muris adventum imperatoris, to watch for, L.

prospere.definition: prōsperē adv. prosperus, according to hope, as desired, favorably, luckily, fortunately, prosperously : quicquid gestum est: evenire: haec minus prospere procedebant, N.

prosperitas.definition: prōsperitās ātis, f prosperus, good-fortune, success, prosperity : vitae: valetudinis, vigorous health , N.: improborum prosperitates.

prospero.definition: prōsperō āvī, ātus, āre prosperus, to render fortunate, make happy, prosper : populo R. vim victoriamque, L.: patrum decreta, H.

prosperus.definition: prōsperus adj. with comp. pro+spes, according to hope, as desired, favorable, fortunate, prosperous : fortuna: res avi tui: hominum generi prosperus fulgor, propitious : si cetera prospera evenissent, L.: prosperos ex…

prospicientia.definition: prōspicientia ae, f prospicio, foresight, forethought, precaution : vigilia et prospicientia.

prospicio.definition: prōspiciō ēxī, ectus, ere SPEC-, to look forward, look into the distance, have a view, look out, look, see : parum prospiciunt oculi, do not see well , T.: ex superioribus locis in urbem, Cs.: multum, have an extensiv…

prosterno.definition: prō-sternō strāvī, strātus, ere, to strew before, spread out, cast down, throw to the ground, overthrow, prostrate: ceteros, T.: arbor prostravit multam pondere silvam, O.: se ad pedes meos: prostraverant se omnes hum…

prostituo.definition: prōstituō uī, ūtus, ere pro+statuo, to set forth in public, expose to dishonor, prostitute, offer for sale : faciem lucro suam, O.: se, Ct.: Ingrato vocem foro, O.

prosto.definition: prō-stō stitī, —, āre, to be on sale, be exposed for sale: liber prostat, H.: cuius vox prostitit.— To offer one's person for sale, prostitute oneself, Iu.— Fig.: illud amicitiae numen Prostat, i. e. is venal, O.

prosubigo.definition: prō-subigō —, —, ere, to dig up, cast up: pede terram, V.

prosum.definition: prō-sum prōfuī, prōdesse (inf fut. prō fore, H.), to be useful, be of use, do good, benefit, profit, serve: prodesse aequomst, T.: quorum altera prosunt: aliena ac nihil profutura petunt, S.: magis Menenianum profuit …

protego.definition: prō-tegō tēxī, tēctus, ere, to cover before, hide in front, cover over, cover, protect, shelter: tabernacula protecta hederā, Cs.: aedes, furnish with a projecting roof: hunc scutis protegunt hostes, protect, Cs.: scu…

protelo.definition: prō-tēlō —, —, āre pro+telum, to drive forth, drive away : te dictis, T.

protendo.definition: prō-tendō —, tus, ere, to stretch forth, stretch, reach out, extend: hastas, V.: bracchia In mare, O.: ire in protenta tela, O.—In zeugma: oculos dextramque precantem, i. e. lifting eyes and hands in supplication, V.

protero.definition: prō-terō —, trītus, ere, to tread under foot, trample down, wear away, crush, bruise: equitatus aversos (milites) proterere incipit, Cs.: agmina curru, V.: viride protritum et corruptum, L.—To trample, overthrow, malt…

proterreo.definition: prō-terreō uī, itus, ēre, to frighten off, scare away, drive away, affright, terrify: filium hinc, T.: Aulesten Adverso equo, V.: patriā proterritus: proterritis hostibus, Cs.

proterve.definition: protervē (prō-, T.), adv. with comp. protervus, recklessly, boldly, wantonly, impudently : iracundus, T.: consectans proterve bene de re p. meritor: quicquid facias protervius aequo, O.

protervitas.definition: protervitās ātis, f protervus, wantonness, pertness, sauciness, impudence : tua, T.: de protervitate oratio: Glycerae grata, H.

protervus.definition: protervus adj. pro+1 TER, pressing forward, violent, vehement : venti, H.: stella canis, oppressive , O.—Fig., forward, bold, pert, wanton, shameless, impudent : homo: dictum aut factum: vidua: iuvenes, H.: oculi, O.:…

protinam.definition: prōtinam (-tenam) adv. old for protinus, forthwith, immediately : hinc me conicere, T.

protinus.definition: prōtinus or prō-tenus adv., right onward, forward, farther on, onward: pergere: vox, quā protinus omne Contremuit nemus, i. e. far and wide, V.—Right on, continuously, directly, without pause, uninterruptedly: Laodice…

protraho.definition: prō-traho trāxī, tractus, ere, to draw forth, drag out, bring forward, produce: hinc in convivium Cominium: pedibusque informe cadaver (Caci) Protrahitur, V.: nudi in medium protrahebantur, L.—To bring to light, disco…

protrudo.definition: prō-trūdō sī, sus, ere, to thrust forward, push out: cylindrum: capite est protrusus foras, Ph. —Fig., to put off, defer: comitia in Ianuarium mensem.

proturbo.definition: prō-turbō āvī, ātus, āre, to drive on, drive away, repel, repulse: his facile pulsis ac proturbatis, Cs.: hostī s telis, L.: hostīs hinc comminus, V.: silvas, prostrate, O.: militum conviciis proturbatus, assailed, Ta.

prout.definition: pro-ut conj, according as, in proportion, accordingly, proportionately as, just as, as: tuas litteras, prout res postulat, exspecto: id, prout cuiusque ingenium erat, interpretabantur, L.

proveho.definition: prō-vehō vēxi, vectus, ere, to carry forward, move along, convey (old in act.).—Pass, to advance, move forward, go on, ride, drive: leni Africo provectus, Cs.: provehimur portu, V.: paulum ab suis equo provectus, L.: …

provenio.definition: prō-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come forth, appear, arise, be produced: proveniebant oratores novi, Naev. ap. C.: provenere ibi scriptorum magna ingenia, S.: Lana, O.: provenere dominationes, Ta.—To grow up, grow, thr…

proventus.definition: prōventus ūs, m pro+BA-, a coming forth, growth, produce, yield : Proventu oneret sulcos, V. —Fig., an issue, result : in bello omnīs secundos rerum proventūs expectare, Cs.— A harvest, fortunate issue, happy result, …

proverbium.definition: prōverbium ī, n pro+verbum, an old saying, saw, maxim, adage, proverb : tritum sermone: volgatum, L.: quod est Graecis hominibus in proverbio: proverbi locum obtinere: acta agimus, quod vetamur veteri proverbio.

providens.definition: prōvidēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of provideo, foreseeing, provident, prudent : homo: id est ad reliquas res providentius, in other respects more prudent : providentissimus quisque, Ta.

providenter.definition: prōvidenter adv. with sup. providens, with foresight, providently, carefully : exornat, S.: alqd providentissime constituere.

providentia.definition: prōvidentia ae, f providens, foresight, foreknowledge : providentia est, per quam futurum aliquid videtur.— Foresight, forethought, precaution, providence : deorum: alterum ex providentiā timorem adferre solet, S.: de…

provideo.definition: prō-videō vīdī, vīsus, ēre, to see in advance, discern, descry: ubi, quid petatur, procul providere nequeat, L.: Excusare . . . quod non Providisset eum, H.—Fig., to see beforehand, foresee: quid eventurum sit: plus a…

providus.definition: prōvidus adj. pro+VID-, foreseeing, prescient : mens rerum futurarum: futuri opinio, L.: veri augur, O.— Caring for, provident : natura utilitatum omnium: provida cura ducis, O.— Cautious, circumspect, provident, prud…

provincia.definition: prōvincia ae, f an office, duty, pursuit, charge, business, province: dura, T.: sibi provinciam depoposcit, ut me trucidaret.—A public office, appointment, charge, commission, administration, employment, command: urba…

provincialis.definition: prōvinciālis e, adj. provincia, of a province, provincial : negotia: administratio: scientia, the administration of a province : edictum, relating to a province : molestia, in administering a province : abstinentia, f…

provisio.definition: prōvīsiō ōnis, f pro+VID-, a foreseeing, foreknowing : animi.— Foresight, providence : longa animi: posteri temporis, precaution for.—Provision against, prevention : horum incommodorum est una provisio, ut, etc.

proviso1.definition: prōvīsō adv. 1 provisus, with forethought, deliberately : temere, proviso, Ta.

proviso2.definition: prō-visō —, —, ere, to go forth to see, see to it: proviso, quid agat Pamphilus, T.

provisor.definition: prōvīsor ōris, m pro+VID-, a foreseer, provider : dominationum, Ta.: utilium tardus, H.

provisus2.definition: (prōvīsus ūs), m pro+VID-.—Only abl. sing., a looking forward, distant view : ne oculi provisu iuvabant, Ta.— A foreseeing : periculi, Ta. — A caring for beforehand , Ta.

provivo.definition: prō-vīvō vīxī, ere, to live on, Ta.

provocatio.definition: prōvocātiō ōnis, f provoco, a citation before a higher tribunal, appeal : ad populum: poena sine provocatione: de provocatione certatum ad populum est, L.: provocationes omnium rerum.

provocator.definition: prōvocātor ōris, m provoco, a kind of gladiator .

provoco.definition: prō-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call forth, call out, summon: Pamphilam cantatum, T.: ad se Simonidem, Ph.: <*>oseo ore diem, O.—To call out, challenge, invite: (Aiacem) ad pugnam: provocatus haec spolia ex hoste caeso po…

provolo.definition: prō-volō āvī, —, āre, to fly forth, hurry forth, rush out: subito omnibus copiis, Cs.: ad primores, L.

provolvo.definition: prō-volvō volvī, volūtus, ere, to roll forward, roll along, roll over, overturn: hunc in mediam viam, T.: hunc iuga subter Provolvēre rotae, V.: fortunis provolvi, i. e. to be expelled from, Ta.— With se, to cast ones…

proxime.definition: proximē or proxumē adv. sup. proximus. —Of place, nearest, very near, next : quam proxime potest castris, as close as possible , Cs.: exercitum habere quam proxime hostem.—Fig., of time, very lately, just before, most…

proximitas.definition: proximitās ātis, f proximus, nearness, vicinity, proximity : nimia, O.—Fig., near relationship : ipsaque damno est mihi proximitas, O.— Similarity, resemblance : lateat vitium proximitate boni, O.

proximo.definition: proximō adv. proximus, very lately, shortly : proximo a. d. vi Kal. Octobr., just before .

proximus.definition: proximus or proxumus adj. sup. prope, the nearest, next : vicinus, next neighbor , T.: oppida, Cs.: mare, S.: iter in Galliam, most direct , Cs.: paries cum proximus ardet, adjoining , H.: ex proximo vicini fundo deie…

prudens.definition: prūdēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. for providens, foreseeing, foreknowing : quos prudentīs possumus dicere, id est providentīs: satisque prudens oti vitia negotio discuti, aware , Cu.— Knowing, skilled, skilful, …

prudenter.definition: prūdenter adv. with comp. and sup. prudens, sagaciously, intelligently, discreetly, circumspectly, learnedly, prudently : res attendere, S.: facere: disputavit multa: quaestio non satis prudenter constituta: belli adm…

prudentia.definition: prūdentia ae, f prudens, a foreseeing : futurorum.— Acquaintance, knowledge, skill, professional learning : civilis, statesmanship : iuris publici: iuris civilis, N.: verbosa simulatio prudentiae: cani rectoris, Iu.— …

pruina.definition: pruīna ae, f PVR-, hoar-frost, rime : quae (aqua) neque nive pruināque concresceret: pruinae ac nives: canae, H.: matutinae, O.: gelidae, i. e. snow , V.: ad medias sementem extende pruinas, i. e. winter , V.

pruinosus.definition: pruīnōsus adj. pruina, full of hoar-frost, frosty, rimy : herbae, O.: nox, O.

pruna.definition: prūna ae, f PVR-, a burning coal, live coal : medium per ignem multā premimus vestigia prunā, V.: prunae batillum, H.

pruniceus.definition: prūniceus adj. prunus, of plum-tree wood : torris, O.

prunum.definition: prūnum ī, n , prou=mnon, a plum: cerea, V.: pruna ferre, V., H.

prunus.definition: prūnus ī, f , prou/mnh, a plum-tree: prunis lapidosa rubescere corna, on the plum-trees, V.

prurio.definition: prūriō —, —, īre PVR-, to itch : si prurit ocelli Angulus, Iu.— To be wanton, make a wanton display , Ct., Iu.

prytaneum.definition: prytanēum or prytanīon ī, n , prutanei=on, in Greece, a city hall, hall of the prytanes, state dining hall, C., L.

prytanis.definition: prytanis is, m , pru/tanis, in Greece, a member of the chief executive body, prytane, L.

psallo.definition: psallō ī, —, ere, ya/llw, to play upon a stringed instrument, sing to the cithara: elegantius, S.: Doctae psallere Chiae, H.

psalterium.definition: psaltērium ī, n , yalth/rion, a stringed instrument, lute, psaltery.

psaltria.definition: psaltria ae, f , ya/ltria, a female player on the cithara, lutist, T., C., Iu.

psephisma.definition: psēphisma atis, n , yh/fisma, among the Greeks, an ordinance of the people, plebiscite.

pseudomenos.definition: pseudomenos ī, m , yeudo/menos, in logic, a false syllogism, piece of sophistry.

pseudothyrum.definition: pseudothyrum ī, n , yeudo/thuron, a backdoor, secret entrance: (nummi) per pseudothyrum revertantur, i. e. secretly.

psithius.definition: psithius (psy-) adj. , yi/thios, of a species of Grecian vine producing a sweet wine, Psithian: vitis, V.—As subst f. (sc. vitis), V.

psittacus.definition: psittacus ī, m , yi/ttakos, a parrot, O.

psychomantium.definition: psȳchomantīum (-ēum) ī, n , yuxomantei=on, a place for inquiring of the dead, place of necromancy.

pte.definition: -pte enclit., added to the abl. of a pron possess., self, own: suopte pondere: suāpte manu: nostrāpte culpā, T.

ptisanarium.definition: ptisanārium ī, n ptisana, barley-groats, a decoction of barley-groats, gruel : oryzae, H.

pubens.definition: pūbēns entis, adj. pubes, mature, flourishing, exuberant : herbae, V.

pubertas.definition: pūbertās ātis, f pubes, the age of manhood, maturity , Ta.— A sign of maturity, beard : dentes et pubertas.— Manhood, virility : inexhausta, Ta.

pubes1.definition: pūbēs eris, adj. 3 PV-, grown up, of ripe age, adult, pubescent : filii: priusquam pubes esset, N.: aetas, L.— Plur m . as subst, grown-up persons, adults, men : omnes puberes armati convenire consuerunt, Cs.— Covered…

pubes2.definition: pūbēs is, f 3 PV-, grown-up males youth able to bear arms, youth, young men : Italiae: robora pubis Lecta, V.: Romana, L.: indomita, i. e. the young bullocks , V.— The youth, throng, people : agrestis, V.: captiva, H.…

pubesco.definition: pūbēscō buī, ere, inch. pubes, to attain puberty, come to maturity : cum primum pubesceret: flos iuvenum pubescentium ad militiam, L.: aequali tecum aevo, V.— To grow up, ripen : omnia, quae terra gignit, maturata pub…

publicanus.definition: pūblicānus adj. publicus, of the public revenue : muliercula, i. e. a farmer-general's wench .— As subst m., a farmer-general of the revenues , usu. from the equestrian order: novum genus publicani: princeps publicano…

publicatio.definition: pūblicātiō ōnis, f publico, an appropriation to the state, confiscation : bonorum.

publice.definition: pūblicē adv. publicus, on account of the people, publicly, officially, for the state, in behalf of the state : Haud cito mali quid ortum ex hoc sit publice, any public misfortune , T.: aurum signanto, coin : disciplin…

publicitus.definition: pūblicitus adv. publicus, on the public account, at the public expense : asportarier, T.

publico.definition: pūblicō āvī, ātus, āre publicus, to make public, adjudge to public use, confiscate : regnum Iubae, Cs.: privata: censeo publicandas eorum pecunias, S.: bona Claudii, L.— To make public, impart to the public, make comm…

publicus.definition: pūblicus adj. populus, of the people, of the state, done for the state, public, common : rem bene gerere publicam, the business of the state , Enn. ap. C.: sacrificia publica ac privata, Cs.: iniuriae, to the state , …

pudendus.definition: pudendus adj. P. of pudeo, causing shame, shameful, scandalous, disgraceful, abominable : ut iam pudendum sit honestiora decreta esse legionum quam senatus: vita, O.: volnera, V.

pudens.definition: pudēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of pudeo, shamefast, bashful, modest, shy, chaste, sensitive, honorable : filius: pudens prave, H.: animus, T.—Plur m . as subst: neque pudentes suspicari oportet sibi parum c…

pudenter.definition: pudenter adv. with comp. and sup. pudens, modestly, bashfully, shyly : respondere: vivendo: sumere, H.: pudentius accedere: pudentissime hoc petere.

pudeo.definition: pudeō uī or puditum est, ere 4 PV-.— Intrans, to be ashamed, feel shame : non simultatem meam Revereri! non pudere! T.: inducitur ad pudendum.—Trans, to make ashamed, put to shame, humiliate : quem neque pudet Quicqua…

pudibundus.definition: pudibundus adj. pudeo, ashamed, covered with shame : matrona, H.: ora, O.

pudice.definition: pudīcē adv. pudicus, modestly, chastely, virtuously : doctum ingenium, T.

pudicitia.definition: pudīcitia ae, f pudicus, shamefastness, modesty, chastity, virtue : hinc pudicitia, illinc stuprum: nec suae nec alienae pudicitiae parcere: violare: praesidia pudoris et pudicitiae: pudicitiā amissā, L.: in propatulo…

pudicus.definition: pudīous adj. with comp. 4 PV-, shamefast, bashful, modest, chaste, pure, virtuous : ingenium, T.: possumus eos pudicos dicere?: coniunx, H.: Penelope, chaste , H.: nupta, O.— Chaste, pure, undefiled : preces, pure , O…

pudor.definition: pudor ōris, m 4 PV-, a shrinking from blame, desire of approval, shame, shamefastness, modesty, decency, propriety : patris, before a father , T.: ex hac parte pugnat pudor, illinc petulantia: ut pudorem rubor consequ…

puella.definition: puella ae, f dim. puer, a female child, girl, maiden, lass : puellam parere, T.: puella infans, H.: audi, Luna, puellas, H.: puellarum chorus, H.: proditor puellae risus, H.: Danai puellae, i. e. daughters , H.— A you…

puellaris.definition: puellāris e, adj. puella, of a girl, girlish, maidenly, youthful : animi, O.: plantae, i. e. of Europa , O.

puellula.definition: puellula ae, f dim. puella, a little girl, little sweetheart , T., Ct.

puer.definition: puer erī, m 3 PV-, a male child, boy, lad, young man (usu. till the age of seventeen): aliquam puero nutricem para, T.: id est semper esse puerum: laudator temporis acti Se puero, when he was a boy , H.: puerum filium…

puerilis.definition: puerīlis e, adj. with comp. puer, boyish, childish, youthful : puerili specie, senili prudentiā: tempus, O.: vox: regnum, L.: agmen, a troop of boys , V.: (facies) in virgine, boyish , O.— Boyish, childish, puerile, t…

pueriliter.definition: puerīliter adv. puerilis, like a child : ludentes, Ph.: blandiri, L.— Childishly, foolishly, sillily : facere.

pueritia.definition: pueritia (puertia, H.), ae, f puer, boyhood, childhood, youth (see puer): in pueritiā his artibus institutus: mihi cum eo a pueritiā Fuit familiaritas, T.: e pueritiae disciplinis ad patris exercitum profectus: omnem …

puerperium.definition: puerperium ī, n puerperus, a lying in, giving birth , Ta.

puerperus.definition: puerperus adj. puer+2 PAR-, parturient, bringing forth children : verba, charms to aid child-birth , O.—As subst f., a woman in labor : illa, T., H.

puerulus.definition: puerulus ī, m dim. puer, a little boy, little slave : inter suos puerulos versari.

puga.definition: pūga (pȳga) ae, f , pugh/, the rump, buttocks, H.

pugil.definition: pugil ilis, m PAC-, one who fights with the cestus, a fist-fighter, boxer, pugilist : pugilem esse (virginem) aiunt, T.: Olympionices: Illum non labor Isthmius Clarabit pugilem, H.

pugillaris.definition: pugillāris e (pūg-, Iu.), adj. pugillus, a handful, filling the fist, as large as the clenched hand , Iu.—Plur n . as subst, writing-tablets , Ct.

pugillatio.definition: pugillātiō ōnis, f pugillor, to be a boxer, boxing with the cestus, fist-fighting .

pugillatus.definition: (pugillātus, ūs), m pugillor, a fighting with the cestus, boxing (only abl sing .).

pugio.definition: pūgiō ōnis, m PAC-, a short dagger, dirk, poniard : cruentum extollens pugionem: pugione succinctus.—Fig.: o plumbeum pugionem! O leaden dagger! i. e. O weak argument!

pugiunculus.definition: pūgiunculus ī, m dim. pugio, a small dagger, stiletto .

pugna.definition: pūgna ae, f PAC-, a hand-to-hand fight, fight at close quarters, battle, combat, action, engagement : eam pugnam laudibus tulit, i. e. the single combat , L.: res ad pugnam atque ad manūs vocabatur, came to blows : di…

pugnacitas.definition: pūgnācitās ātis, f pugnax, combativeness, pugnacity : Dabunt Academici pugnacitatem, Ta.

pugnaciter.definition: pūgnāciter adv. with sup. pugnax, contentiously, violently, obstinately : certare cum aliis: pugnacissime defendere sententiam.

pugnantes.definition: pūgnantēs ium, m P. plur. of pugno, fighters, warriors : species pugnantium, Cs., Cu.

pugnantia.definition: pūgnantia ium, n P. plur. of pugno, contradictions, inconsistencies, things irreconcilable : pugnantia loqui: secum componere, H.

pugnator.definition: pūgnātor ōris, m pugno, a fighter, combatant : pugnator esse desierat, had ceased fighting , L.: pellis iuvenco Pugnatori operit, V.

pugnax.definition: pūgnāx ācis, adj. with comp. and sup. pugno, fond of fighting, combative, warlike, martial : centuriones: Minerva, O.: filius Thetidis, H.: gentes pugnacissimae, Cu.: Cumque sit ignis aquae pugnax, at war with , O.— C…

pugno.definition: pūgnō āvī, ātus, āre pugna, to fight, combat, give battle, engage, contend : sinistrā impeditā, Cs.: eminus lapidibus, S.: cum hoste comminus in acie: ex equo, on horseback : de loco, T.: extra ordinem in hostem, L.: …

pugnus.definition: pūgnus ī, m PAC-, a fist : (manum) comprimere pugnumque facere: certare pugnis: pugnos in ventrem ingerere, T.: pugno victus, in boxing , H.: gaudere pugnis, H.

pulchellus.definition: pulchellus (-cellus) adj. dim. pulcher, beautiful, pretty, little : Bacchae (i. e. Baccharum statuae).—As a mocking surname of Clodius Pulcher, Prettyman .

pulcher.definition: pulcher (pulcer) chra, chrum, adj. with comp. pulchrior, and sup. pulcherrimus, beautiful, beauteous, fair, handsome : homo, Enn. ap. C.: virgo, T.: iuvenis, Ph.: quo pulchrior alter Non fuit, V.: formā pulcherrima, V…

pulchre.definition: pulchrē (pulcrē) adv. with sup. pulcherrime pulcher, beautifully, excellently, finely, nobly, very : pulcherrume dictum, T.: adseverat, bravely : proxima hostia litatur saepe pulcherrime, very favorably : mihi pulchre…

pulchritudo.definition: pulchritūdō (pulcr-) inis, f pulcher, beauty : corporis: pulchritudinis verissimum iudicium.—Fig., beauty, excellence, attractiveness : oratoris: virtutis.

puleium.definition: pūlēium ī, n fleabane, fleawort, pennyroyal: aridum.—Fig.: tui sermonis, i. e. fragrance.

pullarius.definition: pullārius ī, m 1 pullus, the feeder of the sacred fowls, chicken-keeper, chicken-ward , C., L.

pullatus.definition: pullātus adj. 2 pullus, clothed in black, in mourning : proceres, Iu.

pullulo.definition: pullulō āvī, ātus, āre 1 pullus, to put forth, sprout, shoot, come forth : ab radice, V.: tot pollulat atra colubris, swarms with , V.—Fig.: pullulare incipiebat luxuria, to spread , N.

pullus1.definition: pullus ī, m 3 PV-, a young animal, foal, young, offspring : ranae, H.: columbini: gallinacei, L.: ciconiae, Iu.: ex ovis pulli orti, chicks.—A young fowl, chicken : mea pullis in parte catini, H.: caveā liberati pulli…

pullus2.definition: pullus adj. 2 PAL-, dark-colored, blackish-gray, dusky, blackish : ne maculis infuscet vellera pullis, V.: capilli, O.: myrtus, dusky , H.: praetor cum tunicā pullā, i. e. dressed like a common workman : toga, mournin…

pulmentarium.definition: pulmentārium ī, n pulmentum, a relish, appetizer : pulmentaria quaere Sudando, i. e. let severe exercise be your appetizer , H.

pulmentum.definition: pulmentum ī, n for pulpamentum, a relish of flesh : Lepus tute es et pulmentum quaeris? You are a hare and yet hunt for game? T.— A portion of food : in singula pulmenta, into bits , H.

pulmo.definition: pūlmō ōnis, m , pleu/mwn, a lung: tauri: e molli sanguis pulmone remissus, O.: columbae, Iu. —Plur, the lungs: loqui, quod fieri nec sine pulmorum vi potest: pulmonibus errat Ignis imis, O.

pulpamentum.definition: pulpāmentum ī, n pulpa, flesh; 1 PAL-, flesh, animal food, a choice bit, relish, appetizer : mihi est pulpamentum fames.

pulpita.definition: pulpita orum (sing. late), n a scaffold, platform, pulpit, lecture-desk, stage: percurrit pulpita socco, H.: vati, quem pulpita pascunt, Iu., O.

puls.definition: puls pultis, f 1 PAL-, a thick pap, pottage, porridge, mush (used in sacrifices, and given to the sacred chickens): si in offam pultis invasit (avis): grandes fumabant pultibus ollae (as food of the poor), Iu.

pulsatio.definition: pulsātiō ōnis, f pulso, a beating, striking : scutorum, L.: Alexandrinorum Puteolana, defeat .

pulso.definition: pulsō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. pello, to push against, strike upon, beat, hammer, keep hitting, batter : cum pulsetur incursione atomorum sempiternā: lictores ad pulsandos homines exercitatissimi: pulsari alios et verber…

pulsus2.definition: pulsus ūs, m 1 PAL-, a pushing, beating, striking, stamping, push, blow, impulse, stroke : pulsu externo agitari: pulsu remorum praestare, in rowing , Cs.: sonum vocis pulsu pedum modulantes, keeping time in the dance…

pulto.definition: pultō āvī, —, āre, freq. pello, to beat, strike, knock : ostium, T.: forīs, T.

pulvereus.definition: pulvereus adj. pulvis, of dust, filled with dust, dusty : nubes, clouds of dust , V.: farina, i. e. fine , O.: palla (Boreae), raising clouds of dust , O.

pulverulentus.definition: pulverulentus adj. pulvis, full of dust, covered with dust, dusty : via: aestas, V.: agmina, V.—Fig., attended with labor, toilsome : praemia militiae, O.

pulvillus.definition: pulvillus ī, m dim. pulvinus, a little cushion, small pillow , H.

pulvinar.definition: pulvīnar (polv-) āris, abl. ārī, n pulvinus, a couch of the gods, cushioned seat spread at a feast of the gods (before their statues in the lectisternium): Saliaribus Ornare pulvinar deorum dapibus, H.: in Iovis epulo…

pulvinarium.definition: pulvīnārium ī, n pulvinus, a cushioned seat of a god : in pulvinario consedisse, L.

pulvinus.definition: pulvīnus ī, m PLE-, a cushion, bolster, squab, pillow : pulvinos poposcisse: perlucidus: epistula super caput in pulvino posita, S.: de pulvino surgat equestri, i. e. the seat of honor , Iu.

pulvis.definition: pulvis eris, m or (rarely) f 1 PAL-, dust, powder : multus in calceis: pulveris vim magnam animadvortunt, S.: qui (ventus) nubes pulveris vehit, L.: nigro glomerari pulvere nubem, V.: pulverem Olympicum Conlegisse, H.…

pumex.definition: pūmex icis, m (once f , Ct.), a pumice-stone: liber pumice mundus, polished, H.: geminae poliantur pumice frontes (libelli), O., Ct.: pumice crura terere (to smooth the skin), O.—A rock with cavities, porous rock, hol…

pumiceus.definition: pūmiceus adj. pumex, of pumice-stone, of lava : molae, O.

punctim.definition: punctim adv. pungo, with the point : petere hostem, L.

punctum.definition: punctum ī, n P. n. of pungo, a prick, puncture : volucris parvulae (i. e. muscae), Ph.— A point, mathematical point , C.—Since in the comitia a point upon the waxed tablet indicated the name voted for, an affirmative …

pungo.definition: pungō pupugī, punctus, ere PIC-, to prick, puncture : neminem.— To produce by pricking, make by a thrust : volnus acu punctum.— Fig., to prick, sting, vex, grieve, trouble, disturb, afflict, mortify, annoy : (scrupulu…

punio.definition: pūniō or poeniō īvī, ītus, īre poena, to punish, correct, chastise : ambitum: sontes: facinus puniendum: tergo ac capite puniri, L.: quod non ego punior, O.— To take vengeance for, avenge, revenge : Graeciae fana.

punior.definition: pūnior or poenior ītus, īrī, dep. poena, to punish, correct, chastise : aliquem: inimicos: peccata: ira in puniendo.— To revenge, take satisfaction for, avenge : cupiditas puniendi doloris: hominum necem.

punitor.definition: pūnītor or poenītor ōris, m punio, an avenger : doloris sui.

pupilla.definition: pūpilla ae, f dim. pupa, girl, an orphan girl, female ward : infans: pupillae mater.

pupillaris.definition: pūpillāris e, adj. pupillus, of an orphan, belonging to a ward : pecuniae, L.

pupillus.definition: pūpillus ī, m dim. pupus, an orphan boy, orphan, ward : reliquit pupillum parvum filium: piger annus Pupillis, H., Iu.

puppis.definition: puppis is, acc. im, abl. ī (puppe, O., Iu.), f the hinder part of a ship, stern, poop: navem convertens ad puppim: navis longae, L.: surgens a puppi ventus, aft, V.: stans in puppe recurvā , O.: sedebamus in puppi et …

pupula.definition: pūpula ae, f dim. pupa, girl, the pupil of the eye : acies ipsa, quā cernimus, quae pupula vocatur: fixae, H.: duplex, O.

pupulus.definition: pūpulus ī, m dim. pupus, a little boy , Ct.

pure.definition: pūrē adv. with comp. purus, clearly, cleanly, brightly : lauta corpora, L.: splendens Pario marmore purius, H.— Distinctly, simply : loqui: pure apparere rem, as it is , H.— Completely, fully : Quid pure tranquillet, …

purgamen.definition: (pūrgāmen īnis),n purgo.—Only plur, a means of cleansing, expiation, atonement : mali, O.: caedis, O.: mentis, O.— That which is removed by cleansing, sweepings, offscourings : Vestae, from the temple of Vesta , O.

purgamentum.definition: (pūrgāmentum ī), n purgo.—Only plur, sweepings, offscourings, filth, dirt : receptaculum omnium purgamentorum urbis, L.: hortorum, Ta. —Of persons, refuse, dregs, offscouring : purgamenta servorum, Cu.: urbis suae, Cu.

purgatio.definition: pūrgātiō ōnis, f purgo, a cleansing, purging : alvi: purgationibus consumptus es.—Fig., an apology, justification , T.: purgatio est, cum factum conceditur, culpa removetur.

purgatus.definition: pūrgātus adj. P. of purgo, cleansed, clear : auris, i. e. open to admonition , H.

purgo.definition: pūrgō āvī, ātus, āre purus+1 AG-, to free from what is superfluous, make clean, make pure, clean, cleanse, purify : piscīs ceteros purga, bone , T.: falcibus locum, cleared the ground : domum muribus, Ph.: educ omnīs …

puriter.definition: pūriter adv. purus, purely, correctly : vitam egi, Ct.: lavit dentīs, Ct.

purpura.definition: purpura ae, f , porfu/ra, purple color, purple: violae sublucet purpura nigrae, V.: certantem uvam purpurae, H.—Purple stuff, purple cloth, purple garment: plebeia ac paene fusca: usque ad talos demissa, i. e. the tog…

purpurasco.definition: purpurāscō —, —, inch. purpuro, to grow purple : unda purpurascit.

purpuratus.definition: purpurātus ī, m purpura, one clad in purple, an officer of a royal court, king's attendant, courtier : minitare purpuratis tuis: ex purpuratis regis esse, L.

purpureus.definition: purpureus adj. , porfu/reos, purple-colored, purple, dark-red: toga: mare, i. e. dark.—Poet., of many hues, red, dark, brown, violet, purple: flos rosae, H.: pannus, H.: aurora, rose-red, O.: rubor (oris), a rosy blus…

purus.definition: pūrus adj. with comp. and sup. 1 PV-, free from dirt, free from admixture, clean, pure, unstained, unspotted : alqd purum liquidumque haurire: aqua, H.: manus, H.: purissima mella, V.: aëre purior ignis, O.: humus, cl…

pus.definition: pūs pūris, n 2 PV-, matter from a sore, pus ; hence, fig., gall, bitterness, malice : Rupili, H.

pusillus.definition: pusillus adj. dim. pūsus, boy; 3 PV-, very little, very small, petty, insignificant : testis: terra homines nunc educat pusillos, Iu.: villula: libelli: alqs, H.: habuimus in Cumano quasi pusillam Romam.—As subst n., …

pusio.definition: pūsiō ōnis, m 3 PV-, a little boy , C., Iu.

pustula.definition: pūstula ae, f pus, a pimple, pustule , Tb.

puta.definition: puta adv. imper. of puto, suppose, for instance, namely : Quinte, puta, aut Publi, H.

putamen.definition: putāmen inis, n puto, that which is pruned away, clippings, waste, shells : iuglandium.

putatio.definition: putātiō ōnis, f puto, a pruning, lopping .

putator.definition: putātor ōris, m puto, a pruner, trimmer , O.

puteal.definition: puteal ālis, n putealis, a kerb-stone of a well : putealia sigillata duo.— A puteal, stone enclosure marking a sacred spot ; esp., the Puteal in the Comitium : supra impositum puteal accepimus (to mark where Navius cu…

putealis.definition: puteālis e, adj. puteus, of a well : undae, well-water , O.

putearius.definition: puteārius ī, m puteus, a well-digger , L.

puteo.definition: pūteō —, —, ere 2 PV-, to stink : putet aper, H.: diurno mero, H.

puter.definition: puter tris, tre, adj. 2 PV-, rotten, decaying, putrefying, stinking, putrid : quibus alabaster puter esse videtur: fanum, mouldering , H.: poma, rotten , O.: bos, O.: corpora cicatricibus, Cu.: vomicae, Iu.— Crumbling…

putesco.definition: pūtēscō or pūtīscō pū tuī, —, ere, inch n. puteo, to rot, putrefy, decay : humi: cur Aiax putescit, H.: quā (muria) putuit orca, has become soaked with , H.

puteus.definition: puteus ī, m 1 PV-, a well : ex puteis iugibus aquam trahi: se in puteos abiecisse: putei perennes, H.— A pit : In solido puteum demitti, V.

putide.definition: pūtidē adv. with comp. putidus, disgustingly, disagreeably, affectedly : dicere: primi litteras putidius, with nauseous precision .

putidiusculus.definition: pūtidiusculus adj. dim. putidior, rather more tedious .

putidus.definition: pūtidus adj. with comp. 2 PV-, rotten, decaying, stinking, fetid : caro.—Of persons, rotten, withered : longo saeculo, H.: Putidius cerebrum, more addled , H.—Of style, affected, disgusting .

puto.definition: putō āvī (putāstī, T.; putā rem putāsset, C.), ātus, āre putus, to clean, cleanse, trim, prune : vitem, V.—Fig., to clear up, arrange, settle, adjust : rationes cum publicanis, close accounts.—To reckon, value, estima…

putrefacio.definition: putrefaciō fēcī, factus, ere puter+facio, to make rotten, cause to putrefy, rot : (templum) imbribus putrefaciendum, L.: putrefacta est spina, O.— To make friable, soften : saxa infuso aceto, L.

putresco.definition: putrēscō —, —, ere, inch. putreo, from puter, to rot, moulder, decay : vestis putrescit, H.

putridus.definition: putridus adj. putreo, from puter, rotten, decayed : dentes: pectora, withered , Ct.

putus.definition: putus adj. with sup. 1 PV-, pure, bright, splendid : meae putissimae orationes.

pyctes.definition: pyctēs ae, m , pu/kths, a boxer, pugilist, Ph.

pygargus.definition: pȳgargus ī, m , pu/gargos, a kind of antelope, Iu.

pylae.definition: pylae ārum, f , pu/lai, a narrow pass, defile: Tauri: Susides, Cu.

pyra.definition: pyra ae, f , pura/, a funeral pile, pyre: Ingens, V.: Constituere pyras, V., O.

pyramis.definition: pȳramis īdis, f , purami/s, a pyramid, C., Pr., Ta.

pyrethrum.definition: pyrethrum ī, n , pu/rethron, Spanish chamomile, pellitory.—Plur., O.

pyropus.definition: pyrōpus ī, m , purwpo/s, an alloy of copper and gold, gold-bronze, bronze, O., Pr.

pytisma.definition: pȳtisma atis, n , pu/tisma, that which is spit out: Qui pytismate lubricat orbem, i. e. spits out wine on the floor, Iu.

pytiso.definition: pȳtīsō —, —, āre, puti/zw, to spit out: pytisando modo mihi Quid vini absumpsit, T.

pyxis.definition: pyxis idis, f , puci/s, a small box, casket: veneni.— A toilet-box, powder-box: Pyxidas, O., Iu.
